articleTitle: 3D Random Scattering Effects on MIMO Channel Capacity With a Multiple Scattering Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the development of 5G/6G communication technology, precise channel analysis considering the spatial characteristics of waves has become important. Traditional methods for analyzing random environments often rely on testing, statistics, and approximation techniques, which are not convenient or accurate enough for high-frequency and near-field communication scenarios. In this paper, we propose a method for evaluating the capacity of MIMO channels by combining an accurate electromagnetic scattering model and analyze the channel effects with Monte Carlo simulations in a random environment. Firstly, 3D multiple scatterers are uniformly randomly generated within a given space. The Foldy-Lax multiple scattering theorem is applied next to calculate the field under single dipole source excitation, and the channel matrix is obtained by sequentially excitations from each transmitter input. The MIMO channel capacity is computed using matrix decomposition and water-filling theorem. The effects of different scatterer distribution areas, including line-of-sight and non-line-of-sight effects, are analyzed, and stable random scattering channel effects are obtained through Monte Carlo simulations in each area. The proposed method utilizes precise electromagnetic analysis to accurately characterize the impact of random scatterer distributions on the channel. This makes it a potential valuable tool for modeling and evaluating channels in next-generation communication systems.

articleTitle: A Multi-scale Domain Decomposition Strategy for the Hybrid Time Integration Scheme of DGTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Accurate fast transient simulations have a considerable influence on the design of antennas and devices. In this paper, an efficient domain decomposition strategy is proposed for the hybrid time integration scheme of the discontinuous Galerkin time domain (DGTD) method. This strategy inherits the advantages of locally implicit and local time stepping methods and uses an adjustable time scale to reduce the storage and computational complexity. Numerical results show the effectiveness and confirmed that this method can be applied to the fast transient simulation of complex structures.

articleTitle: Absorptive Microwave Filters: From Narrowband to Wideband Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a method to control the out-ofband performance of absorptive filters in both narrowband and wideband cases. To verify the method, a narrowband absorptive filter is designed with wideband matching, and a wideband one is proposed to achieve an infinite low-reflection range. Finally, the narrowband filter is implemented in microstrip-line platform, not only attaining symmetrical geometry but also improving impedance-matching performance.

articleTitle: Design of SIR Coupled Resonator Bandpass Filter Based on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper describes a 6th-order coupled bandpass filter based on the SIR structure. In order to reduce the size of the filter and improve its performance, LTCC technology is adopted. The overall dimensions are 6.8mm×4.2mm×1.5mm. Following the basic principles of SIR coupled resonance, cross-coupling is introduced between input and output resonant stages to generate transmission zeros, achieving high out-of-band suppression. The HFSS software is utilized for modeling, simulation, and optimization of key parameters. The filter operates between 3.15GHz and 3.45GHz with a center frequency of 3.3GHz, exhibiting return loss better than 10dB. Multiple transmission zeros are generated outside the passband, achieving attenuation of 34dB at low out-of-band frequencies of 120MHz and 32dB at high out-of-band frequencies of 120MHz. Thus, the filter demonstrates excellent frequency selectivity.

articleTitle: A Parallel MLFMA with Multiple Octrees for Scattering of Complex Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an implementation of the parallel multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA), which is used to solve scattering problems with complex structures. Different from the parallelization of MLFMA calculating perfectly electric conducting objects, the proposed method uses multiple MLFMA trees to handle different integral equations. Furthermore, a parallelization strategy is designed for the proposed MLFMA to improve load balance and parallel efficiency on the cluster. Finally, the numerical simulation results show that the algorithm is very efficient using up to 480 CPU cores.

articleTitle: A Novel Parameterized Scattering Center Model for Complex Honeycomb Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To address the modeling challenges and high computational complexity associated with full-wave algorithms for honeycomb absorbing materials, this paper proposes a parametric scattering center model for complex honeycomb absorbing structures. The model derives the generalized reflection coefficient of the homogenized honeycomb structure using the geometrical optics (GO) method to characterize the amplitude factor of the scattering center model. Subsequently, full-wave method data is used to optimize the parameters of the scattering center model. Validation results indicate that the scattering characteristics computed with the proposed model are highly consistent with those obtained using multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). However, our parametric model significantly improves computational efficiency and reduces memory consumption. Therefore, this method provides an innovative approach for simulating the scattering characteristics of complex honeycomb materials.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-thermal co-simulation of radome antenna systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The thermal effects produced by antenna arrays during operation are becoming increasingly significant. In this study, the electromagnetic-thermal co-simulation method for antenna arrays and radomes is investigated based on the frequency-domain finite element electromagnetic simulation method and the time-domain finite element thermal simulation method. In the electromagnetic simulation, the finite element-boundary element method and the domain decomposition method are used, which substantially increase the solution scale of the computable problem. The electromagnetic-thermal co-simulation of 1024-elements antenna array and radome is completed at the end of the article.

articleTitle: High-Gain Substrate Integrated Cavity Circularly-Polarized Antenna Loaded with Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel metasurface-loaded high-gain substrate integrated cavity (SIC) circularly-polarized antenna is proposed in this paper. The SIC antenna is fed using Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW), and the integration of a hexagonal patch with the feed gap enables the TM121 mode and TM211 mode in the SIC antenna to have equal amplitude and a 90-degree phase difference, achieving circularly polarized radiation. Based on this, a periodic metasurface is designed and loaded on top of the antenna. This metasurface not only broadens the working bandwidth but also further enhances the antenna gain. The antenna gain increased by approximately 2dB without affecting efficiency.

articleTitle: A Large Span Beamforming Array Antenna with Cosecant Squared Pattern for Mobile Communication Application in Railway Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A 16-element microstrip patch antenna array with beamforming radiation pattern is proposed for railway mobile communication applications. Four antenna arrays with different beam angles are designed first, and their beams can be superimposed to achieve a cosecant squared pattern. Then, the four arrays are mapped into a composite antenna array. The feeding network of the composite array is designed based on the amplitudes and phases obtained by superimposing those of the four arrays in a weighted way. The simulated results show that the impedance bandwidth ( |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|< -10 dB) of the antenna array is between 3.45 - 3.55 GHz and the peak gain is 13.8 dBi. The designed radiation pattern is consistent with the desired cosecant squared pattern very well, and an angular beamforming range of 60° can be achieved at 3.5 GHz, which proves the effectiveness of the beamforming method in this paper.

articleTitle: Research on 3D Imaging Technology for Bridge Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This study addresses the challenges of detecting internal defects in reinforced concrete highway bridges by developing a visual 3D imaging algorithm using ground-penetrating radar (GPR) technology. The proposed system employs a multi-transmit, multi-receive array antenna and advanced data processing techniques to enhance detection accuracy and efficiency. Experiments demonstrate that this approach provides clear 3D visualizations of rebar and internal defects, significantly improving bridge inspection and maintenance processes. This technology reduces reliance on operator expertise and has broad potential applications in various reinforced concrete structures.

articleTitle: A Wideband Fabry-Perot Resonant Antenna with Sextuple-Layer Partially Reflective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This manuscript presented a Fabry-Perot resonant antenna with sextuple-layer partially reflective surface working in both C-band and X-band. To enhance the performance of proposed resonant antenna, a modified U-slotted patch antenna is introduced as the feed. A wideband (5.0 GHz - 8.9 GHz) positive reflection phase gradient is introduced by the partially reflective surface element. The presented element consists of six metallic layers, formed by five square patches and a square-ring patch, and three stacked substrates separated by two air gaps. 5 × 5-sextuple-layer elements are arranged periodically to form a partially reflective surface which is placed ahead of the feed. Then, the Fabry-Perot resonant antenna is obtained. In simulation, the proposed antenna realizes a 108.7% bandwidth (3.8 GHz - 12.9 GHz) for 3-dB drop while the peak gain is 9.8 dBi. Meanwhile, its impedance bandwidth and overall size respectively are 100.0% (4.0 GHz - 12.0 GHz) and 0.80λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.80λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.47λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (this value corresponds to the length, width and height of the presented antenna, and λ0 is the wavelength at 8.0 GHz).

articleTitle: On the Improvement of Volume-Surface Integral Equation Using the Combined Enforcement of Normal and Tangential Boundary Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the moment method solution of the volume-surface integral equation (VSIE), the normal and tangential boundary conditions are combined together and explicitly enforced on the perfect electric conductor (PEC)-dielectric interfaces. The number of volumetric unknowns is therefore reduced and the solution accuracy is improved. Based on the proposed scheme, when a dielectric tetrahedron is terminated by a PEC triangle, three expansion coefficients of the four SWG base defined on this tetrahedron are straightly determined.

articleTitle: Analysis of Bistatic RCS of Multiple Simple Targets Based on MoM-ACA Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, adaptive cross approximation (ACA) is introduced into Method of Moments (MoM) to analyze the multiple targets EM scattering problems by the electric field integral equation (EFIE) approach. The targets are divided into near-field regions and far-field regions based on the distance from the midpoint of the edge. The interactions of the near-field regions are calculated directly by MoM, and ACA is used for accelerated calculation of the far-field regions impedance matrix. The memory requirement and CPU time consumption are reduced drastically. When the subdomains decomposition size is 2.0 λ of the first case, it is the optimal coarsest level for this case. When the subdomains decomposition size is 1.0 λ of the second case, it is the optimal coarsest level for this case. ( λ is the wavelength)

articleTitle: Design of Miniaturized Comb-line LTCC Bandpass Filter Based on Cross Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a four-order bandpass filter with a center frequency of 2.58 GHz and a bandwidth of 2.43 to 2.73 GHz. The insertion loss is 1.21dB and the return loss is about 19.5 dB. The filter has a good selectivity by adding the cross-coupling between the resonators to generate transmission zero, with stopband suppression of 36.21dB at 0.85f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and 47.59dB at 1.15f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. Based on Low- Temperature Co-fired Ceramics (LTCC) technology, the final size of the filter is 5mm×3.3mm×1mm, which has good passband performance in a small size.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-band Dual-Sense Circularly Polarized OAM Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the rapid development of fifth-generation communication technologies, demands for a high channel capacity are increasing to enhance spectrum utilization. We propose a compact multi-mode orbital-angular-momentum (OAM) antenna array consisting of four dual-band dual-sense circularly polarized pentagon patch elements with U-shaped slots. The sequentially rotated array could generate two OAM beams simultaneously at dual frequency for high-speed communications. Simulation results indicate return-loss bandwidths of 2.62 GHz (8.90-11.53 GHz) at lower frequencies and 0.97 GHz (13.33-14.30 GHz) at higher frequencies. Furthermore, two OAM beams of modes 1 and -1 work at 9.2 GHz and 13.7 GHz, respectively, while axial ratio bandwidths are 0.17 GHz and 0.22 GHz. The antenna exhibits good impedance matching, with isolation levels over 18 dB across the operating frequency bands.

articleTitle: RCS Calculation of Multi-scale Targets by Iterative MOM-VSBR Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A new efficient hybrid technique is presented, which combines the method of moments (MoM) and the volume meshed shooting and bouncing ray (VSBR) for analyzing scattering of complex multi-scale structures. The multi-scale targets are divided into different sub-regions, and the scattering contributions from sub-regions with different electrical sizes are solved using different solvers. By applying the SBR method for the large scale sub-regions, a corrected incident field including not only the direct incident field but also the multi-bounce field from the SBR region contributes to the integral equation in the MoM sub-regions. For the VSBR region, it also considers the interaction from MoM region and then a physical optics type integration is performed to calculate the scattered field. For complex multi-scale electromagnetic problems, the proposed technique is more efficient and simpler to implement in a general-purpose computer code. Numerical results are presented to show the efficiency and accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Measurement of Electromagnetic Parameters of Inductively Coupled Plasma Based on Langmuir Probe
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Langmuir probe is one of the basic diagnostic methods for plasma properties. In this paper, a single probe is used to measure the electromagnetic parameters of Inductively Coupled Plasma under different discharge conditions, the principle of single probe measurement is introduced, and the electron density parameters of Inductively Coupled Plasma are extracted for analysis. According to the measurement results, it is found that the electron density increases with the increase of air pressure when the air pressure is 0.8torr-1.1torr. The electron density in the 1.1torr-1.3torr range will gradually decrease. As the power increases from 700W to 1000W, the electron density first increases and then decreases.

articleTitle: Design of A Novel Frequency Selective Surface based on Three-Dimensional Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel frequency selective surface based on three-dimensional structure, which consists of the planar periodic hexagonal ring gap structure and three-dimensional structure with gas printed on it. The proposed structure can achieve switchable transparent/reflective states, and the transparent state can provide high transmittance and cutoff state outside the passband, it is advantageous for application in complex electromagnetic environment

articleTitle: Fast Leapfrog Transform of 2-D Split-Field FDTD Method for Analyzing Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a fast leapfrog transform implementation of the 2-D split-field (SF) FDTD method for solving problems of the oblique incident plane wave on periodic structures. By using the central approximate difference method to transform the split form of the traditional SF method. This implementation allows for rapid execution of the 2-D leapfrog algorithm. Compared with the traditional SF method, the proposed method is not only easier to implement but also saves CPU time and memory. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed method is more efficient.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Dual-Band Dual-Circularly Polarized Transmit-Reflect-Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A dual-band dual-circularly polarized (CP) transmit-reflect-array (TRA) antenna with high efficiency is proposed. Novel TRA cells possessing x-polarized transmission and y-polarized reflection characteristics are designed for achieving equal dual-CP radiation amplitudes at both transmission and reflection sides. The phases of transmission and reflection CP waves can be modulated separately by adjusting the x-polarized transmission, y-polarized reflection phase-delay line lengths, and the cell rotation angles. Under the excitation of CP incident waves, the designed TRA antenna generates eight CP beams, i.e., two K-band dual-CP transmission beams, two K-band dual-CP reflection beams, two Ka-band dual-CP transmission beams, and two Ka-band dual-CP reflection beams. The measured peak gain values are about 24 dBic and 27 dBic at K-band and Ka-band, respectively, for the demonstrated TRA antenna.

articleTitle: Investigation of A Wearable RF Energy-Localized Harvester for On-Body Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable radio-frequency (RF) energy-localized harvester utilizing spoof surface plasmon (SSP) technology, designed for on-body performance testing. To accommodate various wearing needs and body postures, we simulate the human body in different positions and optimize the harvester’s structure based on the simulation results. The study compares scenarios where the loops are placed at the center versus the edges of the structure, and at the front versus the back of the body. Additionally, we examine the impact of placing the structure on the body at different angles. The harvester’s stable frequency and high gain over a wide bandwidth make it suitable for a broad range of wireless systems and adaptable to numerous body positions and postures.

articleTitle: A 1-Bit Wideband Dual Polarized Metasurface Design for RCS Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a programmable metasurface has been developed for wide-band RCS reduction application. The dual-polarized metasurface unit cell integrated with eight PIN diodes is designed to achieve the flexible phase and magnitude manipulations in X band. By switching eight PIN diodes from ON state to OFF state at the same time, the reflective phase difference of 180° can be achieved, with the reflective magnitude better than -2 dB. As the applied currents of the eight PIN diodes are reduced from 1 mA to 0.01 mA, the reflective magnitude is switched from -2 dB to -15 dB. When the proposed unit cell is arranged into an array and manipulated by the controlling circuit, the resulting metasurface can achieve the RCS reduction based on the scattering cancellation and absorption mechanisms. Simulation results are given to demonstrate the backward RCS reduction of -10 dB under two operating mechanisms, providing a feasible solution for dynamic electromagnetic stealth.

articleTitle: Research on Adaptive h-Refinement Algorithm in Method of Moments Based on Interpolation Recovery Error Estimator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Due to the high computational cost of adaptive h-refinement based on residual error estimator in the method of moments(MoM), this paper, based on the basic theory of MoM, studies the interpolation recovery error estimator for the divergence, represented as surface charge density values, of the PEC model surface current characterized by RWG basis functions. Based on the error estimator and the controller using the B-W(Bowyer-Watson) interpolation algorithm as the mesh refinement algorithm, the adaptive h-refinement scheme of the whole process of MoM is constructed. The numerical results show that the adaptive h-refinement in MoM based on the error estimator of interpolation recovery has high calculation accuracy and can effectively reduce computing resources.

articleTitle: Broadband Metamaterial for Visible and Infrared Transparent Microwave Absorption
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we present a broadband microwave absorber that is visible and infrared transparent, flexible, polarization insensitive, and angularly stable. It is designed with a three-layer structure consisting of a resistance film of indium– tin–oxide (ITO), Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA), and a metallic grid. The proposed absorber can achieve more than 90% absorption in the frequency range of 8–18.34 GHz and greater than 95% in the range of 8.8-17.63 GHz, with a fractional bandwidth of 78.5%.

articleTitle: Empirical Models of Ship’s Induced Magnetic Fields Based on Gaussian Fitting
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the modern naval warfare, the magnetic signals of the ship are crucial indicators for the under-water weapon like mines and torpedoes. Thus, attention has been increasingly paid to the relationship of the induced magnetic field to its direction and location. An empirical model for the induced magnetic field of ships based on the Gaussian fitting is proposed in the paper and the validation has shown a good fitting, greater than 91%. The results show that the proposed empirical model can provide a theoretical basis for stealth technologies such as ship-degaussing and low-magnetization design, serving as an important reference for critical engineering projects.

articleTitle: 3-D Parametric Metal Targets Inversion with Supervised Descent Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, we introduce an inversion method utilizing the supervised descent method (SDM) for reconstructing 3-D parametric metal targets. Trained on a set of simple targets, the SDM learns the mapping relationship between target characteristics and scattering data. This training process integrates prior knowledge into the optimization, effectively mitigating the ill-posedness of inverse scattering problems (ISPs). We demonstrate the application of this method to complicated targets, verifying its capability to predict accurate descent directions. The efficacy of this approach is validated through several examples, demonstrating its low training demands and high accuracy.

articleTitle: Accelerated SBR Method Based on MPI for Electromagnetic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a method called Shooting and Bouncing Rays (SBR) employing the Message Passing Interface (MPI) to address electromagnetic scattering issues arising from complex and electrically large targets. The accuracy of the proposed method has been validated by comparing the simulated results with those obtained from the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM). And a good speedup ratio has been achieved for SBR with MPI.

articleTitle: Spin-Encoded Wavelength-Direction Multitasking Full-space metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Multifunctional wavefront manipulations of waves is essential for high-capacity communications, which is still infancy. We employed vertically cascaded quadrangular patches and crossbars to integrate both geometric and dynamic phases and realize spin-encoded full-space wavefront control. A proof-of-concept metasurface with four-port wavefront manipulations is numerically and experimentally demonstrated, exhibiting distinct functionalities including spin- and frequency-dependent light focusing, quad-beam radiation, anomalous reflections, and Bessel beam generation. Our finding of full-space multifunctional metasurfaces would be vital for multiple-input-multiple-output system and sets up a solid platform for arbitrary spin-encoded full-space integrated devices.

articleTitle: Difference-Beam-Pattern Synthesis of Radome-Enclosed Linear Array Using Convex Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To correct the influence of radome on the radiation pattern of array antenna, the difference-beam-pattern synthesis method of radome-enclosed array antenna based on convex optimization is proposed, which takes radome-enclosed array antenna system as a whole to synthesize difference-beam-pattern. Through fixing the slope phase of the difference beam, the non-convex quadratic objective function which maximizes the difference beam slop is transformed into a convex optimization objective function which minimizes a linear function. Moreover, to accurately consider the interaction between array and radome, active element patterns are used to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the optimization results. Finally, the difference beam-pattern for a 40-element radome-enclosed array with - 30dB sidelobe and -70 dB null depth are achieved, and the validity and efficiency of the proposed method are verified.

articleTitle: A Ku-band low-profile circularly polarized all-metal cavity antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a Ku-band all-metal cavity circularly polarized antenna with low profile is introduced. By loading three kinds of slots with different shapes on the metal cover plate, good impedance matching (VSWR≤2) is achieved in the working frequency band. The gain of the proposed antenna reaches 8.9dBi, and the axis ratio is less than 2dB, thus achieving good circularly polarized radiation characteristics. It has the characteristics of single material, easy processing, low profile (<0.06λ), stable structure and good heat dissipation, which can have a good application prospect in the high performance antenna system of spaceborne SAR system.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Resonant Enhanced Backfire Ring Sector Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wideband dual-resonant enhanced backfire ring sector patch antenna (RSPA) with low-profile is proposed. The key parameters of the antenna are precisely calculated according to the mode synthesis design function of the ring sector patch radiator, leading to the obtained initial size of the antenna. The enhanced backfire radiation characteristic can be evolved from a bent microstrip leaky-wave antenna. As validations, a ring sector patch antenna with the flared angle α = 90° is fabricated, tested and verified on air substrate with thickness h = 5.0 mm (i.e., 0.048-wavelength) at the center frequency. The proposed antenna with the out/inner radii ratio of 1.7 exhibits an impedance bandwidth up to 25.8%. It exhibits an enhanced backfire radiation within the high frequency-band, with backfire gain up to 2.0 dBi, boresight gain up to 7.0 dBi and average radiation efficiency of 96.1%.

articleTitle: Multi-chip Microwave Module Micro-assembly Flexible Automatic Connection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To meet the growing demand for micro-assembly production of microwave products, a flexible micro-assembly automation line has been developed. Equipment layout and track transmission design were carried out to meet the requirements of flexible production. In response to the differences in track height and width of standard automatic equipment for each process of micro-assembly, as well as the different communication protocols of each device, the hardware and software of each type of equipment were uniformly modified to overcome the differences in track height and width between devices, achieve information exchange between devices and tracks, and ultimately achieve successful interconnection of hardware and software between devices. This flexible automated micro-assembly line can achieve the full process production of micro-assembly from bonding and feeding to automatic bonding, with a 400% increase in personnel utilization and a 100% increase in production efficiency.

articleTitle: Application of Deep Learning in Near Field of EMI Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we present a brief summary of two implementations of deep learning in the field of near-field scanning technology for electromagnetic interference (EMI), specifically focusing on the near field to near field transformation and near field to far field transformation. Sufficient data is acquired through a randomly distributed dipoles array for deep learning training purposes. These two applications demonstrate significant potential in the EMI domain and offer innovative solutions for addressing EMI challenges.

articleTitle: Design of Filtering Power Divider Based on LTCC with Double Folded Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a double-folded substrate-integrated waveguide (DFSIW) filter power divider based on low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) technology is proposed. By stacking four DFSIW resonant cavities, the filter is operated at the center frequency of 26 GHz by using the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">101</inf> main mode, and the energy coupling efficiency is improved by adjusting the size and position of the two coupling slots to reduce the insertion loss of the device. Meanwhile, by connecting the Wilkinson power divider with a metal through-hole in the uppermost resonant cavity, the energy is conducted from the filter unit to the power divider unit, thus realizing the function of filter power division. In addition, the isolation of the output is improved by loading isolation resistors at the two outputs of the power divider. In order to verify the design content, a filtered power divider operating at 26 GHz with a 3 dB relative bandwidth of 16.4% is designed and implemented in the high frequency structure simulation software HFSS.

articleTitle: Novel Efficient DGTD Method for Dispersive Bianisotropic Metamaterials via Homogenization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel efficient 3-D discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method is developed for modeling bianisotropic metamaterials. The dispersion nature is characterized by a complete dispersive model. Utilizing the bilinear transform and explicit leap-frog time integration, the novel DGTD method for the dispersive bianisotropic medium has been derived, which represents the first kind in the DGTD community. An actual 3-D bianisotropic Ω-class metamaterial is homogenized and simulated, showing much high efficiency of the proposed DGTD method.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Millimeter-Wave Orbital Angular Momentum Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a wideband millimeter-wave orbital angular momentum (OAM) metasurface. The principle of OAM electromagnetic beams with mode 1 is theoretically analyzed firstly. Next, a wideband magnetoelectric dipole unit integrated with phase delay lines is designed and the phase delay lines are utilized to realize the phase shift of 0°-360°, which it demonstrates good dispersion properties in the X-band range. With this wideband metasurface unit, a 16×16 metasurface that can effectively generate OAM beam is designed and simulated. The results show that the metasurface can achieve a relative bandwidth of 31.57% for OAM modes in the 8 to 11 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: The Design of a K-Band 256-Element Reconfigurable Multi-Beam Phased-Array for SATCOM Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we present a 256-element K-band (17.7-21.2GHz) phased array with 4 concurrent multi-beam, of which the polarization can be reconfigured as linear polarized, dual-polarized or circular polarized. With a stacked patch antenna unit designed of Rogers 4350B, the bandwidth of the phased array can reach 18% with VSWR < 2. Simulation results indicate that the phased array can be steered up to ±60° in 2-dimension space with axial ratio below 4dB within the whole bandwidth, when circular polarization is configured. Besides, with maximum gain of 28.2 dBi in the normal direction, the 3dB beam-width is about 6.9° with the side lobe levels (SLLs) all below -13.3 dB. With the wide spatial coverage and reconfigurable concurrent multi-beam, this design will be promising in applications like SATCOM and wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing MIMO Throughput through Improved Isolation and Radiation Pattern Shaping
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative method for designing hybrid networks employing multiport theory. The approach enhances antenna isolation and optimizes radiation patterns within multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna arrays. The hybrid network integrates a decoupling feeding network with a defected ground structure, utilizing surface-mounted reactive components optimized through an N-ary algorithm. A decoupling example validates the design process, showing improved matching, isolation below -20 dB, and a throughput increase of 58.6% (38.5%), validating the proposed methodology's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Antenna near-field data extrapolation in source reconstruction methods using BP network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The source reconstruction method (SRM) can realize the antenna near-field to far-field transformation accurately, but it still has the problem of high computational cost of near-field data. To solve this problem this article utilizes backward propagation (BP) network to extrapolate the near-field data. When acquiring the antenna near-field data, only 50% of the near-field data is calculated, and the rest of near-field data is predicted using the BP network. Simulation results show that the error of the far-field extrapolation results obtained using the predicted near-field data is less than 2dBi, which verifies the effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: Influences of Inhomogeneous Spatial Distribution of Global Oceanic Atmospheric Refractivity on LF Groundwave Propagation Delay
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Atmospheric refractivity affects the propagation delay of low-frequency (LF) groundwave in the realistic ocean environment. In this paper, a parabolic equation (PE) model based on the ERA5 meteorological reanalysis dataset is applied to analyze the influences of inhomogeneous spatial distribution of global oceanic atmospheric refractivity on LF groundwave propagation delay. The global oceanic atmospheric refractivity is derived from the meteorological quantities given by the ERA5 reanalysis dataset. It is found that the global oceanic surface atmospheric refractivity varies systematically with latitude in the range of 290~300 N-unit to 380~400 N-unit, which in turn leads to the variation of LF groundwave propagation delay reaching hundredth nanosecond for 1000 km-long propagation path.

articleTitle: Influence of Electromagnetic Scattering Phase Fluctuation on Coherence Efficiency of Spatially Distributed Radars
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Widely spatially distributed radar can enhance signal-to-noise ratio O(N) times of a single radar by coherent processing of echoes from sub-radars, where N denotes the number of sub-radars. However, when aperture of the distributed radar is large, target scattering fluctuation between sub-radars becomes un-ignorable and deteriorates coherent processing performance. This paper analyzes influence of target scattering fluctuation between sub-radars on coherence efficiency of spatially distributed radar. It is observed from simulated data that target scattering fluctuation between sub-radars does exist and must be take into consideration when high coherence efficiency is expected.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Fast DC IR Drop Prediction for Power Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Efficiently predicting the DC resistances of power distribution networks (PDNs) is important for the optimization of printed circuit board (PCB) design. This paper proposes a methodology based on boundary integration and algebraic graph theory to calculate the DC resistance of PDNs efficiently, which is much more quickly than traditional full-wave simulation. Then, for PCB design with higher requirements in speed, a deep neural network (DNN) is trained to predict the PDN resistance for different stack-up structures, which can be accomplished within fractions of a second.

articleTitle: An Unconditionally Stable FDTD Method With High-Order Accuracy and Complying Divergence
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel unconditionally-stable finite- difference time-domain (FDTD) method that complies divergence is proposed. This novel method is based on the conventional split- step four sub-steps (SS4)-FDTD method, and a form that complies divergence is obtained by operating input and output. Moreover, a theoretical proof is given to show that the novel method is divergence-complying. Finally, the simulation results are shown to demonstrate the proposed method is more accurate and divergence-complying.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Wideband Metasurface Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave using Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: For the application of 5G millimeter-wave, a wideband miniaturized metasurface (MTS) antenna is proposed. Based on characteristic mode analysis (CMA), a V-slot unit cell is designed with an extended current path, achieving miniaturization while maintaining good dual-mode characteristics. The antenna bandwidth reaches 21.4% (31.91-39.55GHz) for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < –10 dB, within which gain varies from 6.3 to 7.1 dBi, It exhibits an MTS size of 0.35λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>× 0.42λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, a profile of 0.097λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> corresponds to the central operating frequency), providing potential array applications in compact communication devices.

articleTitle: A Cross-Band Decoupling Technique Based on Current Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a method to reduce the cross-band coupling based on the frequency doubling or approximate frequency doubling case. When the high and low frequency bands exhibit an integer multiple relationship, the coupling current path length on the high frequency antenna when the low frequency antenna operates is about one-fourth of the waveguide wavelength of the electromagnetic wave in the low frequency band, which shows the monopole characteristic and makes the cross-band coupling higher. In this paper, by regulating the coupling current on the high-frequency antenna, carving a slot on the high-frequency antenna balun, bending the current, making the resonance frequency move to the lower frequencies, avoiding the low-frequency band so as to realize the cross-band decoupling, and finally reducing the cross-band coupling between the antennas from -10.3dB to -22dB.

articleTitle: On the Directivity, Gain and Realized Gain of Polarization Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To obtain superiority in electronic warfare, the phased array front-end system demands polarization agility capability, i.e., each antenna element can transmit or receive electromagnetic waves of any polarization through two orthogonally polarized antennas. In this paper, the directivity, gain and realized gain of such a polarization reconfigurable antenna (PRA) are explored by theoretical derivation and full-wave simulation.

articleTitle: A Dual Mode Dual Broadband Shared Aperture Antenna for WBAN Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A dual mode dual broadband shared aperture antenna for WBAN communications is presented. The antenna is composed of rectangular patch and ring with circular slot. The antenna operates in the ISM bands at 2.45 GHZ and 5.8 GHZ for ON-body and OFF-body communication. The simulation results indicate that shared aperture antenna bandwidth covers 2.29-2.82 GHZ at low frequency and 4.74-5.84 GHZ at high frequency with isolation greater than 15 dB. In addition, the designed common-caliber antenna has patch-like radiation direction pattern at 2.45 GHZ band and monopole-like radiation direction pattern at 5.8 GHZ band.

articleTitle: Target Localization and Vital Signs Monitoring Based on Spatial-Temporal-Frequency Characteristics With Short-Range FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar is commonly employed for target localization and vital signs monitoring. However, the presence of energy leakage between the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX) often leads to significant degradation in short-range applications. In this paper, A novel short-range target localization and vital signs monitoring technique based on spatial-temporal-frequency characteristics is proposed. Combining the temporal-frequency characteristics of intermediate frequency (IF) signal with anti-leakage signal, leakage is effectively mitigated. Subsequently, precise 2-D target localization and vital signs detection are achieved through the frequency-spatial features of the IF signals. Experiments were conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed technique for short-range target localization and vital signs monitoring. The results indicate a 10 dB improvement in signal-to-interference ratio (SIR), effectively suppressing interference and achieving precise spatial 2-D positioning of the targets, thereby enabling accurate acquisition of respiratory and heartbeat waveform and spectrum.

Author Keywords: short-range target localization and vital signs monitoring

articleTitle: Physics-Assisted Deep Reinforcement Learning-Based TSV Array Design for Signal and Power Integrity Co-Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The signal integrity (SI) and power integrity (PI) co-optimization of through silicon via (TSV) arrays, which involves two goals (SI and PI) and three objects (signal, power, and ground TSVs), has always been a challenging multi-goal and multi-object optimization problem due to the huge search space. This paper proposes a novel physics-assisted deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to tackle this problem, which allows for co-optimizing the SI/PI of TSV arrays during a DRL training process. The verification cases show that our proposed method accommodates various optimization objectives well and achieves faster convergence and better SI/PI quality than the state-of-the-art DRL approach.

articleTitle: Measurement-based Transistor Modeling and Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to construct more accurate model for transistor, the measurement-based transistor modeling from I-V and C-V/Q-V characteristics are analyzed in detail.. Moreover, a novel method of radar chart is employed to evaluate the widely used models. Thus, the challenges and prospects on future transistor modeling is addressed.

articleTitle: Low In-band-RCS Tightly Coupled Dipole Array Based on Metamaterial Absorber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a tightly coupled dipole array (TCDA) with wide-angle radar cross section (RCS) reduction property is designed. Specifically, the planar metamaterial absorber (MMA), which consists of metal strips loaded with resistors, is integrated between the TCDA and the ground plane. This assignment benefits the TCDA with the low RCS property. To verify the design principle, an 8×8 low RCS TCDA is designed and simulated in commercial software. And the simulated results reals that more than 5 dB RCS reduction and ±30° beam scanning angle is realized during 10-15 GHz. This work offers a simple method to design phased arrays with a distinct RCS reduction performance, without significant deterioration in antenna properties, such as gain and bandwidth.

articleTitle: Omnidirectional High Gain Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain omnidirectional antenna array based on folded dipole is designed. The antenna, operating in the UHF band with its length less than 3m, owns 8 folded dipole units placed vertically to form a linear array in order to realize the omnidirectional characteristics. The antenna is processed and measured. The measurement shows that the omnidirectional antenna array is able to realize a VSWR of less than 1.5, a roundness of the directivity pattern in horizontal plane less than 0.5dB, and a gain of more than 7.0dBi within the working band of a relative bandwidth of 10%. The measured results show that the antenna has good horizontal omnidirectional radiation characteristics in the designed frequency bands, which is in good agreement with the simulation.

articleTitle: Efficient Group-Aware Graph Neural Network for Air Quality Forecasting in Small-scale Spaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Air pollution poses significant risks to life and health in small-scale spaces. Accurate air quality predictions can provide critical data hours or days in advance, facilitating preventive actions. Previous research has primarily concentrated on large areas, such as countries, with ample data, often overlooking smaller, data-limited spaces. In this paper, we present a novel hierarchical model designed for forecasting air quality in such conditions, an Efficient Group-Aware Graph Neural Network for Air Quality Forecasting in Small-scale Spaces (EGAGNN). This model has the potential to significantly improve our understanding of air quality dynamics in small, data-limited spaces with its ability to capture direct and indirect influences among nodes. It identifies potential node connections and forms groups using a differentiable grouping network. Additionally, the model employs an encoder to capture group correlations and applies a messagepassing mechanism to learn the final node representations. Extensive experiences demonstrate that our model outperforms existing approaches.

articleTitle: C/K-Band Dual-Frequency Shared-Aperture Antenna with High Isolation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-frequency shared-aperture antenna operating at 4.7/25.2 GHz. By embedding a high-frequency dielectric resonant antenna (DRA) into a perforated discrete patch of a low-frequency patch antenna, the two antennas are highly integrated. The proposed antenna has a compact size of 0.51λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.51λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.05λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength in the vacuum at 4.7 GHz). Simulation results show that the -10 dB impedance bandwidths of this shared-aperture antenna are 4.26-5.15 GHz (18.9%) and 23.7-26.7 GHz (11.9%), with peak gains within the bands of 6.2 dBi and 16.6 dBi, respectively. The channel isolation between the two bands is more than 40 dB at low frequency and 20 dB at high frequency.

articleTitle: A Wide-band Circularly-Polarized Metal Cavity Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: this paper, a novel circularly polarized metal cavity antenna is proposed. The radiating element is composed of a tilted slot cut in the narrow walls of a ridge waveguide and a bending slot in the bottom of the L-shaped wall. The inclined part of the bending slot is orthogonal to the slot on the narrow walls. Two polarized fields form a 90°phase difference, which is offered by the quarter of the wave length depth of the ridge. At the center frequency of 10 GHz, impedance bandwidth of S11 less than -10 dB is about 16% (8.8GHz-10.4GHz) and the axial bandwidth of antenna less than 3dB is 25% (8.5GHz-11.0GHz). The proposed antenna obtains high efficiency, excellent circular polarization purity, wide-band characteristics and simple structure.

articleTitle: The Independently Controllable Multi-beam of Time-Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an independent controllable multi-beam technology based on time-modulated array (TMA). Stepped waveform generated by in-phase/quadratue (I/Q) time modulation with digital attenuators is applied to present flexible time-modulated signals. It adjusts the time delay of each sideband independently to control the direction of the corresponding beams. Simulated radiation patterns at the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd sidebands are presented and other undesired sidebands are suppressed.

articleTitle: A reconstruction method for obscured SAR images using VAE
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to protect sensitive information, Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) images often need to be mosaicked or obscured, which brings difficulties to the further application of images. In this paper, a deep learning generation model Variational Autoencoder (VAE) is proposed to reconstruct damaged SAR images. First, the same type of normal SAR images are used for training, and then obscured SAR images are tested as input. The results show that this process effectively removes the mosaics or obscurations in SAR images and reconstruct the original visual effect of the images. It performs well in many evaluation indexes and realizes the reconstruction of obscured images.

articleTitle: A Fast CG Extraction Algorithm With pFFT for Interconnects Embedded in Lossy Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An integral equation formulation is developed to extract the capacitance and conductance (CG) parameters of lossy media in packages. In addition, the pre-corrected fast Fourier transform (pFFT) is carried out to accelerate the matrixvector product and improve the efficiency. A real-life circuit structure is simulated to validate its effectiveness and accuracy. Results show that it is accurate and efficient to extract the CG parameters of interconnects embedded in lossy media.

articleTitle: Reverse Time Migration of Ultra-Wideband Ground-Penetrating Radar Based on Multiple Time-Gating Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To address the issue of clutter interference in ground-penetrating radar (GPR) imaging using a VNA (Vector Network Analyzer), this paper improves the traditional reverse time migration (RTM) technique for ultra-wideband GPR imaging. The improved method retains the effective signals in the detection wavefield as the valid imaging area and suppresses signals in non-valid areas. Due to variations in the distance between the transmitting and receiving antennas and the number of anomalies in the experiment, the traditional time window cross-correlation is not ideal for this scenario. The improved method automatically applies reasonable windowing to each data channel, avoiding the simultaneous enhancement of clutter interference and effective signals through direct stacking, and preventing the filtering out of effective signals. Experimental results demonstrate that this method, when applied to real measured data and compared with the traditional cross-correlation RTM method, shows advantages in more accurately locating anomalous areas and suppressing clutter interference. This validates that the Multiple Time-Gating Reverse Time Migration (MTG-RTM) method offers better localization and higher imaging accuracy in practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: A wideband coaxial filtering branch-line coupler
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wideband coaxial branch-line coupler with filtering function working at Q-band is proposed, which consists of a quadrature coupler and four bandpass filters. By cascading a coaxial quadrature coupler with bandpass filters, the branch-line coupler has a self-supporting structure and achieves both a wide operating bandwidth and bandpass filtering characteristics. Simulation results show that the filtering branch-line coupler centered at 37 GHz has a wide bandwidth of 37.84% (30 GHz to 44 GHz) and an output power imbalance better than 0.5 dB, while the return loss and isolation are better than 13.5 dB. Compared with conventional branch-line couplers, the filtering branch-line coupler in this paper has a wide operating bandwidth and is easy to process.

articleTitle: Low-dose CT image processing based on controllable residual U-shaped network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Medical Computed Tomography(CT) requires the use of the lowest possible low-dose scanning mode. However, too low dose scanning will produce low-quality CT images containing a large amount of noise and artifacts affecting the diagnosis, and the intensity and distribution of noise and artifacts in different parts of the tomographic images under the same dose are not the same. For this reason, this paper adopts a dynamically controllable residual network to improve the CT image restoration effect, the main idea of this network is to add a control variable to the conventional residual network connection to allow the acquisition of the weighted sum of residuals, and realize the dynamic controllability of residuals. With the help of conditional residual blocks, a tunable UNet (DR-UNet) is designed in conjunction with the UNet. The network consists of two parts: the base network and the conditional network, which will consist of the conditional residual block, the downsampling layer and the upsampling layer, which consists of the encoder path and the decoder path. The conditional network takes the image quality assessment coefficients as inputs, and a modified form of multilayer fully connected network will be used to improve the accuracy of the control weight estimation. Experimental results show that the proposed method exhibits competitive performance in terms of noise suppression, structural realism and visual browsing improvement.

articleTitle: A Compact CMOS Broadband Single-Sideband Time Modulator Based on 4-bit Vector-Sum Phase Shifter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A compact CMOS broadband single-sideband time modulator (SSBTM) is presented. The proposed SSBTM is based on a periodically controlled 4-bit passive vector-sum phase shifter (VSPS) to realize high precision phase shifting, high sideband rejection and low amplitude variation. The SSBTM uses particular-sized cells to reduce impedance changes in state switching. Additionally, the 8-bit control sequences are generated by using a true-single-phase-clock (TSPC) divide-by-16 frequency divider which is controlled by 1-bit square wave control signal. The SSBTM is designed in 55-nm CMOS technology with a layout area of 0.83 × 0.54 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The simulated results show that sideband suppression ratio (SSR) is −23.8 dBc, the power consumption is 15.6 mW from the 1.2 V supply, and its gain is −5.2±1.3 dB. In the frequency band of 1−4.5 GHz, the phase resolution can reach more than 10-bits, RMS phase error is 0.1∼0.2°, maximum gain error is less than 0.02 dB.

articleTitle: A Novel ACA for Analyzing Electromagnetic Field Problems of Filter with Waveports
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a fast direct method based on adaptive cross approximation (ACA) is used to calculate the electromagnetic field of the waveport which is a difficulty when analyzing metal-dielectric filter models. Different from the traditional method of moments (MoM), the system matrix is divided into blocks and then compressed in this method which greatly improves the calculation efficiency while ensuring the calculation accuracy. Numerical results are presented to demonstrate that the proposed ACA can efficiently and accurately calculate the metal-dielectric filter models.

articleTitle: Analysis of Large Array Antennas Based on Finite Element Domain Decomposition Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A fast solving algorithm for large periodic structures has been proposed. This algorithm is based on domain decomposition method (DDM) and divides regions according to periodic structure element. Some subdomains have the same system matrix, the feature of subdomains are extracted to reduce the memory in the DDM calculation process. the computational accuracy and efficiency of the implemented solver is verified through numerical examples. A large array antenna which generates exceeded 6.86 million tetrahedrons and 48.54 million unknowns is calculated with only 27 minutes on a single workstation.

articleTitle: Effective Combination of Convolutional Perfectly Matched Layer and the HIE-FDTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The combination of the hybrid implicit-explicit (HIE) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method with the convolutional perfectly matched layer (CPML) is effectively implemented (HIE-CPML). The results of S11 and radiation patterns of the proposed HIE-CPML method are compared with other methods and software through the example of a dual-band microstrip patch antenna. Numerical results show that this method is highly consistent with the results obtained by the FDTD with CPML method. Although the Courant-Friedrichs-Lewy number (CFLN) increased to 7, the relative error of the HIE-CPML method is still lower than 6 dB, effectively verifying the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency Selective Surface using Residual Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This letter proposes a frequency selective surface (FSS) inverse design method based on a residual learning framework. Traditional FSS designs that meet industrial demands depend on designers' experience and repeated simulation iterations. The proposed method, however, can automatically design the FSS structure parameters that meet specific frequency response requirements. The residual-learning-based method is not only validated by two passband FSS design examples but has shown advantages over the commonly used convoluted neural network-based methods.

articleTitle: Design of a Multi-Section Omnidirectional High-Gain Base Station Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: High-gain omnidirectional antennas are widely used in outdoor emergency communication systems. This paper presents a multi-section omnidirectional high-gain base station antenna based on coaxial colinear (COCO) structure. It operates within the UHF band and has an overall length of less than 5.4m. The antenna is divided into three sections to improve portability, in which each coaxial unit uses air coaxial transmission, compared with dielectric coaxial, the use of air coaxial transmission can significantly reduce the number of antenna oscillators, at the same time significantly improve the radiation efficiency of the antenna. Due to the use of air coaxial, the impedance is relatively large, for this reason, the design of specific impedance sectionalizer can realize impedance mutation to achieve the specifications required. Test results show that the gain is greater than 9dBi in the operating band and the VSWR is less than 1.5, and good horizontal omnidirectionality in the working band, which is consistent with the simulation results.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Parasitic Microstrip Array With Customized Tilted Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A single-layer microstrip parasitic array with customizable tilted-beam radiation performance is proposed. The antenna consists of one driven patch and twenty parasitic patches and the tilt angle is designed using the index-modulation principle. The index-modulation principle is derived based on the index modulation principle. According to this principle, the size of the patch unit can be adjusted to control the refractive index and the tilt angle is determined by the refractive index distribution. This paper uses circular patch units to configure the tilted-beam antenna. Simulation results manifest that the antenna has a high gain radiation up to 11.54 dBi with large tilt angle of 60° off boresight and a bandwidth of 9.89%.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarized Triple-Layer Transmitarray Antenna with Isolated Element Design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized triple-layer transmitarray antenna(TAA) using isolated elements is proposed. First, a triple-layer isolated metal TAA element is designed. To realize the design, a substrate frame is used to support the elements. The adjacent elements are isolated, which is beneficial for broadening the element passband. Then, a dual-polarized triple-layer TAA with 185 elements is designed. Simulated results of the TAA indicate that its gain at the center frequency 10.5 GHz is 26.1 dBi, and its 1-dB gain bandwidth is about 20%.

articleTitle: RCS Near-Field Measurement Method Based on ISAR Imaging and Scattering Center Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This study combines inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging with scattering center extraction techniques to explore an efficient near-field-to-far-field conversion method to address the challenge of accurately measuring target radar cross sections (RCS) in a near-field test environment. We investigate two such conversion methods: the CLEAN algorithm and the direct reconstruction method. We conduct an in-depth study of scattering center extraction and point spread function construction, and thoroughly examine and validate these methods through simulation experiments on different targets to demonstrate their effectiveness and accuracy in converting near-field measurements to far-field RCS predictions.

articleTitle: Design of Frequency-polarization Dual Mode Manipulation Metasurface Unit with Phase Change Materials
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a reflective metasurface unit, which can realize the manipulation of frequency and polarization of electromagnetic waves. The designed unit has a three-layer structure with a metal plane in the bottom layer, a quartz dielectric in the middle layer, and a topology combining VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and metal in the top layer. The inner ring structure of the top layer mainly realizes the function of polarization conversion. The VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> outer ring on the top layer is combined with metal patches, which will enhance the conductivity of the outer ring in terms of both equivalent conductivity and heat absorption efficiency, making the outer ring conductivity higher than the inner ring, affecting its resonance, and producing a frequency offset. Simulation results show that when VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> is in dielectric state, the unit operates from 29 GHz to 31.6 GHz; Increasing VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> conductivity, the unit's operating band will be shifted to lower frequency band of 24.8 GHz to 26.5 GHz. This unit design provides a new approach for multi-mode-manipulation metasurface device design.

articleTitle: Height-Adjustable Phased Array with Regulated RCS Amplitude for Dual-Linear Polarized Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A height-adjustable phased array’s (hPA’s) is designed in this work with monostatic radar cross section (mRCS) amplitude regulation performance for dual-linear polarized waves. Based on the analysis on the antenna’s structural mode scattering and antenna mode scattering, the reflection coefficient with higher-order-mode condition has been integrated into the antenna mode scattering. With the perfect absorption for in-band RCS reduction, the inevitable higher-order-mode reflection at ultra-wideband frequency has been considered to realize the hPA’s mRCS amplitude regulation. Finally, a 4 × 8-element hPA optimized for 5 and 15 dB ultra-wideband mRCS reductions is designed, measured, and analyzed. The proposed analysis method for an antenna’s scattering characteristics will provide a new perspective for the realization of PA’s ultra-wideband mRCS reduction.

articleTitle: Study of the Impact of Hydrocarbon Fluid Distribution on Reservoir Electrical Resistivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Unconventional oil and gas reservoirs have complex geological structures, and very often consists of dense fracture network. The charging and migration of hydrocarbon fluids within it also exhibit heterogeneity and anisotropy. In the oil and gas exploration process, geophysical parameters such as resistivity are widely used for inversion to estimate the proportion of hydrocarbons and other components. However, establishing the relationship between hydrocarbon distribution and equivalent resistivity is the foundation for improving the accuracy of inversion predictions. Based on pore-scale multiphase flow simulation and tensor resistivity analysis methods, we can simulate the overall migration process of hydrocarbon fluids in fractured media and calculate changes in resistivity. The results indicate a correlation between the direction of hydrocarbon charging and changes in the equivalent resistivity of the medium. In order to predict the migration paths of hydrocarbons and the orientation of medium fractures, we change the angle of the factures to observe the effect of hydrocarbon injection on the effective resistivity of the medium. Based on the observed results, we construct inversion models for the variation of resistivity at different angles. This work is expected to improve the accuracy of resistivity inversion, determine the oil and gas formation patterns, and optimize oil and gas extraction strategies, provide theoretical references for related fields.

articleTitle: A Rapid prediction method for S-parameter of the stretchable antenna based on Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a pioneering and rapid approach to predict the S-parameters of flexible antennas under stretching condition based on Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). Two ANN models with feedback are developed and trained on a dataset of flexible antennas undergoing diverse stretching amounts. These models demonstrate robust predictive capabilities for the S-parameters of flexible antennas, providing efficient simulation and analysis avenues, which could propel advancements in flexible antenna technology research.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Structured Mesh Generation Method for FDTD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high-precision structured mesh generation method for finite difference time domain (FDTD) algorithm is proposed. Utilizing triangular elements from .STL files as inputs, our method identifies the edges of the target based on the characteristics of these elements. The mesh is then refined according to the edge positions, the minimum wavelength of the simulated frequency band, and the size of the triangular elements. This edge recognition capability allows our method to more accurately capture the target’s features compared with traditional mesh generation methods. To validate this, an inverted-F antenna was subdivided using the proposed method. The FDTD method was then employed to compute the S-parameters and the directional pattern of the antenna, based on the generated meshes. Comparison of the FDTD results with those obtained from CST software confirmed the high accuracy of our mesh generation method.

articleTitle: CLEAN and FrFT based Cross-range Scaling Method for ISAR Image
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Improper scaling for ISAR image will result in shape and proportion distortion of the target, unfavorable to target detection and recognition. According to the system bandwidth, the range scaling factor is easily obtained. To determine the cross-range scaling factor, the rotational angle between the radar and target is needed. However, this is usually unknown, resulting in difficulty of cross-range scaling. In this paper, the CLEAN is employed to extract dominant scattering centers from the ISAR image. Then, the fractional Fourier transform (FrFT) is utilized to estimate the chirp rates of the range cells in which the dominant scattering centers locate. With the chirp rates estimation result, the cross-range scaling factor can be calculated, and cross-range scaling of the ISAR image is finally implemented. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the cross-range scaling method.

articleTitle: Large Scene SAR Image Sample Construction Method Based on VAE_GAN Generated Data and Pixel Replacement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of high cost and difficulty in acquiring large scene SAR target image data, and the problem that it is difficult for intelligent generation algorithms to generate complex large scene images, this paper uses VAE_GAN to expand a small number of small scene SAR target images, and then uses the method of histogram matching to match the luminance histograms of the parts that need to be replaced in the SAR target image and the SAR scene image, and constructs a Gaussian image to smooth the matching result, and then use the pixel replacement method to fuse the processed target image with the scene image, and use the generated small scene target image and the existing SAR large scene background image to construct a large scene target image dataset. For VAE_GAN the introduction of the variational self-encoder is to enhance the diversity of samples generated by the generator; and the self-attention mechanism module is introduced to capture the long-distance dependence between location information.

articleTitle: A Ultra-Wideband Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna With Improved Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a new ultra-wideband magnetoelectric dipole antenna with improved feed structure is proposed. Not only is the trapezoidal electric dipole used instead of the traditional rectangular electric dipole, but the step feed structure is also used instead of the traditional 「 type feed structure to extend the operating bandwidth of the antenna. In addition, the gain of the antenna is effectively improved by loading a rectangular cavity structure around the antenna which utilizes the cavity to reflect the electromagnetic wave. The simulation results show that an impedance bandwidth of 57% is realized in the frequency band range of 1.74 ~ 3.13 GHz with VSWR < 2. The antenna has a good directional radiation pattern with a gain range of 7.45 ~ 9.23dBi over the whole operating band. In addition, the antenna obtains a low back radiation.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Shared-Aperture Frequency-Scanning Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A leaky-wave antenna (LWA) utilizing different modulation periods to achieve frequency scanning in dual bands within a spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) structure is proposed. This antenna can achieve radiation leakage from microwave to millimeter-wave bands under the same aperture. Before the fundamental mode cut-off frequency of the periodic structure, the antenna realizes frequency scanning in the microwave band through external periodic disturbances. Frequency scanning leakage in the millimeter wave band is achieved via SSPP periodic structure modulation. The modulated radiation structures of the two bands operate under the same aperture, with independent radiation modes. Finally, the proposed antenna achieves a 93° (-90° to 3°) beam scanning angle in the slow wave band (4.5-8 GHz), and a 96° (-70° to 26°) beam scanning angle in the fast wave band (9-21 GHz).
