The average realized gain in the two operating bands is about 8dBi, and the radiation efficiency is greater than 85%.

articleTitle: Solving Electromagnetic Scattering of 3D PEC Targets Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this study, a deep learning-based approach is proposed to address electromagnetic (EM) scattering of 3D perfect electric conductor (PEC) targets. Message passing graph neural networks (GNNs) are employed to build a surrogate model capable of predicting the surface currents of 3D PEC targets. Triangle meshes are converted into graph-structured data, allowing the 3D PEC targets to be represented as graphs that can be processed by GNNs. Training and testing datasets are generated by applying the method of moments to solve the combined-field integral equations (CFIE) of 3D PEC targets. Three basic types of 3D target geometries are considered, including spheroids, conical frustums, and hexahedrons. With the unique capability of adaptively managing unstructured data and varying unknown quantities, the proposed GNN model demonstrates good numerical precision. This study reveals the great potential of GNNs for 3D EM modeling.

articleTitle: OpenSEMBA/DGTD: An Open-Source Full-Wave Maxwell’s Equations Solver
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Numerical solvers have been essential tools in the industry, R&D and other similar fields in the last two decades. While it is important to understand the advantages and limitations of most common methods and look for the best candidates in terms of simplicity, accuracy, and computational performance; the capacity to be able to simulate, with relative simplicity, complex physical problems and obtain results which can serve as validations or preliminary testing has increased efforts towards obtaining more efficient and stable methods. In this work, we will discuss our choice to utilize the discontinuous Galerkin in the time domain (DGTD) method by extending an available finite element method library, MFEM, which allows us to introduce a Maxwell's equations solver in all dimensions without having to implement the basic framework a numerical method would require. A basic form of a DGTD solver has been successfully implemented, with further development planned in the future.

articleTitle: Deep Conditional Generative Adversarial Network-Assisted Inverse Design of Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Conventional metasurface (MS) design relies on time-consuming simulation iterative method and high design costs. As a new technology, deep learning (DL) has been applied in the field of MS design and shown good performance. This paper develops an innovative deep conditional generative adversarial network (DCGAN) for the inverse design of MS. By constructing and training the network model, the corresponding MS structure can be quickly and automatically generated with the required polarization conversion rate (PCR) as input, and then the purpose of on-demand design can be achieved.

articleTitle: Design of a transparent chessboard metasurface with low infrared emissivity and broadband RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This study introduces a transparent, ultra-thin, single-layer chessboard metasurface formulated based on the principle of phase cancellation, which can attain dual stealth in both radar and infrared spectrums. The metasurface achieves over 10 dB radar cross section (RCS) reduction within the 11.7-19.5 GHz bandwidth. Based on the unique properties of indium tin oxide (ITO), the designed metasurface is transparent in the optical range and has a thickness of merely 1.5 mm. Furthermore, with a top ITO filling rate of approximately 0.798, the metasurface exhibits a low infrared emissivity of around 0.254. The simulation results match the theoretical predictions well, which demonstrate excellent infrared-radar stealth performance of the designed metasurface. This research provides novel perspectives and possibilities for high-frequency radar stealth technology and optical device design.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Side-firing Bidirectional Antenna Array Based on Periodic Cross-meander Metallic Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A side-firing bidirectional antenna array based on a pair of periodic cross-meander metallic lines is proposed in this paper, which exhibits the advantages of compact design and high aperture efficiency. A novel meandered-line element is introduced to reduce the width of the bidirectional antenna while maintaining its effective bidirectional radiation capability. Furthermore, using a novel dual-layer periodic array design approach, the bidirectional antenna array achieves a uniform aperture amplitude distribution while maintaining a compact structure. A prototype is fabricated and measured to validate the design strategy. The overall dimensions of this antenna array are only 1.42λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.16λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.02λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength at the center frequency), and the -10 dB impedance bandwidth ranges from 2.4 GHz to 2.5 GHz. The proposed antenna array exhibits a narrower width and a higher gain-to-area ratio.

articleTitle: Broadband Multiple Vortex Beam Generation Based on Pancharatnam-Berry Phase Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a metasurface for generating broadband deflection vortex beams based on the Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase principle is proposed. The units with different phase responses are arranged according to the calculated vortex phase compensation matrix, thereby the proposed metasurface can convert the incident plane wave into a reflected high-purity third-order vortex wave within a broadband from 14 GHz to 20 GHz, and the relative bandwidth is 35.3%. In addition, by adding beam deflection phase distribution to the vortex phase distribution, reflected vortex wave towards specified direction can be obtained. Therefore, it is possible to achieve modulation of multiple modes, multiple beams, and capability of customizing beam of vortex waves by compositely designed metasurface. The approach can be used to design metasurfaces generating desired vortex waves in complex communication scenarios, thereby can further expand the application of vortex waves in wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Dual-Circularly Polarized Reflectarray With Independent Beam Control For Each Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-circularly polarized reflectarray unit cell composed of a linear-to-circular polarization conversion unit and a dual linear polarized reflective unit, which can independently adjust the phase shift of each circularly polarized incident wave. According to this unit, a dual-circularly polarized reflectarray is designed to produce left- and right-handed circularly polarized radiation beams directed to (-5°,0) and (5°,0) with peak gains of 25.76 dBi and 25.50 dBi at 21 GHz, respectively. The 2.5 dB axial ratio bandwidth of the reflected left- and right-handed circularly polarized beams is 17.31% (19 - 22.6 GHz) and 15.31% (19.3 - 22.5 GHz), respectively.

articleTitle: Research Advance on Transparent Surface Plasmon Polaritons Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we present a transparent endfire antenna based on an optical and radio frequency (RF) transparent quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs) structure. The antenna utilizes two different phase propagation constants resulting from the asymmetric quasi-1D SPPs structure for phase modulation. The loading of quasi-1D impedance matching structure contributes to the efficient conversion of SPPs waves to space waves. The proposed antenna achieves stable endfire radiation in the operating band of 14.5-15.5 GHz, with excellent optical transparency of the radiation portion. This approach demonstrates the ability of the quasi-1D SPPs structure to modulate the phase propagation constant and proves the potential of the quasi-1D SPPs structure to realize transparent antennas.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Transmission and Absorption of Metasurfaces Using Quasi-Complementary Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Metasurfaces that satisfy certain response usually seems as a uniform bulk with corresponding dispersion curve of permittivity and permeability using effective medium theory (EMT). This theory provides a framework for constructing medium-type metasurfaces to achieve the targeted response. Here, we report on the discovery of a new degree of freedom termed as quasi-complementary structure, which complements effective permittivity and permeability method for the design of robust single-layer metasurface in the microwave realm. Dissatisfied with the design of uniform metasurfaces that allow electromagnetic (EM) wave to pass at low frequencies and absorbs incident energy at high frequencies as derived from EMT, our approach enhances EM performance by modifying the metasurface configuration. Simulation results indicate that the quasi-complementary metasurfaces significantly outperform traditional patched designs when employing the same magnetic materials. Our findings thus confirm a viable strategy for boosting the EM performance of metasurfaces within the microwave spectrum.

articleTitle: A Wideband Multi-Layer Meta-Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel wideband multi-layer meta-dielectric resonator antenna (MLMDRA) is proposed in this paper. The MLMDRA is consist of 1×5 meta-dielectric resonator cuboid array. The MLMDRA achieves a wideband -10 dB impedance bandwidth of 45% (3.22-5.08 GHz). The proposed MDRA achieved a realized gain of 9.7 dBi.

articleTitle: Efficient DG-SETD Method for Multiscale Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An efficient discontinuous Galerkin spectral element time-domain(DG-SETD) method is proposed to calculate the electromagnetic scattering problem. Compared with the traditional continuous Galerkin time-domain spectral element method, the DG-SETD method discretizing the structure with small cell in the fine, irregular, high-dielectric-characteristic parts and coarse elements in the regular or simple smooth regions (e.g., air, PML, etc.)by nonconformal mesh, so the spatial discretization is more flexible. The upwind flux is introduced to ensure the continuity of the unknowns at the interface and the Gaussian integration is used to obtain the total surface integration. In addition, the proposed method adopts the Gauss-Lobatto-Legendre(GLL) basis function, which forms a mass matrix with orthogonal properties, so it can realize fast operations such as matrix multiplication and inverse. For-multi-scale complex electromagnetic models, the SETD method uses conformal-mesh for the entire region, which leads to a significant increase in the number of unknown quantities, prolonging the computation time, resulting in a waste of computational resources. In this case, the DG-SETD method uses non-conformal mesh splitting, which greatly reduces the number of cells and thus the number of unknown quantities, thus shortening the calculation time. At the same time, the use of fine dissection for fine regions ensures that the computational efficiency is improved without compromising the accuracy of the results. In this paper, the accuracy and efficiency of the above algorithm will be verified by calculating the scattering characteristics of a dispersive medium cube in the optical frequency band, providing a theoretical basis for calculating electromagnetic problems of multi-scale complex structures in the optical frequency band.

articleTitle: Formation and Side Lobe Suppression of Scanning Beams for Non-coplanar Distributed Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a beam forming method and a side lobe suppression method for non-coplanar distributed arrays((NCOPDAs)). In the simplified analyzing model extracted from the application model, two same uniform linear arrays are served as the subarrays, and their excitation conditions and scanning patterns at different angles in the airspace are deduced and computed respectively. Then the scanning beams of two subarrays are adjusted to point in the same direction respectively to ensure that two subarray’s electric fields have the same phases, so that they can be summed up to form the scanning beams. Finally, the excitation conditions for the scanning beam synthesis are obtained and verified to be valid. Further, via the idea of band-pass filtering, the scanning beam is processed with the adaptive Sa function filtering factor which is equal to the width of the beam to maximize the preservation of the main lobe, and filter out and suppress the high side lobe. The processed measured scanning patterns of the linear NCOPDAs in different states all show the side lobe level <-13dB, which verifies the effectiveness and flexibility of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Calculation of Parabolic Antenna Near-Field Coupling Characteristics with PO and Measurement Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The large radio telescope and the surrounding electronic equipment reside in the near-field region, where the coupling response between the electromagnetic signal and the parabolic surface directly impacts the telescope's electromagnetic compatibility design. We used the physical optics method to compute and analyze the electromagnetic coupling gain response of a 3 m aperture parabolic antenna in the 1-6 GHz frequency band to address the technical challenge of calculating electromagnetic coupling between near-field signals and the parabolic antenna. Based on this, we constructed an electromagnetic coupling measurement system and compared the measured data with theoretical calculations, showing an error of approximately 5 dB, thereby verifying the accuracy of the method. This method can be used for near-field electromagnetic coupling analysis of large radio telescopes, supporting the electromagnetic compatibility design of the telescope.

articleTitle: Invertible Fourier Neural Operator for Inverse Problem in Magnetotellurics
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In Magnetotellurics (MT), limited by the computing efficiency of traditional methods, time-consuming is an urgent research topic for complex models. In the past few years, artificial intelligence has been applied to speed up calculations of partial differential equations. Such artificial intelligence methods are also applied in MT. These MT inversion algorithms are based on designing forward models using artificial intelligence. They are used to replace the traditional forward modeling algorithms for speedup in the inverse algorithms. However, it didn't directly solve the inverse problem. A novel approach with the combination of the invertible neural network and Fourier neural operator is proposed in this paper. Due to the reversibility of the proposed approach, the inverse process is completed by training the forward process in the meantime. In addition, it can perform bidirectional training for higher accuracy of the inverse problem. The experimental results show that the approach can perform both forward simulation and inverse problem prediction well simultaneously.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Hydrodynamic Analysis of Optical Nonlocal Effects of Nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The effect of non-local optical response metallic nanostructures described by the hydrodynamical Drude model (HDM) is modeled and analyzed by the finite element method (FEM). A coupling is achieved by means of a set of Maxwell's equations and the hydrodynamic equations. An example of metallic nanodimer is provided to demonstrate this multiphysics modeling .

articleTitle: On Fast Tabulation of Green’s Function in Layered Medium Based on the GPU Parallelism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The method of moments for layered media structures requires the establishment of a three-dimensional interpolation table to compute the Green's function of layered media using the interpolation method. For multi-layered large-scale structures, the computation of interpolation tables is very time-consuming. This paper proposes an efficient computation method for three-dimensional interpolation table of dyadic Green’s Function for layered medium based on the graphics processing units. The decoupling of the horizontal and vertical position parameters in the spectral domain Green's function and Bessel function is utilized to reduce the computational burden associated with the integrand in the direct integration method. The numerical results show that the proposed method has good accuracy and reduces the time for the creation of the interpolation table to a few seconds from dozens of minutes.

Author Keywords: Dyadic Green’s Function for Layered Medium

articleTitle: Research on the application of wave absorbing materials in the design of ground penetrating radar antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper aims to explore the application requirements of absorbent materials in the design of time-domain ground-penetrating radar (GPR) antennas. It analyzes the propagation and absorption principle of absorbent materials at material interfaces and within materials. Based on the analysis, various loading methods of multi-layer composite foam absorbent materials are applied to the antennas. The CST electromagnetic simulation software is used to compare the simulation results of antennas with different loading methods in terms of waveform fidelity, gain, port impedance matching, and other parameters. Additionally, system-level modeling of transmission antennas, receiving antennas, detection scenarios, and target objects is conducted in conjunction with actual application scenarios. By comparing the received echo signals of antennas under different loading conditions, a study on the loading methods of absorbent materials is conducted, providing design and debugging guidance for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Partially Overlapping Basis Functions for Surface Integral Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This study proposes novel partially overlapping Rao-Wilton-Glisson (PO-RWG) basis functions defined at the boundary of local refined meshes, to solve surface integral equations for electromagnetic (EM) scattering. Differing from the traditional RWG basis functions, the proposed PO-RWG basis functions exhibit the property of localized domain overlapping. The normal continuity of the surface currents across the tearing contours is automatically satisfied by simply introducing additional RWG basis functions, eliminating the need for interior penalty (IP) terms typically required by the discontinuous Galerkin surface integral equation method. Key features of the proposed PO-RWG basis functions include ease of construction, straightforward implementation, adaptability, and versatility.

articleTitle: Flat-Top Metasurface Lens Antenna Synthesized by Woodward-Lawson Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a flat-top metasurface (MS) lens antenna synthesized by the Woodward-Lawson Method. The proposed MS lens antenna is composed of an MS and a circular patch antenna, while the patch antenna serves as the feed. To determine the transmission phase and amplitude distribution of the MS, theoretical analyses are applied. Then, a simulation model is established to verify the analyses. The proposed MS antenna operates at the central frequency of 10 GHz. The size is 6λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×6λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×1.53λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free-space wavelength). Simulated results show that a flat-top pattern is generated with a peak gain of 12.6 dBi and a 2-dB fluctuation range of nearly ±21°.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction via Coding Metasurfaces with Pancharatnam-Berry Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, two types of coding metasurfaces are designed based on the rotational phase modulation of the unit cell to reduce the radar cross section (RCS). The polarization conversion rate (PCR) of the unit cell exceeds 93.4% within the frequency band of 12.1-25.4 GHz. The 1-bit coding metasurface consists of two elements, denoted as "0" and "1", with rotational angles of ±45 degrees, respectively. By employing a rotation angle interval of 22.5° per element and a range spanning from 0° to 157.5°, a 3-bit coding scheme is realized, enabling the formation of a 3-bit coding metasurface. Both the 1-bit and 3-bit coding metasurfaces comprise 40×40 units cell, resulting in a total size of 200mm×200mm. Compared to the equivalently sized copper plates, the proposed metasurfaces yield 10dB RCS reduction within the 12.2-25.3 GHz frequency range. The simulation results validate that the design methodology of metasurfaces is effective, showcasing significant potential for applications in emerging technologies and materials for stealth capabilities.

articleTitle: A High-gain Differential-fed Dual-polarized Filtering Patch Antenna with Wide Stopband Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A high-gain differential-fed dual-polarized filtering antenna with broad out-of-band suppression is proposed. A ring resonator is attached to the antenna at the differential feed, along with the introduction of two low-frequency radiation nulls and one high-frequency radiation null. Furthermore, a novel high-frequency radiation null is formed by loading the SLR (stub-loaded resonator) structure, which improves the upper band’s edge selectivity and produces a broadband stopband suppression. The loading of U-shaped parasitic branches increases the current coupling path and broadens the working bandwidth. The proposed filtering patch antenna has a simple and compact structure and a low profile. It can reach a maximum gain of 8.72 dBi and an impedance bandwidth of roughly 10% (2.5-2.76 GHz). More than 30 dB separates the cross polarization from the main polarization, and the upper stopband can reach 1.5 f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the center frequency of the antenna), the lower stopband can reach 0.38 f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> , and the measured inhibition rate can reach 85%.

articleTitle: Multi-Resolution Preconditioned Augmented EFIE for Adaptive h-Refinement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multi-resolution preconditioned augmented electric field integral equation (MR-AEFIE) suitable for adaptive h-refinement based on residual error estimation is presented. The proposed MR-AEFIE effectively eliminates spurious resonances by incorporating the normal boundary condition of a perfect conductor into the MR-EFIE formulation. This resolves the issue where spurious internal resonances hinder the accurate estimation of errors by the residual estimator. Furthermore, by exclusively employing the $\mathcal{L}$-operator, the MR-AEFIE avoids the accuracy degradation caused by the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) and retains the pure characteristics of the electric field. Consequently, it can analyze scattering and radiation problems defined solely by the electric field with high fidelity.

articleTitle: Study on the Coupling Characteristics of High-power Electromagnetic Pulses and Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The time-domain coupling characteristics of different buildings under the impact of exterior high-power electromagnetic pulses (EMP) are studied in this paper. Field values and field distribution in horizontal sections inside buildings illuminated by high-altitude electromagnetic pulse (HEMP), ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse, high-power microwave (HPM), and Gaussian pulse are presented and compared in detail using the finite integration technique (FIT) method. Different factors such as the number of building layers which may affect the propagation characteristics are analyzed. These simulated results are useful for further evaluation of electromagnetic environment destruction effects and electromagnetic protection of sensitive devices or systems inside the buildings.

articleTitle: Forward Modeling for Bistatic Scattering center of Complex Target
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper develops a forward method to establish component-level bistatic scattering center for complex target. The model can not only describe the bistatic scattering characteristics of complex targets concisely and accurately, but also has clear electromagnetic scattering mechanism, physical meaning of parameters.

articleTitle: Distributed Cooperative Optimization for EIRP Improvement of Subarrayed Phased Array with Wide Beam Scanning Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A distributed cooperative optimization method is proposed in this paper, which aims to improve the effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP) of subarrayed phased array with a wide-angle beam scanning range. The EIRP of subarrayed phased array decreases dramatically during wide-angle scanning. However, the centralized optimization of EIRP for subarrayed phased array is recognized as NP-hard due to the complexity of the optimization variables and the non-convex inequality constraints. To address this, the original problem is decomposed into two subproblems: minimizing the quantized phase error and constraining the excitation amplitude dynamic range ratio. By cooperatively addressing these two subproblems, the EIRP is optimized. Numerical results show that the EIRP of the subarrayed phased array with 16×16 elements, under -10dB peak sidelobe level constraint, increases by 3.58dB when scanned to 60°.

articleTitle: Broadband actively amplifying metasurface for reconfigurable amplitude enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Amplifying metasurfaces have emerged as an efficient approach to realize energy enhancement. Here, we propose a broadband amplifying metasurface by combining amplifying circuits with elaborately designed H-shaped slotted square patch antennas. A prototype is fabricated and experimentally verified. The measured peak cross-polarized reflection coefficient is 15.1 dB and the operating band ranges from 3.69 GHz to 4.79 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 25.9%, which agree well with simulation results. The proposed metasurface shows potential uses in real-word applications, such as dynamic radar cross section (RCS) control and wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Forward modeling method for target edges
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Theoretical and experimental studies reveal that, in the high-frequency domain, a target's total electromagnetic scattering field can be decomposed into re-radiations from localized "scattering sources," known as scattering centers. Using the Stratton-Chu surface integral formula, it is understood that radiation from non-uniform electromagnetic flow near surface discontinuities and boundaries corresponds to edge diffraction, while radiation from uniform flow on smoothly curved surfaces corresponds to geometric optical reflection. Radar images typically show "bright spots" that correlate with these surface reflections and edge diffraction. To improve the accuracy of radar target scattering characteristic acquisition and to enhance the scattering center model by incorporating edge diffraction mechanisms, it is essential to advance electromagnetic modeling precision and comprehensiveness. This paper introduces an enhanced forward modeling method for scattering centers that integrates edge diffraction mechanisms. Building on the surface scattering mechanism and incremental length diffraction theory, this method first automatically classifies target edges as edge diffraction scattering centers based on geometric models. It then calculates the amplitude, frequency, position, and other attributes of each edge scattering center using the target's geometric parameters and edge diffraction coefficients.The effectiveness and accuracy of this forward edge diffraction modeling method are validated by comparing the reconstructed radar cross section (RCS) and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data with simulation results obtained from the Method of Moments (MOM). This method addresses the forward scattering center modeling of target edges and provides critical support for the detection and identification of low-observable targets.

articleTitle: Unified Localization Method Without Prior Range Information of Moving Target
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a unified localization method based on the time difference of arrival (TDOA) and the frequency difference of arrival (FDOA), which can estimate the position and velocity of the target when it is in the near-field, or the direction of the target when it is in the far-field. We use the modified polar representation (MPR) to unify the far-field and near-field models to construct an optimal localization problem with two constraints and propose an algebraic solution. The method first uses the least squares method to find the initial value without considering the constraints. Then the constraints are used to build an optimization equation to reduce the error of the initial value and obtain the precise value. Simulation results show that the proposed algorithm is close to the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB), verifying the performance.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Pattern Roundness for Handset Antennas using Reactive Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient and systematic design method for enhancing the pattern roundness of the handset antenna is proposed, providing more reliable links for terminal communications. Based on the platform of the handset antenna, an N-port network is constructed on the top part of the handset using discrete ports. Full-wave simulations are then carried out to obtain the impedance matrix and the single-port-excited patterns. Based on the impedance matrix, pattern synthesis is formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem and solved using the algorithm of NSGA-II. A WLAN antenna on the metallic-frame based handset is designed, with remarkable improvement in pattern roundness using only two lumped components. Specifically, the in-band gain of the proposed antenna is reduced by about 1.5 dB compared with the reference monopole antenna. More importantly, the original deep nulls are reduced, improving the SNR at many directions. The optimized handset antenna was fabricated and measured, with the measured results agreeing well with the simulated ones.

articleTitle: Wavelength-decoupled reflection-type metasurface with Hybrid Phase Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Manipulating the phase of incident electromagnetic (EM) waves is vital for directional modulation-enabled devices. Yet it still challenging to realize dual- or multi-wavelength independent phase modulations, where conventional multi-wavelength phase-controlled MSs consist of several resonant structures that make the process of design and fabrication complicated. Here, we employed a corner-truncated patch with hybrid phase modulation to simultaneously and mutually manipulate the reflective phase of dual wavelengths for circularly polarized (CP) incident EM waves, where it introduces Geometrical-Scaling-Induced (GSI) phase and Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase. To validate our concept, a multifunction polarization converter integrated on a 27 × 27 metasurface is devised, numerically characterized, and simulated, exhibiting distinct beam radiations within dual wavelength. Our study holds a novel possibility to realize multi-wavelength message encryption devices in smart communication and imaging systems.

articleTitle: Wearable Haptic-Response Object Sensing for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The paper presents a millimeter wave object detection technology for the visually impaired. A non-invasive PCB is designed to be used at shoe level combining with Body Area Networks (BANs) for tripping hazard detection. An accelerometer is used for calculating the orientation of the PCB. Time of Arrival (TOA) estimates derived from the Millimeter wave module trigger diverse haptic responses through DC Eccentric Rotating Mass (ERM) vibration motors. The device is engineered not to disrupt existing aids like white canes for the visually impaired.

articleTitle: A Provably Stable FDTD Method for MTL Equations
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To guarantee the long-time stability and accuracy of simulations of multiconductor transmission lines (MTLs), a provably stable summation-by-parts simultaneous approximation term (SBP-SAT) finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is proposed. In the proposed method, SBP operators were introduced to model MTL equations and simultaneous approximation terms (SATs) were used to enforce the impedance on the boundary weakly. Its long-time stability can be theoretically given. Several numerical results validate its accuracy and stability.

articleTitle: Wide-angle Scanning and Beam Optimization of Circularly Polarized Hemispherical Phased Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Conformal phased arrays have received continuous attention from scholars due to their excellent beam scanning performance. In this paper, a circularly polarized hemispherical phased array is designed to achieve half-space beam scanning. The active element patterns (AEP) for each array element are extracted, and beam synthesis of the spherical array is conducted considering mutual coupling. The numerical experimental results are in good agreement with the High Frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS) simulation results, validating the effectiveness of the method. For conformal arrays, not all antenna elements contribute to the main beam, so it is necessary to determine which antenna elements are active and which are inactive. An adaptive evolution strategy based on the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES) is employed to optimize the excitation phases of working antenna elements, greatly reducing side lobe level (SLL).

articleTitle: A Broadband Large-angle Anomalous Reflection Phase Gradient Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, a broadband phase gradient metasurface (PGM) that can achieve relatively large-angle anomalous reflection is proposed. The PGM unit consists of a cross dipole and three square rings. Simulated results show that the PGM with the size of 160×160 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> can achieve anomalous reflection at 11-15 GHz when the incident angle is less than 35°.

articleTitle: Research on Music Recommendation System Based on Collaborative Filtering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the explosive growth of Internet multimedia technology, the application of music recommendation system refers to the recommendation of personalization, helping users to have a large number of sounds, out of their taste. Based on the separation of Vue+Python, this system has developed a voice recommendation platform based on the collaborative recommendation mechanism. And based on the user's preferences in the first few rows, select the music works pushed or tasted by the user's like-minded user and the associated user.

articleTitle: Tunable Magnetic-Core Inductor Based on TSV Vertical Switch
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: As an important passive device, tunable inductor has great potential in the field of radio frequency (RF) integrated circuit (IC). In this paper, a tunable magnetic-core inductance based on through-silicon via (TSV) vertical switch is proposed. The inductor has two tuning modes. Firstly, the magnetic field generated by the control inductor plus DC bias current causes the change of the core permeability, thus causing the change of the inductance value, so as to realize the continuous adjustment of the inductance. Secondly, by turning on and off of TSV vertical switch, two different inductance connection modes and inductance coil length are generated to realize two different inductance values. The results show that the inductor can achieve 91 % tuning under the DC bias current of 0.1 ~ 40 mA.

articleTitle: A Mixed Total Field/Scattered Field-Based Discontinuous Galerkin Frequency Domain Method in a Uniaxial Medium
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A mixed total field/scattered field (TF/SF) discontinuous Galerkins method in frequency domain (DGFD) in a uniaxial medium is proposed to model scattered fields accurately. The TF/SF is implemented with the domain decomposition method, where different subdomains can either use TF DGFD scheme or SF DGFD scheme. The Riemann transmission condition is adopted to couple different subdomains, where at interfaces the Riemann transmission condition is modified with the incident fields from uniaxial background medium due to imposed sources. A numerical example with uniaxial background media and a uniaxial scatter is modeled to validate the algorithm by comparing the results with the finite element method.

articleTitle: Enhanced DGTD Method Using RCM Unit Reorder Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an enhanced Discontinuous Galerkin Time Domain (DGTD) method is proposed to solve the time-consuming problem of discontinuous memory access by using a unit reorder method based on Reverse Cuthill-McKee (RCM). The influence of locality on cache hit was analyzed for DGTD method and an example was used to assess the improvement of unit locality by the RCM reorder. The numerical results demonstrate efficiency and the performance of the DGTD method using RCM unit reorder technique.

articleTitle: Efficient Solution of Characteristic Modes Using Wideband Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In characteristic mode analysis (CMA), characteristic modes (CMs) on wideband frequency need to be solved for analyzing physical characteristics. This paper proposes an efficient method to obtain wideband CMs by solving the generalized eigenvalue problems (GEPs). In this method, the wideband Sherman-Morrison-Woodbury algorithm (WSMWA) is embedded into implicitly restarted Arnoldi method (IRAM). Numerical results show that the proposed method can save much CPU time.

articleTitle: Intelligent and Efficient Optimization Design for Ultra-Wideband High-Performance Complex Wave-Absorbing Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a intelligent approach for designing and optimizing multi-layer resistive film absorbing structures across various frequency ranges. Initially, a deep neural network (DNN) is trained to accurately forecast the wave absorption performance of the model. Subsequently, utilizing the genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization (GA-PSO), parameters are optimized for absorption within the target frequency band and the overall thickness of the model, establishing a rapid and effective design methodology tailored to diverse requirements. The proposed algorithm is employed to simulate and validate the optimization outcomes for the 8-100GHz and 2-20GHz frequency bands, achieving an average absorption rate exceeding 90% throughout the bands. This method simplifies the design process significantly and facilitates intelligent optimization for intricate absorption structures.

articleTitle: Dual-Layer Coupling Enhanced Complementary Metasurfaces for 1-bit Terahertz Beam Steering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In addressing the challenges of independent control and low efficiency in single-layer structures for terahertz (THz) electrically-controlled encoding metasurfaces, this paper presents a novel 1-bit independently-controlled reconfigurable intelligent metasurface integrated with high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) heterostructures. By modulating dual-layer coupling on complementary hexagonal ring resonators by HEMT, the reflection efficiency and phase shift bandwidth are effectively enhanced. Within the frequency range of 0.32-0.37 THz, the metasurface exhibits unit insertion loss of less than 5 dB within a phase shift range of 180±30 °, and a beam scanning range exceeding 120°. The proposed dual-layer complementary coupling-enhanced THz HEMT reconfigurable metasurface offers an effective technological approach for realizing large-scale, highly integrated THz reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS), holding significant application value in THz wireless communication, imaging, and radar detection systems empowered by RIS.

articleTitle: Dual-UWB Shared-Aperture End-Fire Antennas Embedded in an Inverted Trapezoid Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The increasing demand for ultrawideband end-fire antennas with a compact shared aperture on aircraft platforms. These antennas are sought after for their ability to achieve multiband capability and maximize spatial efficiency. This paper presents a dual ultra-wideband shared aperture end-fire antenna embedded in an inverted trapezoid cavity, which consists of a low-band antenna, a high-band antenna, and a dielectric lens. The antennas have been miniaturized and embedded into the cavity. An antenna prototype is fabricated and tested, which can operate independently at 2.1GHz-6GHz and 6GHz-18GHz, and exhibits stable end-fire radiation patterns. It demonstrates the potential for embedment applications on aircraft platforms.

articleTitle: A Wideband Filtering Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wideband filtering dielectric resonator antenna (FDRA) with compact structure is proposed. The DRA is fed by three vertical stepped metal strip and two rectangular rings, excited in its fundamental TE111 mode. Therefore, the antenna achieves a wide bandwidth of 28.9% and obtains a smooth average realized gain of 5.5 dBi. Besides, the feed structure produces two radiation nulls close to the lower and upper edges of the passband, enabling FDRA to achieve out-of-band rejection of over 15dB.

articleTitle: Wideband Bandpass Filter Based on HMSIW and SSPP Structures with Controllable Notch Band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel wideband bandpass filter (BPF) with a controllable notch band, utilizing a combination of half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) and spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPP) is proposed. The wideband BPF is designed using a triangular HMSIW structure integrated with an SSPP structure. To introduce a notch, a U-shaped ring resonator is embedded in the metal layer. The center frequency of the notch band can be controlled by varying the length of the U-shaped ring resonator. Simulation results indicate that the frequency range of the passband is from 4.53 GHz to 9.27 GHz, and the notch band are operated at 7.85-8.54 GHz, with a return loss of less than -10 dB.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized Fabry–Perot Antenna Carrying Orbital Angular Momentum
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A circularly polarized Fabry–Perot (FP) antenna with orbital angular momentum (OAM) order l=1 is proposed in this paper. The presented FP antenna is fed by a patch radiator with conical beam operated at TM21 mode which radiates circularly polarized vortex beam. A single-layer complementary partially reflective surface (PRS) with positive slope of reflection phase is used to increase the directivity and decrease the beam divergence angle of the patch radiator. The proposed FP antenna with vortex beam exhibits a peak gain of 12.1 dBi at 5 GHz with a beam divergence angle of 11 degrees, compared with 5 dBi and 35 degrees for the feed, indicating the validity of the proposed design.

articleTitle: Compact Quarter-Mode SIW MIMO Antennas Using Neutralization Line for V2X Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: We introduce a neutralization line (NL) in quarter-mode substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) antennas, aimed at constructing compact MIMO antennas for V2X applications while mitigating their mutual coupling. By exploring a simple NL between dual-element quarter-mode SIW antennas, it is discovered that mutual coupling can be effectively suppressed even though the edge-to-edge distance is only 1 mm. The effectiveness and adaptability of the NL in decoupling SIW MIMO antennas are confirmed. Meanwhile, it is revealed that the proposed MIMO SIW antennas with NL has advantages of high isolation, compactness, and easy integration.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation and Analysis of Magnetic Detection in Oil and Gas Casings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Metal oil and gas casings undergo magnetization phenomena when influenced by the geomagnetic field, subsequently affecting the surrounding magnetic field. By utilizing COMSOL Multiphysics software, the distribution pattern of magnetic anomalies around casing with couplings under the influence of the geomagnetic field can be simulated and analyzed. The research results indicate that the direction of the magnetic field generated by casing magnetization is correlated with the direction of the geomagnetic field. Additionally, the magnetic field surrounding the magnetized casing exhibits significant fluctuations at a distance of approximately 5 meters from the casing. Analyzing these fluctuations can help identify abnormal conditions such as casing damage. These research findings provide theoretical assistance for understanding the distribution pattern of the magnetic field around magnetized casings and contribute to practical drilling casing applications.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Bandpass Filter with Low Insertion Loss Using Simple SIR Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a new dual-band bandpass filter with low insertion loss and compact size is presented. The study focuses on the resonance features of mixed electromagnetic coupling and cross coupling. The system utilizes a pair of dual-resonance resonators (DRRs) with mixed electromagnetic coupling to generate two signals of different frequencies. It then employs an open-ended stepped-impedance resonators cross-coupled with short-circuit stepped impedance DDRS to produce transmission zero. The analysis results indicate that the open-ended stepped-impedance resonator generates a transmission zero that is located close to the passband. This leads to a reduction in out-of-band insertion loss and enables the realization of a wide passband bandpass filter.

articleTitle: RCS Frequency Extrapolation Based on two-dimensional GTD Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The radar cross section (RCS) database needs to store a large number of measured or calculated RCS in different frequency bands. There are two methods to obtain RCS: theoretical calculation and actual measurement. It is very difficult to calculate the RCS of a complex target by theoretical analysis, while the actual measurement is often demanding on the test equipment and the workload is high. Therefore, the methods of RCS compression, interpolation and extrapolation appear to be of crucial importance. In this paper, we propose a method for extrapolation based on the 2D-GTD model. This method can extract the scattering center model parameters of complex scatterers, synthesize the frequency response of the target, and extend the echo data from a certain frequency band to other frequency bands. The extrapolation data were compared with the FEKO simulation data to verify the feasibility and accuracy of the extrapolation method. From the obtained results, the method can effectively synthesize the RCS of the target in different frequency bands.

articleTitle: A Transparent Water-Based Radar-Infrared Bi-Stealth Metamaterial with Microwave Tunability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A transparent water-based tunable radar-infrared (IR) bi-stealth metamaterial is proposed in this paper. The IR emissivity of the proposed metamaterial in the IR band of 8-14μm is less than 0.24. The simulation results show that the microwave reflection band below -10 dB can be tuned from 3.74-6.03 GHz to 7.21-9.58 GHz by changing the thickness of the water spacer. Meanwhile, the metamaterial has good incident angle and polarization stability. In addition, The metamaterial composed of transparent materials are optically transparent.

articleTitle: Miniaturization Design of LC Filter Based on LTCC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to reduce the circuit area and improve the performance of the device, an LC bandpass filter with dimensions of 7.1 mm×2.8 mm×1.63 mm is designed for the low-frequency band operating from 1.2 GHz to 1.5 GHz using low temperature co-fired ceramic technology in this paper. In particular, in order to improve the harmonics generated by the LC bandpass filter at high frequencies, an LC low-pass filter is designed and cascaded with the bandpass filter for simulation. The simulation results show that the filter has good transmission characteristics and out-of-band rejection, and the return losses are better than 12.5 dB, which realizes the miniaturized design of the filter.

articleTitle: Thermal Transient Response of SOI LDMOSFET Under Electromagnetic Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the development of communication technology, electromagnetic signals in the environment are becoming more and more complex, and many circuits and systems will fail due to external electromagnetic interference. This study conducts an analysis on the Silicon-On-Insulator Lateral Double-Diffused Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistor (SOI LDMOSFET) under electromagnetic interference by using finite element method to solve drift-diffusion equations and the Fourier heat conduction equation. Our in-house developed algorithms are capable to get temperature response of SOI LDMOSFET under electromagnetic pulse. The simulation results are of significance in understanding the reliability of RF power devices.

Author Keywords: laterally diffused metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (LDMOSFET)

articleTitle: Research on Network Intrusion Detection System Based on Independent Q-learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that traditional network intrusion detection systems have low accuracy in identifying complex and changeable network attack patterns, a multi-agent network intrusion detection system based on independent Q-learning is proposed. The system adopts a multi-agent architecture, and each agent uses an independent Q learning algorithm to monitor and assess network behavior, and improves the efficiency and accuracy of network intrusion detection through intelligent methods. The experimental results show that compared with traditional intrusion detection methods, the detection accuracy, response speed and robustness of this system are significantly improved. It can show good adaptability and generalization ability. It provides a new solution for the field of network security and has certain theoretical and practical value for building a more intelligent and reliable network security protection system.

articleTitle: Resonance Scattering Generated by a Rotating Dielectric Mesoscale Sphere
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The resonance scattering generated by a dielectric mesoscale sphere exerted by polarized plane waves is studied based on the "instantaneous rest-frame" hypothesis and Minkowski’s theory. Both the electric and magnetic resonances are discussed. The characteristic of resonance scattering of a rotating sphere is discussed. The impact of the rotating dimensionless parameter γ , which determines the rotation angular velocity of a particle on the resonance scattering, is emphasized. The results of this paper have promising potential applications for mesotronics, which provides a novel design method for rotating resonators and ultra-sensitive sensors.

articleTitle: Double-layer high-gain filter microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-layer high-gain filtering microstrip patch antenna. The filter antenna exhibits high gain and good frequency selectivity. The filter section consists of a CQ filter composed of four open-loop rings, which exhibits good return loss and insertion loss. The antenna section is improved based on etched gaps in traditional rectangular patch antennas, comprising a rectangular loop patch and a rectangular patch with a pair of short-circuit vias, coupled by T-shaped microstrip lines, achieving higher gain. This dual-layer filter antenna demonstrates high gain and impedance matching within the operating frequency band, with two radiation nulls where the gain is very low, resulting in good edge roll-off characteristics.

articleTitle: A Hybrid HIE-FDTD/TDPO Method for Transient Far-Fields of Combinative Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel hybrid schema that combines the hybrid implicit-explicit finite-difference time-domain (HIE-FDTD) method with time-domain physical optics (TDPO) is presented. The HIE-FDTD method employs a hybrid implicit explicit schema along the fine structure direction to mitigate the constraint imposed by fine spatial mesh on the time step size. Consequently, this hybrid method proves advantageous for scenarios involving objects that combine electrically small structure characterized by very fine structures in one direction with an electrically large size target. Compared with the traditional FDTD/TDPO hybrid method, the HIE-FDTD/TDPO hybrid method significantly improves computational efficiency. Numerical results validate the efficiency and accuracy of this novel hybrid approach.

articleTitle: A metamaterial lens system for remote focusing and monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Near-field focusing lenses are frequently constrained by the diffraction limit, necessitating the deployment of large aperture arrays to achieve both small focal spots and long focal lengths. In electromagnetic (EM) sensing applications, it is necessary to ensure that the path is unobstructed, which may lead to the internal sensing being affected by the external environment and even endanger personal safety in high-temperature sensing. In order to address the aforementioned issues, this paper presents a cascade lens system comprising two metamaterial lenses with varying structural characteristics. This configuration enables the focal length to be extended without the necessity for a particularly large array. Furthermore, the material of the secondary lens is quartz glass, which is resistant to high temperatures and serves to isolate the environment. At the same time, it can be used as a viewing window.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Filtering Antenna with Parasitic Strips for 5G Application Using SISL Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A Millimeter-Wave Filtering Antenna is proposed in this paper by using substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) technology. The proposed antenna constitutes a driven patch, a stacked patch, two parasitic strips and a coupling branch. The first radiation null is generated by the coupling branch at the lower band, and the other radiation null is caused by the introduction of two parasitic strips. Due to the introduction of stacked patch, not only new resonance point is generated, but also another radiation null is produced at the upper band edge. The above three radiation nulls achieve good filtering performance with high selectivity. The simulated results demonstrate that the passband is from 24.48 to 27.89 GHz and the peak gain reaches 7.85 dBi. In addition, the out-of-band rejection level is 15.2 dB.

articleTitle: A high-efficiency testing method of microwave high-power module
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of efficient batch and fast testing of microwave high-power module, a high-efficiency testing method is proposed, and a fast testing fixture is developed. Aiming at the problems of many test cables and low test efficiency of microwave high-power modules, a plum blossom-shaped pin and an elastic copper sheet are selected, and a pressing mode is adopted to realize the close contact between the plum blossom-shaped pin and an insulator,between the elastic copper sheet and a microstrip line, achieves the purposes of sodering-free wire powering and sodering-free microwave connection of the microwave high-power module.Finally,the rapid test fixture has a current of 10A and a power of more than 1000W.Compared with the traditional welding test method,the test efficiency is increased by 300%.

articleTitle: A Fast Prediction Approach of Target Partition Scattering Characteristics Based on the Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To grasp the scattering characteristics of each subarea on the target, a fast prediction method for the scattering characteristics of the target subarea considering the fully electromagnetically coupled state on the basis of the integral equation method is proposed in this paper. The radar cross-section for a given frequency and observation direction is firstly solved by the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). Then, the contribution of the scattering field is obtained by integrating the currents in each subarea. The physical concept of the method is clear and the computational cost is extremely low. the proposal is used to analyze the partition scattering characteristics for a typical target, and the simulation results verify the effectiveness of the methodology.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Mixed-Mode OAM Antenna Based on Impedance-Modulated Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A low-profile mixed-mode orbital angular momentum(OAM) antenna based on impedance modulated surface is proposed, which consists of a monopole and a tensor holographic metasurface. This design adopts a partitioning method, where the holographic metasurface is divided into four ring areas. OAM modes of 1, 2, 3, and 4 are generated by these four regions from inside out respectively, and thus realize a directional vortex beam. Besides, the realized directional beam still retains vortex phase distribution, which means this antenna can be employed to improve OAM transmission distance.

articleTitle: Research on High Frequency Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Dielectric-PEC Composite Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The prediction of radar characteristics of complex medium targets has become an important research topic in the field of radar target characteristics. In this paper, within the framework of high-frequency method, a set of more perfect research method of electromagnetic scattering characteristics of medium-containing complex targets is established. Firstly, based on the geometrical model and material electromagnetic parameters of the complex electric target with dielectric material, the geometrical and material model partition and description method of the complex electric target with dielectric material are studied. Secondly, a multiple-action illumination surface judgement algorithm for dielectric targets is proposed to obtain the set of single- and multiple-coupled reflected ray paths on the surface, and the set of multiple-coupled transmitted ray paths in the interior formed by transmission on the dielectric surface. Finally, the scattering field of each ray collection is calculated using the physical optics algorithm, and the scattering characteristics of the whole target are obtained by coherent superposition. The effectiveness and accuracy of the PO method and the GO-PO algorithm are verified using several typical models.

articleTitle: A Transparent Decoupling Surface (TDS) For Multi-Band Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel transparent decoupling surface (TDS) is proposed based on band-stop frequency selective surface(FSS). The TDS can function as a traditional decoupling surface in low band (0.79-0.96GHz), and exhibits transparency in high band (2.3-2.7GHz) simultaneously. First, a miniaturized FSS is proposed through fractal branch design. It is found the FSS exhibit two passbands with little transmission loss, little transmission phase shift is observed in higher passband, too. The proposed TDS is validated on LB and HB antennas, respectively. The simulated results prove its ability of decoupling in low band and transparency in high band. The results indicate that the proposed decoupling surface has good potential for multi-band array. This design extends the scope of decoupling surface by making it applicable to multi-band antenna systems.

articleTitle: A Flexible Numerical Integration Strategy for Accurate Simulation of Cavity Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Accurately simulating electromagnetic scattering within cavities presents significant challenges due to the intricate wave behavior. Beyond the well-known convergence issues, this work focuses on the sensitivity of computational accuracy during numerical implementation. Our research identifies that the accuracy of the integral equation (IE) method is significantly influenced by the Gaussian integration rule. Specifically, achieving high accuracy requires high-order Gaussian integration rules, which in turn increase computational time. To address this issue, we propose a flexible numerical integration strategy (FNIS) that adaptively selects integration rules based on the distance between basis and test functions. Numerical examples validate our approach, demonstrating improved computational efficiency while maintaining high accuracy.

articleTitle: Skeletonization-Scheme Sampling for Narrow-band Pulse Radar Target Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Narrowband pulse radar signals can be received and processed to detect the presence or absence of a target. However, the Nyquist sampling theorem, which has been used for radar signal target detection, actually acquires redundant information when the signal is sampled. The efficiency of signal sampling can be improved if the number of sampling points can be reduced without degradation of detection performance. This paper reduces the number of sampling points by introducing a skeletonization-scheme sampling for time-domain signal. Simulations show that when the number of sampling points and the detection performance are the same as that of the Nyquist sampling scheme, the skeletonization sampling scheme only requires narrower pulse width, which reduces the power consumption of the radar.

articleTitle: Joint Optimization of Radar and Communication Performance Based on Time-Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, a joint optimization method for radar and communication performance based on time-modulated array is proposed with differential evolution (DE) algorithm. With the proposed method, the optimized timing parameters can meet the minimum data rate requirements and maximize the detection probability. A numerical example is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of this method in simultaneously detection and multi-user communication. The proposed method provides an energy-efficient and practical approach for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in future networks.

articleTitle: Multiphysics Modeling and Characterization of Resistive Random Access Memory Device
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Multiphysics modeling and simulation of resistive random access memory (RRAM) device is presented in this paper. Three partial differential equations of physical fields are coupled and solved by finite element method. The breakage of conducting filaments and changes of Oxygen vacancy concentration in a metal oxide RRAM are analyzed.

articleTitle: Multi-Site Prediction Method for Atmospheric Pollutants Based on an Improved MLP-Mixer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The challenge in atmospheric pollutant forecasting lies in the fact that urban areas consist of multiple monitoring stations representing different regions, and the pollutant variations at these stations often differ. Employing traditional methods to design a universal predictive model results in lower accuracy of forecasted outcomes, and training specific models for different monitoring stations requires excessive time and labor costs. To address these issues, a multi-site atmospheric pollutant forecasting method based on an improved MLP-Mixer is proposed. Experiments were conducted on data sets from 12 main meteorological monitoring stations in Beijing and 145 stations in a certain industrial city. The designed model outperforms other models in predicting atmospheric pollutants for the next 24 hours, verifying the accuracy of the improved MLP-Mixer approach.

articleTitle: Vortex Wave OAM Mode Conversion Device with Adjustable Amplitude and Phase Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: As an alternative degree of freedom for wireless communications, orbital angular momentum (OAM) multiplexing and demultiplexing can be applied to achieve higher communication capacity. Metasurface has advanced ability to manipulate electromagnetic (EM) waves, and has gradually become an important technology for future wireless communications. In this paper, we propose a transmission metasurface with adjustable amplitude and phase, which can control the OAM mode spectrum of vortex waves generated by vortex sources. A metasurface is applied as the vortex source, and another transmission metasurface is cascaded as a vortex wave OAM mode conversion device. By introducing weight coefficient of different OAM modes during the design process, the proposed vortex wave OAM mode conversion device can generate vortex waves with energy-distributed controllable OAM modes.

articleTitle: Performance of Parallel Higher-Order Method of Moments Using 10 M Heterogeneous Many-Core Processors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the high-performance heterogeneous many-core processor on the new-generation Sunway supercomputer platform is used to realize the solution of the radiation problem with millions of unknowns, which demonstrates the high efficiency of the heterogeneous parallel Higher-Order Method of Moments (HOMoM). Numerical examples show that the Sunway heterogeneous parallel HOMoM achieved a parallel efficiency of more than 30% when the number of cores are increased from 633,750 to 10,140,000 and has high scalability and stability.

articleTitle: A Broadband and Thin Absorber Using Resistive Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A broadband and thin absorber in relation with frequency selective surface (FSS) is presented in this paper. The lossy layer of the structure consists of a double resonant plane FSS loaded with lumped resistors. The simulated results indicate that under normal incidence the working absorption bandwidth of the proposed absorber from 5.9GHz to 20.7GHz (111.3% in fractional bandwidth) is greater than 90%, and the thickness of the designed unit is only 4mm(0.079λ at lowest cutoff frequency). In addition, the effects of some geometrical dimensions and different incident angles on the sensitivity of absorption are studied.

articleTitle: Optimization of Low-scattering Shape Using Differential Evolution Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In modern warfare, the survivability and penetration ability of weapons are truly crucial, therefore, the radar stealth technology of weapons has attracted widespread attention. Shape is the greatest impact factor on stealth performance, so it is meaningful for the study of shape stealth technology. This paper research on the optimization of low-scattering shape using differential evolution algorithm. The base missile dome model is parameterized by NURBS (Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines) curves, so the shape of the missile dome can be adjusted by changing the coordinates of NURBS control points. The RCS (radar cross-section) of the models can be calculated by SBR (Shooting and Bouncing Ray) algorithm, subsequently, DE (differential evolution algorithm) is used to optimize the coordinate values of NURBS curve control points to find the optimal shape. The results show that compared with the base model, the RCS of optimized model has 5.9 dB reduction. The methods mentioned in this paper can be extended to surface optimization and can also be used for other aspects like optimizing the transmittance of radomes.

articleTitle: A DNN-Based Inversion Algorithm of Soil Moisture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the rapid development of computer science, deep learning methods have achieved applications in many fields. Due to the time-consuming and laborious measurement of soil moisture during ground scattering characterization experiments, a deep learning (DL)-based inversion algorithm of soil moisture was proposed in this paper. First, the Oh model was utilized to generate the training samples. Then, a deep neural network (DNN) was constructed to establish the relationship between soil moisture and the back scattering coefficients. Finally, the inversion values were compared with the measured data. The results demonstrated that the proposed DNN model outperforms other models in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Wave Dispersion Curve Computation for Quasi-1D Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The quasi-one-dimensional (quasi-1D) spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) provides a new route for optically transparent electronic devices. The dispersion curves can control the electromagnetic wave propagation characteristics of the quasi-1D SSPP by manipulating the geometric parameters. However, the dispersion curves of quasi-1D SSPP have not been analytically derived and thoroughly studied. This paper derives the dispersion curves of the quasi-1D SSPP using equivalent permittivity and permeability methods, which can accurately predict the relationship between wave number and its geometric parameters. The simulation results validate the proposed dispersion curves. Based on the dispersion curves, this paper further presents a broadband optically transparent transmission line, which can achieve high-efficiency transmission from 3.0 to 14.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Study on Near-Field Focusing Implemented by 3D-Printed Holographic Impedance Surfaces at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a 3D-printed holographic impedance surface (HIS) for near-field focusing. The focusing spot at different distances from the HIS is studied. The good focusing performance can be achieved when the focusing distance from the HIS is lower than 5λ.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Thermal-Stress Multiphysics Simulation of a Non-uniform Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, A multi-physics field simulation method based on the finite element method is developed for Non-uniform Array. Non-uniform array technology provides a solution for sidelobe level reduction. We analyses the multi-physics fields of non-uniformly spaced array antennas by finite element method.

articleTitle: A Dual-Model-Base Adaptive Sampling Method for Fast Computation of Wide Band RCS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To calculate broadband electromagnetic scattering more quickly, an adaptive sampling method based on dual models is proposed on the basis of traditional interpolation sampling algorithms. This method can independently select sampling frequency points through an adaptive scheme, thus greatly reducing the computation time. This scheme adopts the rational function model and the Lagrange polynomial model to interpolate the frequency sweep curve, and the computation time is significantly lower than that of existing adaptive sampling methods. The Moment of Method (MoM) is used to calculate the induced current at the frequency points, while the proposed dual-model adaptive sampling strategy is used to evaluate the induced current at other frequency points. The final numerical calculation results show that the adaptive algorithm can obtain high-precision broadband radar cross section (RCS) curves and significantly reduce the computation time.

articleTitle: Heart-shaped Wideband Monopole Patch Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The paper presents a heart-shaped wide band monopole patch antenna for wireless communication applications. The patch is designed on Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate with overall dimensions of 41mm×36mm×2.036mm. At the top layer, the patch is V-Chamfered which enable to have good symmetry of radiation pattern and a V-slot at the center was inserted to improve both bandwidth and gain of the antenna.
