The antenna has an operating frequency range from 3.18 GHz to 9.41GHz. Simulation result shows that the peak realized gain of the antenna is 5.52 dBi at 7.2GHz. Due to the wide impedance bandwidths, high gain and good omnidirectional radiation properties, the proposed antenna can be useful in wireless communications applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Power Density Prediction for Mobile Handset Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Compliance with electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure limits is critical in the development of 5G millimeter-wave (mm-wave) terminals equipped with array antennas, requiring peak incident power density (PD). Simulating array antennas within the frame of a mobile handset is time-consuming due to their small size. In this work, an efficient machine learning (ML) method is proposed to predict the maximum PD of array antennas within a mobile handset, significantly reducing computational time. Validation on a 4×1 cavity-backed slot array antenna demonstrated high accuracy in PD prediction, confirming its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Fast Electromagnetic Scattering Calculation for UAV Targets Based on Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To solve the problem of insufficient efficiency in electromagnetic simulation of UAV targets, this paper introduces the Barycentric subdivision method and graph neural network and proposes a fast electromagnetic scattering computational method. This method uses the impedance matrix and right-hand side terms from the method of moments as the node inputs for the graph network, which preserves the electromagnetic principles during computation and ensures the generalization ability. Additionally, the graph network is used to predict updates of the basis function coefficients, accelerating the solution of the matrix equation. Finally, the calculation results of the proposed method, MoM based on direct method and MoM based on BiCGSTAB are compared. The results demonstrate that the proposed method reduces the time consumption by an order of magnitude while maintaining accuracy, proving its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Absorption-High Frequency Transmission Tunable Frequency Selective Rasorber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with broadband absorption at low frequency and tunable transmission at high frequency is proposed. The top layer is loaded with double curved line structure to realize low frequency resonant absorption and high frequency lossless transmission. The bottom layer adopts an active band-pass frequency-selective structure. By loading varactor diodes, the frequency of transmission peak can be tuned continuously in a wide band. Simulation results show that for x-polarized wave, the -10 dB absorption band is 3.1 to 6 GHz. For y-polarized wave, the -10 dB absorption band is 3.1 to 6.6 GHz. The transmission peak of the FSR can be continuously tuned from 8 to 16.8 GHz, and its transmission coefficient is between -3.2 and -0.8 dB. The design has a broad application prospect in the field of stealth and multi-frequency transmission of active radar radome.

articleTitle: Efficient Radiation Analysis of the Antenna Located on Electrically Large Bodies Over a broad Frequency band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel approach is introduced in this study, which integrates the efficient iterative method of moments-physical optics (EI-MoM-PO) with asymptotic waveform evaluation (AWE) technology for fast determination of antenna radiation pattern above the electrically large platforms. This methodology involves Taylor series and Padé approximation to calculate the self-impedance matrix and the additional exciting voltage, enabling the extraction of frequency information in the vicinity of the expansion point. A numerical result demonstrates the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method while comparing with the EI-MoM-PO and the conventional MoM-PO.

articleTitle: Synthesis Design of Three-Dimensional Wideband Polarization-Rotating Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The synthesis technique for a wideband three-dimensional Polarization-Rotating Surface (PRS) is presented in this paper. Firstly, two types of circuit models with shunt short-ended stubs are discussed, whose frequency responses can be synthesized using Chebyshev functions. Upon specifying performance parameters, including filtering orders (N=4, N=5), fractional bandwidth (FBW), and return loss (RL), all circuit parameters can be derived from the filtering response specifications. A fourth-order wideband three-dimensional PRS with an FBW of 80% and an equal-ripple RL of 10 dB is then proposed, realized using a slotline-microstrip-slotline coupling structure. To further improve the frequency responses, a fifth-order wideband three-dimensional PRS with an FBW of 120% and an equal-ripple RL of 10 dB is proposed. The close alignment between the simulated and measured results with the predicted responses indicates that the proposed synthesis method is an efficient solution for designing a wideband PRS.

articleTitle: Radiation-Stealth Integrated Antenna Structure Based On FSR
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article proposes a radiation-stealth integrated antenna structure based on an FSR (Frequency Selective Rasorber) structure. When the antenna is operational, this structure functions as a normal radiator; however, when it is inactive, the entire system becomes a broadband absorber. Simulation results indicate that the structure exhibits a VSWR < 3 bandwidth spanning from 9.69 GHz to 10.63 GHz, with boresight radiation gains exceeding 5.4 dBic. In non-operational state, the antenna structure achieves broadband absorption across the frequency range of 4.8 GHz to 15.48 GHz.

articleTitle: Miniatured and High-density 3D Solenoid Inductor Based on TSV Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: By using the through-silicon via (TSV) to interconnect the stacked layers vertically, three-dimensional integrated circuits (3D ICs) offer performance improvements in RF/microwave applications with reduced footprints and shortened wiring. In this work, a high-density 3D solenoid inductor based on TSV arrays is proposed. And the mathematical analysis model of the proposed inductor is established. Finally, by comparing with the structures proposed by other researches, a higher inductance density of 379.6nH/mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is observed in the proposed configuration while maintaining a good quality factor and a miniatured chip size. The performance superiority of the proposed inductor is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide Electromagnetic Coupled Filter with High Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes an electromagnetic coupled bandpass filter based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW). The 3dB passband range of the proposed filter is 30.8-33.74GHz with the center frequency of 32.27GHz, which is suitable for 5G millimeter wave systems. The stopband bandwidth with an out-of-band rejection level better than 20dB reaches nearly 10GHz. Two transmission zeros (TZ) are generated at frequencies of 29.85GHz and 35.1GHz, respectively, enhancing the out-of-band rejection and improving the frequency selectivity of the filter.

articleTitle: A Simple Decoupling Approach Based on Edge Effects of Millimeter Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The article presents a simple method to address the edge effects and surface wave impact of millimeter wave (mm-wave) by cutting a portion of the floor edge to achieve decoupling, eliminating the need for additional decoupling units and without increasing the profile height. The paper introduces a design using microstrip patch antennas and microstrip-coaxial feed for a 1×2 antenna array. Simulation results demonstrate that within the impedance bandwidth 22.82 - 26.81 GHz (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> < - 10 dB), and the coupling decreases from -18.5 dB to less than -25 dB, with the decoupling bandwidth lies between 23.67 - 26.94 GHz. This decoupling approach is simple, remains good radiation performance, and offers new insights for the design of multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna arrays.

articleTitle: Integrated Modeling and Analysis Approach for Folded Rinehart-Luneburg Lens Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Rinehart-Luneburg lens antenna with feature of rotational-symmetric shape offers a wide angular range and multiple-beam capabilities. An integrated modeling and analysis approach is proposed in this paper to simplify the design of this antenna with non-parametric folded curve. An optimized Rinehart-Luneburg lens antenna working at Q-band with reduced profile is designed. The height of the designed lens has been reduced by a factor of 2.7 compared to original Rinehart-Luneburg lens. Eleven waveguides are placed at an angle of 12° provide beam scanning capability in 120° range with scan loss below 1 dB, a realized gain higher than 18.5 dBi over the whole bandwidth.

articleTitle: Integrated Design and Simulation of Conformal Antenna and Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, based on the theoretical design of conformal antenna and Frequency selective surface(FSS), the conformal antenna and FSS array are modeled and simulated by finite element method (electromagnetic simulation software Ansys HFSS, and the optimal distance between the FSS structure and the conformal antenna is determined. The effect of FSS and antenna frequency on the gain pattern under the condition of optimum distance is studied. The design results show that after the optimal distance between the antenna and the FSS array is determined, the performance of the antenna will be greatly affected when the operating frequency of the FSS is different from that of the antenna. Therefore, When designing the integrated structure of conformal antenna and FSS, it is necessary to co-design and simulate the system composed of conformal antenna and FSS.

articleTitle: Circular waveguide TM01−TE11 mode converter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to the design of waveguide mode converters that differs from the commonly used double-bend and triple-bend structures. The approach employs sinusoidal function curves to construct the mode converters, and is based on the coupled wave theory. Furthermore, an optimization program for the structural parameters of the mode converters is developed. The differential evolution algorithm is employed to optimize the geometric structure of the circular waveguide TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> – TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> mode converter with a center frequency of 9.7 GHz, with the objective of achieving a maximum mode conversion efficiency of 99% or above. The efficacy of this approach is validated through simulation using HFSS simulation software. The results demonstrate that this mode converter exhibits high conversion efficiency. The highest mode conversion efficiency is 99.59%, and the bandwidth with conversion efficiency above 90% is approximately 1.19 GHz. The mode converter exhibits high conversion efficiency and a wide bandwidth, and is compatible with both input and output coaxial standards.

articleTitle: An interleaved parallel adjustable frequency selective surface based on varactor diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Designed a frequency selective surface that is continuously adjustable within multiple bands. By combining single-layer resonant components with variable capacitance diodes, dual band pass is achieved, and the passband frequency is continuously adjustable. Varactor diodes are arranged in the pattern gap, with adjacent rows of diodes facing opposite directions, known as staggered arrangement. The feeding metal wires make the entire circuit parallel, with the aim of loading them with equal voltage. By adjusting the voltage to change the capacitance value between the gaps, tuning function can be achieved.

articleTitle: A compact, metasurface-based wideband circularly polarized patch antenna with L-shaped AR tuning stubs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A compact, wideband circularly polarized (CP) patch antenna based on the metasurface (MS) is presented. The antenna composed of a truncated corner square patch with four L-shaped axial ratio (AR) tuning stubs is sandwiched between the metasurface (MS) and the ground plane. The MS is composed of a lattice of 4 × 4 periodic metal plates. When surface waves on the MS are stimulated within the antenna structure, it will broaden the impedance bandwidth and AR bandwidth of the antenna. The proposed antenna adopts a stacked layout with an overall size of 40mm × 40mm × 4.5mm (0.71λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.71λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, at 5.3 GHz). The simulation results show a |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < -10 dB bandwidth of 4.24-6.38 GHz (40.3%) and 3 dB AR bandwidth of 4.42-5.45 GHz (20.9%). Additionally, it achieves a peak gain of 8.67 dBi.

articleTitle: Study on Composite Electromagnetic Scattering of a Ship in Land-Sea Junction Background
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the electromagnetic scattering of a PEC ship target in land-sea junction area with a curved coastline is calculated using the shooting and bouncing ray method combined with the physical theory of diffraction (SBR-PTD). The land-sea composite surface with a curved coastline and dielectric constant information is established based on the hierarchical matching method proposed in this work. The basic theory of SBR-PTD is expounded and then the monostatic radar cross sections (RCSs) of the established land-sea junction background composite the ship model is simulated. The data comprehensively demonstrate the coupling effect between the ship model and the land-sea junction background, providing theoretical support for radar scattering research in coastal areas.

articleTitle: Research on The Algorithm of GPR Data Bandwidth Extension Based on Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Enhancing the temporal resolution of Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) data has been one of the primary goals in GPR data processing, as higher temporal resolution can yield more precise information on the subsurface structure. In subterranean medium, high-frequency electromagnetic waves weaken more quickly. As a result, the signal's high-frequency component shows comparatively weak energy when it is broken down into the continuous wavelet domain. Enhancing resolution means making up for the lost high-frequency energy in the continuous wavelet domain, assuming that the amplitude spectral energy of high-resolution GPR signals is roughly horizontal. This paper presents an algorithm for bandwidth extension using Continuous Wavelet Transform (CWT) and explores the selection of key parameters to enhance the resolution of GPR data. The effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed algorithm are validated using practical detection data.

articleTitle: A Method for Setting Alarm Limits for Electromagnetic Alarm System Applied in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To assess and manage nuclear power plant electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) comprehensively, this paper proposes a method for setting alarm limits. Based on this, alarm limits for typical equipment in a nuclear power plant were established to ensure both accurate alerts and avoid false alarms, supporting overall electromagnetic compatibility assessment.

articleTitle: A High-Efficiency Folded Mode-Converting Transmitarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high-efficiency folded mode-converting transmitarray antenna (FMCTA) is proposed. The proposed FMCTA consists of a top-layer receiver-transmitter surface (RTS), a bottom-layer polarization rotating surface (PRS) and a TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode actuator with a conical horn. The circular waveguide TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode can be converted into a linearly polarized (LP) wave by the RTS and the whole profile of the antenna is reduced by PRS. The simulated results show that the proposed FMCTA obtains a gain of 27.4 dBi with an aperture efficiency of 61.9% at 12.7GHz and a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 25.8%.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-Based Method with RA-Net for Static IR Drop Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel machine learning-based method is proposed for fast and accurate prediction of the static IR drop of integrated circuits. A neural network called RA-Net, deriving from U-Net model, is applied for instance-level IR drop analysis. The ResBlock module and Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) are introduced in RA-Net, which improves the capability of feature extraction and leads to a better prediction. A new data preprocessing method is utilized to generate RA-Net inputs and enhance the predictive performance of small-sample designs. The numerical results demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed method.

articleTitle: An ultra-wideband high-isolation dual-port MIMO antenna design
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an antenna for ultra-wideband multiple-input and multiple-output (UWB-MIMO) is designed. The design comprises two hexagonal monopole antennas. In order to achieve ultra-wideband characteristics and mitigate the coupling, a stepped microstrip line structure for impedance matching and T-shaped defective ground structure are employed, which optimizes the broadband characteristics and achieves high isolation characteristics. The antenna achieves a wide impedance bandwidth of 3.5 GHz to 13.9 GHz (relative bandwidth of 119%). Furthermore, the isolation between the two feed ports of the antenna exceeds 18 dB, the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.012, and it exhibits favorable radiation characteristics.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Non-Conformal Volume Surface Integral Equation Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Traditional volume surface integral equation for analysis of metal-dielectric composites requires the target mesh to be conformal, which leads to over-meshing of the multi-scale model and reduces the solution efficiency. In order to deal with this problem, a non-conformal volume surface integral equation (VSIE) method based on the discontinuous Galerkin volume integral equation (DGVIE) and the grid-robust higher order vector basis (GRHOVB) surface integral equation is proposed in this paper to enhance the computing efficiency. In this method, the DGVIE is used to deal with dielectric target, which avoids the computation of higher-order singular integrals and facilitates the use of volume non-conformal meshing and mixed basis function discretization. The GRHOVB function is used to deal with PEC target, so that the surface mesh also does not need to be conformal. Numerical results verify the good performance of this non-conformal method.

articleTitle: An EM Optimization Method with Adjoint-Sensitivity-Based Multifeature Surrogate for the Design of Microwave Filters
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an efficient electromagnetic (EM) optimization method with adjoint-sensitivity-based multifeature surrogate for the design of microwave filters. This method is designed to solve the EM optimization problem where the starting point is far from the design specifications. Feature sensitivities are incorporated into the multifeatured surrogate modeling to achieve a surrogate with higher accuracy compared to the existing methods during the EM optimization process. A new design objective function in the feature space is also utilized to improve the speed of multifeature surrogate optimization. A microwave filter example is presented to illustrate this optimization method.

articleTitle: Application of Static Surface Current Modes in Electromagnetic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The application of static surface current modes in analyzing electromagnetic scatterings from perfect electrically conducting (PEC) targets is presented in this paper. Static surface current modes are able to solve the low-frequency collapse problem. In addition, static surface current modes are independent of the frequency and the material properties of the target, so static surface current modes can be flexibly used for the analysis of electromagnetic targets of the same shape and can effectively reduce the amount of computation. The numerical results verify the properties of static surface current modes as a basis function.

articleTitle: Ultrabroadband Metamaterial Absorber Based on Multilayer Resistive Film Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An ultrabroadband metamaterial absorber is proposed based on multilayer resistive film frequency selective surface (RFSS). Each dielectric-resistive film composite layer consists of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and a resistive film. Effective absorption is achieved through the multilayer RFSS, modeled as a series-connected RLC circuit. Experimental result shows that the absorber covers a -10 dB bandwidth of 1.07-11.84 GHz, with a fractional bandwidth of 166% and a thickness of 0.105 λL. It covers the L-, S-, C-, and X-bands, making it suitable for low-frequency applications such as satellite navigation and communications.

articleTitle: Simulation Research on Neutral Point Voltage Balance Control Strategy of Three-level Frequency Conversion System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: For the participation of the neutral point potential of the three-level inverter in energy transmission, it will bring the problem of inconsistent voltages of the two voltage-dividing capacitors. In this paper, changing the action time of the small vectors can control the neutral point voltage without changing the output voltage, that is, detecting the voltage magnitude of the DC side capacitors, and then, according to the deviation direction of the neutral point voltage, reasonably arranging the action time of the positive and negative small vector PWM pulses for neutral point voltage compensation. Through modeling and simulation analysis, the results show that this control method can maintain the neutral point voltage balance without going through complex logical judgments.

articleTitle: Integrated CMOS RF Receiver with Antenna and Experimental for DTV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The proposed CMOS integrated circuit design, intended for use in 40~900 MHz broadband radio frequency front-end receiver, has been implemented in tsmc 0.18um CMOS technique. The DTV RF frontend receiver design consists of the broadband differential low noise amplifier, double balance mixer with balun, LC tank voltage-controlled oscillator, ladder SC lowpass filter and patch antenna.

articleTitle: A Single-Ended to Balanced Two-Section Branch Line Coupler Based on Integrated Substrate Gap Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A single-ended to balanced two-section (SETB) branch line coupler based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW) is presented in this paper. Its center frequency is 27GHz. Compared with the traditional branch coupler, the coupler enhances the bandwidth by using twosection branch-line coupler circuit structure. The coupler can not only be used in 5G millimeter wave communication systems, but also can be used to connect single-ended systems and balanced systems directly. The simulation results show that the relative bandwidth of the coupler is 38%, impedance matching, port isolation, and common mode (CM) conversion suppression are also obtained well for it.

articleTitle: A Triple-Band Shared Aperture Antenna Array Based on current-Cancellation structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A Triple-band shared aperture antenna array is proposed, composed of low-band (LB: 0.69-0.86 GHz) antenna, high-band 1 and 2(HB1 and HB2: 3.3-3.6 GHz, 4.7-5 GHz) arrays, located on both sides of LB antenna. To suppress the blockage effects of LB antenna, composite split-slot resonators are etched on the radiating arms of LB antenna, which offsets the induced current and restores the deteriorated radiation patterns. Finally, the proposed array achieves satisfactory radiation performance.

articleTitle: Tunable Electromagnetic Optical Transmission Based on Graphene
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electromagnetic optical transmission (EOT) is different from the traditional frequency selective surface working mechanism. It refers to the phenomenon of enhancing electromagnetic wave transmission through subwavelength hole metal plates by designing subwavelength resonant units or periodic arrays. This paper designs a composite structure based on an SRR and a subwavelength perforated metal plate, which couples the two to achieve electromagnetic supertransmission behavior at 4.668 GHz. The transmittance is increased by more than 130 times compared to subwavelength metal holes.

articleTitle: A Novel Electromagnetic Environment Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The electromagnetic environment in the outer space is highly complex, and it is difficult to obtain high-resolution radiation distribution data. An electromagnetic signal monitoring system is designed for electromagnetic monitoring and sampling of outdoor large space sites. The system consists of an aerial signal acquisition platform based on UAV and a ground signal transmission device. Adaptive sampling method is utilized to improve the signal acquisition efficiency, real test experiments is provided to assess the potentialities and features of the proposed monitoring system.

articleTitle: A 9-10 GHz High-Efficiency GaN HEMT High Power Amplifier MMIC
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a 9-10 GHz high-efficiency, and high-gain three-stage high power amplifier (HPA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) based on 0.25-µm gallium nitride (GaN) high-electron mobility transistor (HEMT) process. The input and output impedances of the MMIC are both designed to match 50 ohms. Post EM simulation results show that this MMIC achieves a gain of more than 30 dB over the operating bandwidth, saturated output power P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">out</inf> better than 30 W, and a drain efficiency greater than 50%. The HPA MMIC layout measures 5 mm × 5 mm.

articleTitle: Time-domain Responses of The Array Antenna Under External High-power EMP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The transient responses of a rectangular microstrip array antenna in the complex wireless electrical system under the impact of an external high-power electromagnetic pulse (EMP) are studied in this paper. The time-frequency coupling characteristics of rectangular microstrip array antennas in radar systems were studied under Gaussian electromagnetic pulse(G EMP), high altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP), high-power microwave (HPM), and ultra-wideband (UWB) pulse, by using the finite integration technique (FIT) method. The induced time-domain voltages characteristics of the antenna illuminated by different EMPs are presented and compared in detail. These simulated results can used to further evaluating electromagnetic environment destroy effects and electromagnetic protection of some complex radar systems.

articleTitle: Sheet Beam Electron Optical System using Periodic Cusped Magnets for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The success of terahertz vacuum electron devices requires efficient generation and transport of high current density electron beams. An electron optical system consisting of a sheet electron beam gun and periodic cusped magnets is proposed to efficiently generate and transport a sheet electron beam for terahertz applications. The system consists of an electron gun and dual-layer magnet blocks aligned with pole pieces. This design not only produces a higher magnetic field in the axial direction but also allows for easier adjustment of the magnetic field in the transverse direction. This focusing system is used to transport a 21.7 kV, 50 mA sheet electron beam with a cross-section of 0.24 mm × 0.08 mm through a 50 mm long tunnel with dimensions of 0.32 mm × 0.12 mm. The current density of the beam exceeds 260 Acm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>. The focusing system is designed to produce an axial magnetic field B<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">z</inf> of 0.2 T. CST Particle Studio is used to model the sheet electron beam gun and the periodic cusped magnet system. The obtained results show a beam transmission efficiency of 100%.

articleTitle: A Frequency Selective Rasorber Utilizing Multi-Parallel Resonator Structures for Wideband Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we designed a dual-polarized frequency-selective rasorber (FSR) that has a second-order passbands with low insertion loss. Combined with a triple-layer bandpass frequency-selective surfaces (FSS). The -3 dB transmission band of the designed FSR ranges from 11.47 GHz to 20 GHz, with an 80% absorption bandwidth from 3.25 GHz to 10.38 GHz, indicating promising applications in radar stealth technology.

articleTitle: A FSS Inverse Design Method Based on Output Space Mapping Enhanced ECM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes an inverse design method for frequency selective surfaces (FSS) based on an equivalent circuit model (ECM) and output space mapping (OSM) technique. The method establishes an OSM enhanced ECM model (forward model) to replace expensive electromagnetic (EM) simulations for FSS shielding effectiveness (SE) evaluation. Furthermore, an inverse model is proposed to predict FSS unit cell structure parameter values using specification-driven feature point sampling method. Experiment results demonstrate that FSS designs with shielding frequency between 2-18GHz can be efficiently predicted and verified by EM simulation.

articleTitle: Calculation of Inverse Square Root of RWG Gram Matrix Based on Chebyshev Polynomial Expansion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The boundary element method usually relies on surface integral equations (SIEs) for the analysis of electromagnetic scattering problems. However, using traditional discretizations for SIEs, the spectrum of boundary element matrices can not represent that of the corresponding surface integral operators, which introduces issues for methods utilizing the spectral properties. To solve this problem, one can use inverse square roots of Gram matrices for SIEs to disclose the spectrum of the surface integral operators. In this work, we designate an algorithm for the calculation of the inverse square root of the Gram matrix associated with the Rao-Wilton-Glisson discretization, which is based on the Chebyshev polynomial expansion of the inverse square root scalar function. Numerical results are provided to demonstrate the efficiency of the scheme.

articleTitle: Radio Propagation Prediction based on Reported Data in Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article proposes a method for predicting radio propagation loss based on parameters such as longitude, latitude, and reference signal strength in mobile communication terminal reported information. Firstly, the applicability of the reported parameters data was validated through frequency sweep measurements in network coverage for typical urban scenarios with a 4G mobile communication band. Then, using a portion of extracted data as input, the parameters of the Standard Propagation Model (SPM) are adjusted through data training to achieve propagation loss prediction for multi cell scenarios in urban areas. Finally, the accuracy of the prediction results is verified through the remaining extracted data from the reported information.

articleTitle: A Wideband Wide-Angle Scanning Circularly Polarized Microstrip Antenna based on metasurface for Ka-band communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A ka-band wideband wide-angle scanning circularly polarized (CP) microstrip antenna base on metasurface is proposed. The proposed antenna achieves CP by introducing rectangular notch on radiating ring structure. The antenna elements are formed into 2×2 subarray in the form of sequential rotation. The sparse optimization of 320-element in the form of 2×2 subarray is carried out by genetic algorithm, which achieves ±55° wide-angle scanning without grating lobe and the array layout sparsity is 60%. The simulation results of element show that the impedance bandwidth (IBW) for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| <- 10 dB covers 24.86-31.54 GHz and the 3dB axial ratio bandwidth (ARBW) covers 28.32-29.84 GHz. The simulation results of 2×2 subarray show that the IBW for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| <-10 dB covers 25.74-31.96 GHz and the 3dB ARBW covers 27.02-31.97 GHz. The proposed wideband wide-angle scanning CP antenna array would be a very attractive candidate for satellite communication.

articleTitle: A novel method for quickly and accurately predicting the scattering response of coated target
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel method for efficiently and accurately predicting the scattering response of coated targets is proposed. By using the scattering center model based on the geometrical theory of diffraction (GTD) as the transfer function, the scattering characteristics of coated targets could be predicted from those of PEC targets. First, a scattering center parameters extraction algorithm based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) is designed to obtain the scattering characteristics of PEC targets. Then, the reflection coefficient is calculated based on the electromagnetic parameters and thickness of the material, and the scattering response of coated targets is predicted by combining it with the scattering center model. Through analysis, the mean absolute error (MAE) of the proposed method for cube and the Slicy targets is 1.96% and 4.1% respectively. Furthermore, the proposed method saves 90% to 98% of the simulation time compared to the calculation time of commercial solver. The results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively enables accurate and rapid prediction of the scattering response of coated targets.

articleTitle: A method for calculating electromagnetic scattering of complex targets using sparsely sampled current
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electromagnetic calculation is the main way to obtain electromagnetic scattering data of radar targets, but it is affected by computer performance and electromagnetic algorithms. Especially for electrically large targets, the calculation complexity is high. Therefore, it is necessary to optimize the calculation algorithm and improve calculation efficiency. This paper studies the distribution characteristics of complex target surface currents and proposes sparse sampling of target surface currents to obtain data. This sparse sampling method can not only effectively capture the target surface current distribution characteristics, but also achieve electromagnetic calculations of complex targets by interpolating the data with high calculation accuracy. This method reduces the cost and complexity of data collection, improves calculation efficiency, and is suitable for electromagnetic computing, radar imaging and other fields.

articleTitle: Research on UWB electromagnetic pulse signal generation method based on optical frequency comb
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the integration of electronic information equipment, the electromagnetic sensitivity and electromagnetic compatibility of complex models cannot be ignored. Electromagnetic radiation produces a great threat to the normal operation and protection of each equipment. The key challenge in testing electromagnetic radiation sensitivity lies in the necessity of an ultra-broadband signal source to provoke the electromagnetic radiation-sensitive response of the complex space. Due to the number of electronic devices work in a large frequency band, the bandwidth of the signal source for excitation of radiation sensitivity is at least DC ~ 20GHz. This paper proposes an ultra-broadband(UWB) signal generation method based on optical frequency comb, aiming to modulate the existing broadband signals with a comb carrier signal. The cascaded MZM-based optical comb generation method produces optical combs with adjustable comb spacing. It can be used to generate UWB electromagnetic pulse signals from DC to 20 GHz. The generation method has a simple idea, a simple comb shaped carrier signal generation structure, and is flexible and tunable. This makes the bandwidth of the UWB signal generated by this method highly scalable and adjustable according to actual needs.

articleTitle: High Performance 3D Integrated Common-Mode Noise Suppression Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a three-dimensional (3D) common mode (CM) noise suppression filter based on through-silicon via (TSV) technology is proposed. The Chebyshev low-pass filter is used to equate the signal transmission channels. The inductors are realized by TSV technology and the proposed common-mode noise suppression filter is verified by HFSS software. The results demonstrate that the filter is capable of suppressing common-mode noise more than 10dB across the frequency range of 3.3GHz to 11.8GHz, with a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 112.6%. Meanwhile, the differential signal insertion loss is kept less than 3dB and the bandwidth reaches 17.8GHz. In addition, the size of the common-mode noise suppression filter is only 250×430μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (0.0063× 0.011 λg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>).

articleTitle: Wideband Directional Coupler Using 3D Copper Additive Manufacturing Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband directional coupler is designed using three-dimensional (3D) additive manufacturing technology. To solve the mismatch issue of the odd-even mode impedance at high frequencies, a compensate method is proposed to make up the electrical length and the odd-even mode impedance for a flat coupling response over wide frequency range. For demonstration, a 5.1-34.8 GHz directional coupler is designed using a nine-layer additive manufacturing technology. The coupling degree is 20.8±1.4dB, the directivity is better than 15dB in the working band, and the insertion loss is as low as 0.3dB.

articleTitle: Electrothermal Effects on Hot-Carrier Reliability of FinFETs in Ring Oscillators Based on Equivalent Thermal Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This study presents a computational analysis of electrothermal effects on hot-carrier injection (HCI) in FinFETs within a ring oscillator (RO) using an equivalent thermal model and circuit simulation. Based on transient temperature response of the 3D structure of the RO calculated by finite element method (FEM), the thermal model can be extracted. Then, combining thermal model with power obtained in a SPICE simulator, the transient temperature of the FinFETs in RO can be calculated quickly and accurately. With the transient temperature and voltage stress, the HCI induced threshold voltage drift (TVS) of FinFETs can be predicted successfully and the effect of the operating voltage of the RO on the electrothermal response and HCI of FinFET are also investigated.

articleTitle: Adaptive HODBF-Based Direct Surface Integral Equation Solver for Electromagnetic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An adaptive hierarchically off-diagonal butterfly direct solver (A-HODBF) is proposed for fast and accurate solution of three-dimensional surface integral equations (SIE). The novel generalized admissibility condition (GAC) is put forward to enable refined control of the butterfly rank (BF-rank) during matrix filling and inversion phases. Numerical results show that the proposed method has a reduced complexity compared to hierarchically off-diagonal low-rank-based Matrix solver (HODLR) and has optimized leading coefficients compared to traditional BF methods, providing a scalable solution for large-scale electromagnetic problems.

articleTitle: Holographic Imaging Technology Based on Dual-polarization Programmable Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The utilizations of dual-polarization programmable metasurfaces in holographic imaging technology offer solutions to overcome the challenges in traditional holographic imaging techniques. Specifically, the conventional holographic imaging method usually suffers from suboptimal image quality and large structural footprint. The presented method in this work can address these problems and thus enable multi-channel dynamic imaging functionality. In this paper, a 1-bit dual-polarization programmable metasurface is utilized to address imaging objectives separately in the x and y polarizations, and the phase inversion algorithm is also used to obtain the phase distribution of the metasurface. Subsequently, simulation of polarization multiplexing holographic imaging with this dual-polarization programmable metasurface is implemented and verified. Simulation results demonstrate that the imaging outcomes of the metasurface are consistent with theoretical calculations, exhibiting stable performance across a wide bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Polarized Wideband Patch Antenna Array with Enhanced Isolation for Integrated Sensing and Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact dual-polarized wideband patch antenna array with isolation improvement is proposed for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) at the ISM band. The decoupling technique is proposed and evolved to suppress the elements mutual coupling and self-interference of a 2×2 patch antenna array under the extremely closely edge-to-edge distance of 0.019 λ0. A prototype of this antenna is simulated, fabricated, and measured to validate the feasibility of the proposed design scheme. The measured results show that both the poor isolation between the Rx/Rx elements and self-interference between the Tx/Rx ports have been improved to better than 15 dB within a wide-matched bandwidth of 10.5%, indicating the proposed scheme is promising for wideband ISAC applications.

articleTitle: Design of 6GHz~18GHz broadband power amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of wide bandwidth, miniaturization and good heat dissipation of electronic equipment, a 6GHz-18GHz broadband power amplifier is developed. To solve the problem of low efficiency of temperature test for SIP products, select the temperature change module to open the sealed heat preservation cavity to realize local temperature control and avoid affecting the running accuracy of the device. The automatic manipulator and high-precision visual recognition system are selected, and the adjustable automatic rotating tray is adopted to realize the automatic temperature test of SIP products. Finally, assist data processing program, automatically generate test report. Finally, the temperature automatic test and sorting system is developed, which is unattended for 24 hours and increased the test efficiency by 350%.

articleTitle: An Improved Phaseless Pattern Reconstruction Method in Imperfect Reverberation Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This work presents an improved antenna pattern reconstruction method in reverberation chamber using phaseless near-field data. The proposed method firstly introduces the way of calculating radiation pattern in reverberation chamber without phase information. Then, the optimization for finding the invertible solution of the objective matrix when using the generalized pseudoinverse matrix to derive the targeted antenna pattern is analyzed in detail. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively improve the reconstruction accuracy of the antenna radiation pattern obtained in reverberation chamber with phaseless near-field measurement.

articleTitle: Photonics-Assisted Interpulse modulation for LFM radar Jamming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article proposes a novel radar interference system based on microwave photons (MPW), which has ultra wideband performance and combines miniaturization and integration. The system structure consists of an RF receiver, transmitter, and microwave photon modulation module. By dynamically changing the DC bias voltage of MZM to modulate the operating point, phase modulation can be achieved in ultra wideband. Subsequently, its feasibility was verified through simulation. From the analysis of the results, system hides real targets and generates fake targets with high peak values, demonstrating good interference performance.

articleTitle: Near-field Scattering Center Modeling based on Complex Target Structure and TFR Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The method proposed in this paper extracts the location information of the scattering center (SC) through in-depth analysis of the structure of the near-field target; it determines the amplitude information of the scattering center based on time-frequency feature, and models the near-field scattering center based on the high-frequency analytical expression of the near-field scattering feature.Taking a certain type of missile target as an example, the accuracy of this method was verified by comparing with the results of multilevel fast multipole algorithm(PMLFMA). The modeling method in this article can provide certain reference significance for research in the fields of radar target identification, tracking and positioning.

articleTitle: Research on the method of active cancellation stealth with broadband and wide-angle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a method for broadband and wideangle active cancellation stealth is proposed to address the issue of radar angle measurement errors. The method involves utilizing a phase shifter and an amplifier connected to the antenna in order to control the re-radiation field of the antenna and cancel out the scattering field of the target. Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is employed to calculate the values of phase shifters and amplifiers. The effectiveness of this method in achieving broadband and wide-angle active cancellation is confirmed through two monostatic simulation cases. Specifically, when using a flat plate as a case, it is demonstrated that the reduction in radar cross section (RCS) exceeds 10dB with a frequency width greater than 35MHz and an angle width greater than 15°. In the case of a missile, similar results are achieved with RCS reducing by 10dB when the frequency width exceeds 32MHz and the angle width exceeds 5°.

articleTitle: Antenna decoupling based on manipulating reflection phase
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna decoupling method based on controlling the reflection phase is proposed in this communication. This MIMO antenna mainly consists of a wideband stacked patch antenna array at the bottom and a meta-surface at the upper layer and there is an approximately circular metal patch array on the meta-surface. In this paper, the decoupling of MIMO antenna array is realized by changing the arrangement of the upper patches through a random algorithm based on checkerboard arrangement (CARA), and it is proved by theory and simulation.

articleTitle: Broadband Beam Scanning Array Antenna in 4G/5G/Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The manuscript presents a Rotman lens as a beamforming network for feeding antenna arrays in applications such as satellite communication systems, collision avoidance radar, and ultra-wideband communication systems. The array port connects to the Vivaldi antenna via an SMA connector, forming an array antenna with beam-scanning capabilities. Experimental results show that the designed lens enables beam scanning with a width of ±30°, achieving a maximum antenna gain of 12 dBi. The design results correlate closely with the experimental data, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Single-Sideband Time Modulator with Extremely High Modulation Frequency in 130-nm CMOS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A single-sideband time modulator (SSBTM) with extremely high modulation frequency is presented, which realize a clean output spectrum within ± 1st-order sidebands. The proposed SSBTM uses active switches and high-pass filters in the mixing stage to significantly increase modulation frequency. Meanwhile, it uses particular-sized RF cells in the mixing stage to achieve impedance-invariant in status switching. The proposed SSBTM is designed in 130-nm CMOS process. The simulated result shows it achieves a modulation frequency up to 1 GHz, and unwanted sidebands harmonic components have been completely suppressed. The power consumption is 36 mW from a 1.2 V supply.

articleTitle: Phase Reconfigurable Surface Designed for Microwave Imaging Based on Random Field irradiation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In recent years, the imaging technology based on compressed sensing has received widespread attention. The key of compressed sensing imaging is sparse sampling, which is inseparable from the construction of random radiation field. Random irradiated aperture antennas capable of constructing random radiation fields are particularly important. This paper revealed the theory and design of a phase reconfigurable surface, which enabled the continuously tunability of the transmission phase between 0° and 180°. The phase reconfigurable surface is comprising the periodic arrangement of identical phase reconfigurable units. By randomly modulating the transmission phase of each unit, an antenna array with a random radiation aperture can be realized. The proposed random beam aperture antenna array is expected to be used in fields of microwave imaging, beamforming and other electromagnetic wave transmission.

articleTitle: SSPPs-based Low-pass Filter with Continuously Adjustable Cut-off Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a microwave filter with tunable cutoff frequency is proposed based on spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) structure. The adjustable filter is proposed by adding metal branches controlled by varactors which can be changed through different bias. The simulated results show that the filter has different dispersion characteristics and exhibits low-pass bands with different cut-off frequencies. The proposed active adjustable filter is expected to play a potential role in modern communication system.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Conformal Transmitarray and Its Beam Scanning Property
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces an ultra-thin transmitarray composed of unit cell elements with three layers of identical square ring slots. The structure is characterized by a minimal thickness of 0.508 mm, which is equivalent to 0.04λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> at 25 GHz in free space. The design procedure for specific phase values of the element is developed. By integrating this element into a conformal radiating array, a peak gain of 20.9 dBi is achieved through simulation. Furthermore, the fixed beam conformal transmitarray is expanded to a beam scanning transmitarray. By moving the feedhorn to various positions along the Y-axis, the main beam of the conformal transmitarray can be adjusted within an angle range of ±24°.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction by Via-Loaded Notches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A phased array element based on the concept of antenna-as-package is proposed. The mutual coupling between antenna elements is analyzed. By introducing a via fence, a dielectric superstrate, and via-loaded notches, the sum mutual coupling is reduced through suppression and counteraction. As a result, the scan blindness is eliminated. Meanwhile, the effective bandwidth and cross-polarization suppression of the antenna while scanning are improved by 30% and 12 dB, respectively.

articleTitle: Wide-angle transmitarray metasurface retroreflector
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Due to its important academic values and widespread applications in civil and military domains, metasurface-assisted wide-angle planar retro-reflectors have received much attentions across from optics to microwave band recently. Compared to conventional retro-reflectors such as corner reflectors or Luneburg lens reflectors, metasurface reflector have many advantages such as low-profile, easy fabrications, conformal design and versatile backscattering enhancement control, etc. However, it is a great challenge to design a wide-angle metasurface retro-reflector which can outperform traditional ones with a reduced device thickness. Inspired by recent progresses on high-efficiency transmit-array antenna-assisted flat retro-reflectors, we here provide a complete performance comparison between this kind of four-layer metasurface-assisted retroreflector and conventional reflectors (corner reflectors and Luneburg lens reflectors) in terms of RCS backscattering level and working angular range for the same effective area and operation frequency. According to our measurement results, the 3dB RCS working angular range of metasurface retroreflector is between corner reflector and Luneburg lens reflector while the peak RCS value in the middle is much lower than these traditional retro-reflectors. The reason for this degraded RCS level is also discussed and analyzed. This work is meaningful to judge the device quality of metasurface-based retroreflectors compared to conventional ones and can provide a deep understanding of its working mechanism of this kind of flat retro-reflectors.

articleTitle: Research on 2D Honeycomb Layout Based on Binary Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a two-dimensional honeycomb absorbing structure layout method based on binary particle swarm optimization (BPSO) algorithm is proposed. Firstly, the two-dimensional honeycomb is modeled, and its scattering is calculated by combining the two-dimensional moment method. Finally, the binary particle swarm optimization algorithm is used to optimize it. By adopting this method, the monostatic RCS (Radar Cross Section) of the final optimized cellular layout of the two schemes is reduced by 9.01dB and 10.88dB respectively compared with that of the initial layout. After optimization, the peak of RCS has been obvious improved. The results show that this optimization method has certain application value in the research of honeycomb absorbing materials.

articleTitle: Adaptive Sparse Data Acquisition Technique Based on query-by-committee (QBC) and Sequential Spatial Adaptive Sampling(SSAS)
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an optimization method based on sequence space adaptive sampling (SSAS) and query by committee (QBC) is proposed to accelerate the near-field scanning of Integrated circuit, gradually reduce the sampling interval, and significantly reduce the number of scanned data samples. This method uses the query sub-committee method to collect data at high uncertainty locations. Combined with the SSAS algorithm, the sampling points with high uncertainty can be selected in batches, avoiding the repeated calculation of the sampling points with low uncertainty. The effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by numerical calculation and measurement results.

articleTitle: The incident microwave power measurement in particle accelerator microwave systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In high-reflection microwave power measurements with load impedance mismatch, the limited directivity of directional couplers introduces interference from reverse signals, affecting the accuracy of incident microwave power measurement. To address this issue, this paper presents a method that utilizes auxiliary circuits to adjust the amplitude and phase of the output signals from two directional couplers with lower directivity, combining them to cancel out the interference signal components. This microwave measurement method was validated on a 162.5 MHz high-power microwave experimental platform. The directivity of the new directional coupler measurement system, constructed using two directional couplers with directivities of 19.1 dB and 20.3 dB, reached 47.8 dB.

articleTitle: FPGA Implementation of Control Unit for 3D Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, an FPGA-based control unit for 3D ground penetrating radar (GPR) is proposed. The system composed of FPGA, programmable delay chip (PDC), clock buffer and so on. The control unit adjusts the acquisition parameters according to the commands issued by PC and then trigger the pulse generators and receivers. Equivalent time sampling method is used for this system with an equivalent sampling rate of up to 33.3 GSPS. The control unit support 9 Tx antennas and 8 Rx antennas with up to 16 channels. Experimental results show that the proposed control unit can correctly schedule the timing between the transmitters and receivers, and it can transfer received data to PC via Ethernet, demonstrating the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Simulation of dual-frequency dielectric barrier discharge at atmospheric pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To understand the mechanism of plasma discharge in argon dual-frequency (DF) dielectric barrier discharge (DBD), a two-dimensional symmetric fluid model is established and numerically simulated by the finite element method. The low-frequency excitation source is 500kHz, and the amplitude is fixed at 750V cosine voltage. The RF frequency is 100MHz sinusoidal voltage. The discharge characteristics of plasma under different RF voltages are discussed. At U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RF</inf>=0V, the LF discharge current contains two peaks in each LF cycle, while at DF discharge (U<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">RF</inf> > 0V), the current is a superposition of the LF and RF components. With the increase of the RF voltage amplitude, the electric field and electron density in the discharge gap are more widely distributed, the plasma density increases, and the plasma discharge in the reactor is more uniform. This study contributes to a more specific understanding of the behavior of plasma in DF-DBD reactors.

articleTitle: A SIR dual-band microstrip filter loaded with shaped branches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a SIR-coupled dual-band bandpass filter is proposed, which has lower insertion loss, better out-of-band rejection. The bandpass characteristics of the dual-band are obtained by bending the SIR and coupling it, and loading the shaped branches. By changing the shape of the shaped branches, a transmission pole is added in the first passband, which reduces the insertion loss of the filter and improves the rejection effect of the stopband. The simulation results show that the dual-frequency bandpass filter has a center frequency of 6.26GHz, an insertion loss of 0.17dB, a return loss of less than -27.8dB, and a relative bandwidth of 15.5% for the low band, and an insertion loss of 0.67dB, a return loss of less than -15.8dB, and a relative bandwidth of 11.6% for the high band, at a center frequency of 9.26GHz.

articleTitle: Simulation of ISAR Image Based on the Deep Learning and the Electromagnetic Scattering Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The Inverse Synthetic Aperture Radar (ISAR) image inversion is of great significance in the fields of Earth observation, ocean monitoring and target recognition. However, traditional ISAR imaging algorithms are difficult to meet the requirements of fast imaging due to high computational cost. In order to solve this problem, in this paper, the electromagnetic scattering mechanism and deep learning technology are combined to improve the imaging speed of ISAR and save the computational cost. And the results have been compared with those obtained by the Back Projection (BP) algorithm to show the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed DL-based ISAR imaging method improves the imaging speed with the same imaging quality.

articleTitle: Active frequency selective surface with multiple switchable functions and angular stability
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An active frequency selective surface (AFSS) with multiple switchable functions and angular stability is proposed, which can achieve absorption, reflection, and transmission functions through PIN diodes and resistors. The design consists of three layers, including the first layer consisting of an absorption and transmission reconfigurable surface with a circular ring structure, the middle air layer, and the last layer consisting of a transmission and reflection reconfigurable surface with interdigital resonator. In comparison to previously reported AFSS, the proposed surface offers three different working modes and achieves broadband properties and wide-angle stability.

articleTitle: A Broadband Wide-Angle Frequency-Selective Surface with High Selectivity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A broadband wide-angle frequency-selective surface (FSS) with high selectivity is presented in this paper. The proposed FSS structure achieves considerable bandwidth and high selectivity performance by cascading multiple FSS layers and loading lumped inductors. The simulation results show that the operating frequency band of the proposed FSS structure is 4.6513.19 GHz (95.7%) and the rectangle coefficient (RC) value is 0.84 at normal incidence. When the incident angle changes from 0° to 50°, the transmission bandwidth and RC value remain stable.

articleTitle: The Simulation of Radio Wave Propagation in Single/Multi-Knife-Edge Scenario with Two-Way Parabolic Equation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, we deduces the expression the Two-Way Parabolic Equation method(2WPE). First, in the single-knife-edge scenario, the 2WPE method is used to solve the radio wave propagation problem. The numerical results obtained using the 2WPE were analyzed and compared with those from the One-Way Parabolic Equation method(1WPE). Furthermore, the results were compared and analyzed with the physical mechanism of radio wave propagation. It confirms the correctness of the 2WPE. In the multi-knife-edge scenario, the reflection of radio waves between adjacent peaks was considered. And the reasons for the differences in the propagation factor obtained from the 2WPE and the 1WPE were analyzed. By analyzing the differences of the electric field distribution at different transmitting antenna height, it was concluded that raising the height of the transmitting antenna appropriately can reduce the impact of uneven terrain and obstacles on the signal. The 2WPE can consider the backward propagation field of radio waves, providing more accurate predictions than the 1WPE.

articleTitle: Broadband MIMO Antenna with Defective Ground Structure for Mobile 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband MIMO antenna for 5G applications is proposed with four elements placed orthogonally. The specific dimension of the antenna is 70 × 70 × 2.5 mm3. S-shaped coupling unit are introduced between neighboring components and eight rectangular slots are etched on the ground plane to enhance isolation. Simulation results show that the -6 dB impedance bandwidth is 3.28-5.08 GHz, which is able to cover the N77/N78/N79 bands of 5G and suitable for 5G MIMO mobile devices. The designed four-element MIMO antenna has the advantages of low profile, small size and wide bandwidth, which provides a design idea for the 5G MIMO antenna on the back cover of mobile devices.

articleTitle: Scattering contribution of randomly distributed single tree species
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A complex scattering matrix containing phase information is proposed to establish the Mueller matrix, and then the scattering contribution of the forest vegetation model is solved. Due to the distortion of the signal phase due to the scattering effects of the crown and trunk, the interaction between the vegetation target and the surrounding environment is rarely considered. In this paper, the disk-like and spicule-like particle layer is used as the scattering radiation transmission model of the vegetation canopy, and the vertical thick cylinder is used as the scattering radiation transmission model of the trunk layer. Secondly, the projection mapping algorithm (MPA) is used to calculate the hierarchical vegetation model. This paper studies the scattering and attenuation of randomly distributed single tree target, and evaluates the rationality of using complex scattering matrix to calculate the scattering contribution of vegetation.

articleTitle: Micro Energy Harvesting for IoT Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A significant limitation of modern wireless IoT sensors is their battery life. We propose a small-scale radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting rectenna, paired with a low-power smart sensor that can be deployed in existing buildings without requiring additional sensor infrastructure. By capturing ambient energy in the 2.45 GHz range, the battery life of these low-power sensors can be extended.

articleTitle: Inverse design of cross-polarization conversion metasurfaces using convolutional neural networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to solve the inefficiency problem in the traditional manual design process of cross-polarization conversion metasurface, this paper proposes the optimization design method of cross-polarization conversion metasurface based on deep learning. First, a pseudo-ellipticity angle is proposed to characterize the cross-polarization conversion; second, combined with the coded metasurface, the inverse design of the cross-polarization conversion metasurface is realized based on the deep learning convolutional neural network (CNN) and the electromagnetic simulation software; and finally, a series of structural arrangements of the metasurface units are obtained. Through the demonstration example, a series of cross-polarization conversion metasurfaces are optimally designed, and these metasurfaces achieve narrow-band cross-polarization performance within 8-16 GHz, which verifies the feasibility of the inverse design method.

articleTitle: Modeling Heterogeneity with Flexible and Semantic Aligned Graph Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are particularly effective in machine learning tasks focused on graphs, notably in homophilous graphs where edges primarily connect nodes with identical labels. However, ensuring uniform outcomes in heterophilous graphs poses a challenge. Several studies have extended GNN architectures to address the unique characteristics of heterogeneous graphs. Nonetheless, these approaches often necessitate adaptability enhancement in managing feature combinations for both the central node and its neighboring nodes. To address this challenge, we introduce a Flexible and Semantic Aligned Graph Neural Network (FSAGCN). FSAGCN is based on two core principles. First, it independently encodes information from the central node and its neighbors, combining them to produce a fused output. Second, it aggregates nodes of the same class, aligning them with semantic information from both the feature and neighbor perspectives to impose constraints on the conversion of central nodes and neighbors during the propagation of the graph structure. We conducted comprehensive experiments with eight real-world datasets, demonstrating that FSAGCN outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baseline models.

articleTitle: Antenna Teaching Method From Life to Theory Based on The Multi-Mode Concept
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Antenna principle is an important and basic course for ECE student. Its theory is complex with a set of equations. The traditional teaching method often focuses on theory teaching and formula derivation, lacking intuitive and dynamic display, which makes them difficult for these students to understand the complex antenna principle. Therefore, how to stimulate interest and curiosity in learning and effectively for the students is an important exploration direction of the teaching reform of this course, while improving their autonomous ability with the method to solve practical problems. Therefore, electromagnetic simulation software HFSS is introduced into the teaching of antenna principle course based on the multi-mode. With the help of the intuitive interface and powerful functions, the theoretical concepts are displayed in the actual life, which not only enables students to deeply understand the relevant concepts, but also improves the enthusiasm for the students, so as to effectively enhance the teaching effect.

articleTitle: Dispersion data fitting based on Levenberg-Marquardt data fitting method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article proposes a fitting method for three typical dispersion models. The method is based on the Levenberg-Marquardt (LM) algorithm, which is a mainstream nonlinear least squares method that provides good fitting accuracy and robustness. The dispersion model fitting method proposed in this article fits and solves key parameters for three typical dispersion models: Debye, Drude, and Lorentz models. The simulation results show that the method has good fitting effects for the three typical dispersion models.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Susceptibility Analysis of Basic Communication Functions in Network System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: As a typical wired network system, Ethernet is susceptible to external field interference caused by cable coupling, which can disrupt data transmission and significantly affect communication efficiency and quality. This paper investigates the effects of cable-induced conductive susceptibility. Basic signals are utilized as interference signals, and the Bulk Current Injection (BCI) method is applied for conductive susceptibility testing. The findings indicate that the system's susceptibility behavior is independent of time and bandwidth. Moreover, the system exhibits heightened vulnerability within the high-frequency range from 25 MHz to 255 MHz. Regarding protective measures, it was found that using shielded twisted pairs did not enhance the system's resistance to interference. Consequently, special attention needs to be given to electromagnetic protection measures.

articleTitle: The Influence of Self-Electromagnetic Interference on Shielding effectiveness Measurement and Countermeasure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the process of shielding effectiveness measurement, different levels of electromagnetic interference were found in different frequency bands. Preliminary analysis attributed this interference to the electronic devices within the automated testing system. Following GJB 151B-2013, the electromagnetic radiation characteristics of the interference source were measured in the 30 MHz-6 GHz frequency range. The frequency bands of the electromagnetic radiation in the measurement results matched those of the electromagnetic interference in the shielding effectiveness measurement. To address this electromagnetic interference, a portable shielding tent was further used to shield and suppress the electronic devices in the system. Radiation characteristic measurements were conducted on the shielding effectiveness measurement system after shielding, and no significant electromagnetic radiation was found, successfully suppressing the electromagnetic radiation from the electronic devices.
