Finally, an analysis of the shielding effectiveness measurement results before and after shielding showed that the measurement system regained the accuracy of the shielding effectiveness measurement results after shielding.

articleTitle: Design of a Bandpass Frequency-selective Metasurface Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we designed a frequency selection surface with bandpass characteristics, which is suitable for antenna filtering and stealth function in space. The designed frequency selective absorber (FSA) structure consists of upper and lower layers, both of which can realize nearly transparent wave-transparent band in antenna operating band 12 GHz, and the lower layer of frequency selective surface (FSS) is designed to realize reflections in the surrounding band, so that the incident wave will be secondary absorbed by the upper FSA after reflections. After reflection, the energy of the incident wave will be absorbed by the upper FSA. The designed bandpass frequency selective surface at 11.57GHz-13.50GHz can realize the normal radiation of the applicable antenna in the working band, and the frequency selective absorber (FSA) can realize the absorption of the incident electromagnetic wave of two polarizations outside the antenna’s working band (5.01GHz-10.74GHz and 15.25GHz-16.76GHz) to achieve the single-site and dual-site operation outside the working band of the antenna. single-site and dual-site RCS reduction outside the operating band. For working antennas applying this type of super-surface, the gain of the antenna is not affected because the radiated wave energy is not reflected or absorbed by the designed super-surface.

articleTitle: Triple-mode Filtering Patch Antenna with High Selectivity by Loading Symmetric Slots
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a triple-mode filtering patch antenna with high selectivity is proposed. The patch serves as a radiator that only loads two pairs of symmetrical slots without extra elements. On the one hand, these slots reduce the frequencies of high-order modes TM02 and TM12 modes together with TM10 mode to form the operating band to increase the bandwidth. On the other hand, these slots excite two radiation nulls near the passband due to radiation cancellation caused by the surface current, thus improving the out-of-band selectivity. Finally, a filtering patch antenna is designed and simulated. The simulated results indicate that the filtering antenna operates at 3.5GHz with a fractional bandwidth of 7.14%. Two radiation nulls are located at 3.1GHz and 4.0GHz, resulting in a high selectivity.

articleTitle: Broadband RCS Reduction Based on Coding Metasurface with Independent Control of Amplitude and Phase
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a coding metasurface with independent control of amplitude and phase is developed for broadband radar cross section (RCS) Reduction. First, we designed a metasurface unit consisting of a modified concentric circular ring and a square ring resonator. The reflection phase and amplitude are determined by the size of the circular ring and the loading resistance value, respectively. Furthermore, designed coding metasurface can manipulate electromagnetic (EM) waves by encoding "0" and "1" elements. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed coding metasurface can achieve effective RCS reduction in the frequency range of 4GHz- 22GHz, and the reduction value depends on the value of loading resistance.

articleTitle: Error Estimation and h-adaptive MoM for Modeling Metallic-dielectric Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: We present a combined recovery error estimator for the composite metallic-dielectric structure using the RWG-based method of moments (MoM) in the electric field integral equation Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (EFIE-PMCHW) formulation. An h-adaptive scheme in conjunction with the recovery estimator is given to verify the effectiveness of the method. Results for a microstrip antenna show that the proposed method is flexible and efficient.

articleTitle: Research on the amplitude limiting characteristics of Ultra-Wideband Energy Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article proposes an ultra-wideband energy selective surface (ESS) model consisting of three layers loaded diodes with different metal structure, in which cross-metal strips and metal gate loaded diodes are used to achieve dual polarization protection. The three-layer ESS uses the switching characteristics of diodes to realize adaptive protection against high-power microwaves (HPM). When a low-power microwave is incident, the diode is turned off, and the electromagnetic (EM) wave passes through with less insertion loss. When high-power microwave is incident, the diode is in the on-state, shielding HPM to achieve protection. The simulation results show that the ESS can obtain insertion loss (IL) less than 1dB and shielding efficiency (SE) greater than 27dB at 7.84GHz-23.01GHz, which can realize efficient protection against high-power microwaves.

articleTitle: Application of Asymmetric Window Function in Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave Ground Penetrating Radar
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Stepped Frequency Continuous Wave (SFCW) Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) is a frequency domain radar system based on a waveform consisting of a series of sinusoids of increasing frequency. In this paper, the effect of windows is investigated on detection and imaging. An asymmetric window technique is proposed, which amplifies high-frequency signals while suppressing unexpected components. The result shows the capability to provide high-resolution imaging and potentially solve the resolution/penetration trade-off inherent in pulse-based ground penetrating radar.

articleTitle: An Improved SBR Method for Calculating Electromagnetic Scattering of Multi-layered Coated Media
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an improved approach that utilizes Hierarchical Bounding Volume (BVH) and K-Dimensional tree (KD tree) to accelerate the ray tracing process in the Shooting and Bouncing Ray (SBR) method. This approach extends the application of SBR algorithm to complex multi-layered coated targets. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed approach, when applied to targets with complex coatings, can maintain the same level of accuracy as the traditional SBR method while significantly improving efficiency.

articleTitle: An Ultrathin Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes an ultrathin high-frequency selective frequency selective surface (FSS), which is composed of three metal layers and two dielectric substrates. The receiving patch and transmitting patches are integrated separately on the top and bottom GND layers, respectively. A stripline central guide structure is etched on the middle GND layer. To improve frequency selectivity, a quarter-wavelength stripline resonator is added. High frequency selectivity is also maintained when electromagnetic waves with oblique incidence angles within 40° are incident on the proposed third-order FSS. The frequency selectivity of the proposed third-order FSS at the left and right edges of the passband is 371 dB/GHz and 386 dB/GHz, respectively. It is indicated that the proposed third-order FSS has high frequency selectivity and wide application in the field of electromagnetic compatibility

articleTitle: BIC-based breaking symmetry E-type resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In recent years, metasurfaces have demonstrated remarkable effects in areas such as beam steering, wavefront manipulation, and mode encoding, showcasing their ability for flexible customization in information transmission and processing. This has garnered significant attention. In our work, we discuss a method under the mechanism of Bound States in the Continuum (BIC), where we effectively control the appearance of Fano resonances in metasurfaces by introducing a symmetry-breaking approach. By breaking the x-axis symmetry of the double-E structure, quasi-BIC phenomena can be achieved in the terahertz band. By calculating the Q-factor values, this structure features a symmetry-protected BIC, and the formation of the quasi-BIC is related to the way this BIC symmetry is broken. This lays the foundation for subsequent multi-channel single-band implementations by simultaneously breaking multiple symmetries.

articleTitle: A Broadband Balanced-to-Single-Ended Power Divider with High Common-Mode Suppression Based on ISGW
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a high common-mode (CM) suppression power divider from balanced-to-single-ended (BTSE) based on integrated substrate gap waveguide (ISGW). The microstrip to slotline transition structure effectively suppresses CM signals in the balanced system, while the isolation port between the two single-ended output ports can effectively improve the isolation of the power divider. The slotlines on the top metal layer covered with copper can all facilitate the transmission of electromagnetic energy. them, the double-slotlines non-symmetric microstrip coupling structure introduces new transmission poles, thus expanding the working bandwidth of the power divider. The results show that within the frequency range of 24.9GHz to 36.4GHz, the relative bandwidth reaches up to 37.5%, isolation better than 13dB, and CM suppression is above 35dB.

articleTitle: Semi-Analytical Design Approach to Quasi-Electrically Small Microstrip Annular Sector Patch Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Semi-analytical design approach to circularly polarized (CP) tilted-beam microstrip antenna with quasi-electrically small annular sector patch is presented. At first, the relationship between normalized outer radius $\bar b$, central angle α and outer/inner radii ratio γ=b/a, is studied basing on the eigenfunction family of the asymmetric annular sector patch. In this way, microstrip annular sector patch antenna (MASPA) under dual-mode resonance with quasi-electrically small radius and tilted circularly polarized beam characteristic can be attained. For validations, MASPA with central angle of 355° on air substrate (with a profile less than 0.05-wavelength) is investigated. As is revealed, the antenna can exhibit maximum radius of 0.185-wavelength (quasi-electrically small), tilted CP 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 15.2%, and tilted CP angle ranging from 0° to 20° in the elevation plane.

articleTitle: S-band Circularly Polarized Conformal Antenna Based on Sequential Phase Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized (CP) antenna operating in the S-band that can be used for conformal is presented. The antenna introduces two sets of parasitic patches, both of which are arranged in a sequential rotational manner around a kind of annular patch that provides a 90° phase difference. It is experimentally verified that the antenna also has the ability to be co-formable. Experimental results show that the antenna achieves an impedance bandwidth of 8.61% in the range of 3.56-3.87 GHz. In addition, the antenna achieves a radiation efficiency of 95.8%.

articleTitle: E-pulse Discrimination Technique for Radar Targets of the Same Model But Different Versions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Radar target scattering characteristic in resonance region which takes the shape and size principle information of target is one of the most efficient spectrum characteristic for radar target discrimination. The late-time responses of the targets are usually obvious in the electromagnetic resonance region against those in Rayleigh region and optical region. The E-pulse is designed from the natural modes in the electromagnetic resonance region of the target, and it will eliminate only the late-time response of these specified natural modes. In practical military scenarios, due to various tasks, targets of the same model but different versions with similar appearances but slight differences in certain parts are usually derived. For example, the model of F35 fighter jet has different versions, such as F35A, F35B, F35C. Traditional E-pulse discrimination technique extracts natural modes and constructs E-pulses for every target, which requires a huge amount of calculation and discrimination work and is too time-consuming. In this report, we propose to construct a common E-pulse for the targets belongs to the same model but different versions, provide a specific implementation process, and discuss the impact of method parameters on efficiency. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the method, ensuring recognition accuracy while reducing discrimination time.

articleTitle: Estimation of maximum SAR value based on incident electric field
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The effects of electromagnetic radiation on human health is of public concern. Specific absorption rate (SAR) is commonly used to quantify the electromagnetic radiation level when the radiation frequency ≤ 6 GHz. SAR is used to calculate the electromagnetic power absorbed per unit mass of human tissue. Both experimental measurements and numerical calculations can be used to obtain the specific absorption rate of antenna radiation in the human body. For ethical reasons, it is impractical to conduct real human experiments, and measurements are usually made by building equivalent human heads or physical models of the human body. While the equivalent physical model of the human body has been widely used in industries to assess the exposure level of wireless devices, the complicated environment where human body locate is not considered.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Radar-Based Vital Sign Signal Extraction Using Multiple Distance Bin
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a multi-distance non-contact vital sign signal reconstruction and extraction algorithm based on frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) millimeter wave radar. The technology of measuring vital signs with millimeter wave radar has significant medical value. However, issues such as environmental noise, unconscious micro-movements of the human body, and the extremely subtle vibrations of the thoracic cavity caused by heartbeats greatly reduce the signal-to-noise ratio of the vital sign signals. To address these issues, considering the characteristic that the human body is perceived as a point cloud target under millimeter wave radar, this paper proposes a technique to enhance the signal-to-noise ratio of weak heartbeat signals by utilizing multi-distance vital sign signals. Furthermore, this paper employs the variational mode decomposition (VMD) algorithm for the reconstruction of vital sign signals, achieving high-precision extraction of the human heart rate signal.

articleTitle: Application of The Interpolation Algorithm in Spherical Near-Field Antenna Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In spherical near-field antenna measurements, the interpolation algorithm is utilized to process the measured electric field matrix to achieve two main objectives. Firstly, when the sampling interval fulfills the sampling criteria, the interpolation function is employed to enhance the accuracy of the far-field pattern, which is derived from the spherical near-field to far-field transformation algorithm. Secondly, in cases where the sampling interval fails to meet the sampling criterion, the interpolation algorithm is utilized to improve the accuracy of the far-field pattern. The application of the interpolation algorithm in spherical near-field antenna measurement has been simulated and analyzed, demonstrating that the interpolation algorithm effectively improves the accuracy of the spherical near-field to far-field transformation algorithm.

articleTitle: Design of Four-Element Wide-Band MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A design of four-element wide-band Multiple-input Multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is proposed. The antenna is designed from the basic monopole antenna. The bent feed line of the monopole antenna reduces the overall size of the antenna and the port isolation between different antenna elements is reduced by the defected ground structure. The simulations indicate that the working bandwidth of the MIMO antenna covers 4.5GHz - 7.5GHz, the reflection coefficient is less than 10dB, the coupling between different ports is less than 16dB, and the envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is less than 0.02. The gain of the antenna is 4.4dBi at 4.5GHz, 4.8dBi at 6GHz, and 5.1dBi at 7.5GHz.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Fully Metallic Luneburg Lens Antenna Array with 360° Coverage
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A multi-beam fully metallic Luneburg lens antenna array operating at X-band is presented in this paper. To obtain the 360° beam coverage in the horizontal plane, there are three lens antenna elements in the vertical dimension and each lens antenna element contains twelve radiation beams. The feeder of the lens antenna is the standard waveguide namely WR90, due to its concise structure and stable performance. The simulated results of the lens antenna array show that it can work over 8~12 GHz with good impedance match property and achieve a maximum aperture efficiency of 74% and the gain of 17.65 dBi. The proposed lens antenna array is much suitable for wireless communication and other application.

articleTitle: Position Tolerance Design Method for Antenna Arrays based on Sensitivity Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The position error in antenna arrays is a common and inevitable problem, which can significantly deteriorates the gain and side-lobe of the array. If the required array performance can be determined before designing the antenna arrays, the array element position tolerance can be obtained through some certain methods. This paper focuses on the position tolerance design method based on the sensitivity model while considering multi-dimensional errors. Besides, improvements have been made to the function fitting section of the method, uncertainty analysis results show that the newly designed array has a much higher chance to achieve the desired performance.

articleTitle: Phased array antenna aided by Array Decoupling Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To mitigate coupling effects between phased array antennas, enhance gain, and reduce scanning fluctuations, this paper proposes a slotted feed-backed cavity phased array antenna. An Array Decoupling Surface (ADS) is added above the antenna array to reduce coupling between elements. Finally, a 1×9 H-plane linear array phased array antenna is designed for validation. The antenna array operates at a central frequency of 14.5 GHz with an H-plane scanning angle of ±52°. The scanning gain fluctuation of the antenna is less than 0.62 dB, with a peak gain of 14 dB.

articleTitle: Design of 1-bit Reconfigurable Transmission Metasurface Cell with Spatial Wave Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel active amplified 1-bit reconfigurable transmission metasurface unit that amplifies an incident wave and modulates its transmission phase. The unit consists of three components: a radiating and receiving patch, two PIN diodes, and a transmission amplifier. The receiving patch transfers the incident wave energy into the amplifier and re-radiates it into space with enhanced amplitude and modulated transmission phase. Additionally, the unit features a function that allows for polarization switching. Simulation results show that the amplified reconfigurable transmission unit achieves a phase difference of 180° ± 5° spanning the simulation bandwidth from 4.5 to 5.5 GHz, with a center frequency of 5.0 GHz. The spatial amplification factor is more than 0 dB in the frequency range of 4.73 to 5.24 GHz, with a maximum value of 12 dB. The design provides a new idea for metasurface applications in the field of wireless power transfer.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wideband Circularly Polarized Endfire Atenna Based on Vivaldi Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper we proposed a novel ultra-wideband planar endfire circularly polarized antenna based on Vivaldi antenna. The structure of the proposed antenna includes a unidirectional dielectric radiator (UDR) and a Vivaldi antenna surrounded by the UDR. The Vivaldi antenna is fed by a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) mounted on a 0.025λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> substrate, while the UDR is fed by the Vivaldi antenna, which effectively enhances the vertically polarized (VP) radiation generated by the dielectric instead of the horizontally polarized (HP) radiation. This polarization-selective enhancement technology enables us to develop an ultra-wideband circularly polarized antenna based on a planar Vivaldi structure. The antenna has a -10 dB impedance bandwidth from 10.9 GHz to 18.6 GHz, a relative bandwidth of 52.2%, and a total width of 7.7 GHz; at the same time, the 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth is also 7.7 GHz, ranging from 13.3 GHz to 19 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 35.3%.

articleTitle: Fast Broadband RCS Analysis of Coated Target using EFIE-PMCHWT and MBPE Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To analyze the broadband electromagnetic scattering characteristics of coated target efficiently, the combination of MoM based on EFIE-PMCHWT integer equation and Model Based Parameter Estimation (MBPE) technique based on rational function interpolation is proposed. The MBPE is employed to fit the currents of the whole band with few frequency sampling points currents, which can estimate the broadband RCS quickly. Numerical result shows the proposed method can greatly decrease the calculation time and the calculation accuracy will not be reduced.

articleTitle: A Mixed Precision Direct Electromagnetic Finite Element Solver on GPUs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we present a mixed-precision direct electromagnetic finite element solver on GPU machines. In our solver, we propose a mixed-precision factorization algorithm aimed at obtaining results of the same quality as the double-precision algorithm at a much lower cost. In addition, to accelerate the direct solution of finite element sparse linear systems using GPU machines more efficiently, we propose a novel pipelined offloading technique that utilizes CUDA streams to achieve pipeline scheduling with overlapping computations and data transfers. Our numerical experiments show that by combining our proposed mixed-precision algorithm with the pipelined offloading technique, our proposed solver produces exact solutions with tremendous speedup.

articleTitle: Performance Investigation of OAM-SK Optical Communication System Based on PCNN-NMS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a PCNN-NMS demodulation method for an OAM-SK optical communication system operating under atmospheric turbulence, by integrating the data-driven probabilities of a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) model with the Normalized Min-Sum (NMS) LDPC decoding algorithm. Then we simulated the average bit error rate (ABER). Initially, the transmission of Laguerre-Gaussian (LG) beams through atmospheric turbulence is simulated using the power spectrum inversion method, and a dataset is created for training the CNN network. This training achieves a direct classification accuracy of 97.3% with the CNN demodulator. Subsequently, the classification probabilities from the CNN are incorporated into the NMS algorithm, using the output of the CNN to refine the credibility of channel estimation. The final simulation results show that the PCNN-NMS significantly improves the system's BER performance, offering valuable insights for enhancing the BER performance in free-space optical communication system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Single Reflector Compact Antenna Test Range With High Aperture Usage Based on Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In compact antenna test range (CATR), the aperture usage is one of our most concerned problems. The quiet zone (QZ) performance of a CATR is mainly determined by two aspects: feed system and edge diffraction [1]. We optimize both the feed and serrated edge of an offset-feed CATR and achieve higher aperture usage using a multi-parameter genetic algorithm in this paper.

articleTitle: Enhanced 1-bit Programmable Metasurface Failure Diagnosis via Hadamard Matrices
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the failure diagnosis performance of the 1-bit programmable metasurface is improved by using the Hadamard matrix. According to the compressive sensing (CS) theory, the accuracy of sparse signal recovery is impacted by the orthogonality of the measurement matrix. Thus, the Hadamard matrix is introduced to build up the measurement matrix for 1-bit programmable metasurface failure diagnosis. In order to verify the validity of the proposed method, the diagnostic performance is compared when random and Hadamard matrices are utilized to construct the measurement matrix. Simulation results show that the Hadamard matrix achieves lower reconstruction errors and leads to improved fault diagnosis performance.

articleTitle: A Gain Maintenance Scheme for Pulse Compression Device under Temperature Drift Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes an X-band high-power passive pulse compression device based on a spherical energy storage cavity. The pulse compression device mainly consists of a dual polarisation mode coupler and a spherical energy storage cavity. The device can convert a long-time low-amplitude pulse into a high-amplitude short-time pulse with a peak power gain of more than five times. However, the pulse compression device based on the spherical energy storage cavity is a point-frequency device, and the temperature dramatically affects its resonant frequency. By studying the effect of temperature change on the performance of the pulse compression device, a method of maintaining the gain of the pulse compression device under temperature change based on a temperature probe is proposed.

articleTitle: A Wideband Circularly Polarized Conical Spiral Antenna based on Multistage Nested Cavity Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized spiral antenna with conical and cylindrical surfaces is proposed. The two-arm spiral, whose line width and pitch change gradually with frequency, achieves a wide beam and improves the gain of low elevation. The wound cylindrical spiral and resistance loading improve the radiation performance of low frequency. In order to further increase the low elevation gain and make full use of the backward radiation, a wideband stepped reflector cavity is designed. Its height and diameter vary with frequency, and it is equipped with a choker groove. A spherical dielectric radome loaded at the front end of the antenna reduces beam jitter and makes the radiation pattern smoother. The volume of the antenna is 20.6×20.6× 20.25mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, operates at 8-18GHz, VSWR <2, axial ratio <3dB. Moreover, it has a gain value greater than 0.19dBi in the axial ± 60° range and a gain value greater than -6dBi in the axial ±90° range. The antenna proposed in this paper has good radiation performance in the upper half space.

articleTitle: All-Metallic, H-Shaped Magneto-Electric Dipole Antenna With Ultra-Wide Bandwidth Fed by a Hollow Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An all-metallic, cavity backed magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna in the Ka-band is proposed. The antenna consists of three metal layers combined to exhibit ultra-wide impedance bandwidth and high efficiency performance. The proposed design can be transformed into a planar antenna array while maintaining its wide bandwidth characteristics along with reasonable inter-element spacing. The structure is easy to realize through precision CNC milling technique as well as through 3D printing technology. An antenna element exhibits a gain of up to 10.3 dBi and an impedance bandwidth of about 65% from 27.5GHz to 54GHz and efficiency greater than 90% respectively. The three layers of the antenna include a radiating layer where lies a magneto-electric (ME) dipole element, a cavity layer for bandwidth enhancement and hollow waveguide based feed layer. For planar antenna array design, four such antenna elements can be combined against one cavity and fed by a hollow waveguide at the bottom layer. Low-loss and compact T-junction power dividers can be incorporated in the feed network layer for best antenna performance. The proposed magneto-electric (ME) dipole has a wide range of applications for broad bandwidth millimeter-wave wireless communication.

articleTitle: An Alternative Sub-Structure Generalized Eigenvalue Equation for Characteristic Modes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A new type surface integral equation (SIE)-based sub-structure generalized eigenvalue equation (GEE) for composite objects has been proposed in this paper. The obtained eigenvalues can reflect the radiation efficiency of each mode directly. These mode solutions can provide more flexible guidance for the design of antennas in lossy environments. Numerical results validate the validity and veracity of the proposed GEE for characteristic mode (CM).

articleTitle: A High Isolation Ultra-Wideband Eight-Element MIMO Antenna Pairs Array for 5G Mobile Terminals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high isolation ultra-wideband (UWB) 8-element MIMO antenna array for 5G mobile terminals has come up. The antenna array is composed of four identical antenna pairs, which are respectively arranged on the inside of the four frames. Broadband decoupling is realized by loading the shorting stub connected to the ground plane set in the middle of the antenna pair. The simulation results show that the operating bandwidth of the MIMO antenna array is 3.3-7.5 GHz (S11 < - 6 dB), and the relative bandwidth is 77.8%. The isolation between any two ports is higher than 15 dB. In addition, the ideal overall efficiency and ECC (Envelope Correlation Coefficient) are also simulated.

articleTitle: A high performance stacked band-pass filter with frequency doubling suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high performance stacked bandpass filter based on frequency doubling suppression is proposed. The proposed filter consists of an interdigital structure and a stepped impedance resonator (SIR). The two structures are combined in a laminated manner and connected by vertical metal vias. The filter has compact size, excellent passband performance and wide stopband. The proposed miniaturized bandpass filter is expected to be applied in modern communication systems.

articleTitle: Research on EMI characteristics of electric vehicle charging process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Radiated and conducted emissions are issues that arise during the charging process of electric vehicles. Through electromagnetic interference(EMI) testing of vehicles with various distribution parameters, charging currents, and phase number, it was found that charging current has minimal impact on radiated emission and conducted emissions. Changes in distribution parameters will cause variations in broadband signals of conducted emissions to correlate with the original test results. The radiated emission test results of single-phase AC charging are lower than those of three-phase testing.

articleTitle: Higher order BIC of metasurface excited by magnetic EIT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Metasurfaces enable complex modulation of terahertz waves. However, the quality factor of metallic metasurfaces is often limited by intrinsic ohmic losses. The concept of bound states in the continuum (BIC) has been proposed to enhance terahertz-matter interactions. High order BICs have garnered attention due to their robustness. Previous studies on high-order BICs focused on photonic crystals, requiring high structural symmetry. In this paper, we propose a metasurface design based on the magnetic Electromagnetic induced transparency (EIT) effect to excite higher-order BIC eigenmodes. This novel approach and the resulting robust modes hold great potential for terahertz sensing and communication applications.

articleTitle: Mixed Discretization Scheme Based Discontinuous Galerkin Domain Decomposition Method for Multi-scale Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The discontinuous Galerkin (DG)-based domain decomposition method (DDM) for the surface integral equation (SIE) has been proven to be an effective numerical method for modeling multi-scale electromagnetic (EM) problems. This paper aims to further improve the accuracy of the DG-SIE by incorporating a mixed discretization scheme (MDS) built upon Buffa-Christiansen (BC) functions. To this end, we first discuss a special case for constructing BC functions and make it suitable for discretizing the open-surface subdomains generally involved in the DDM framework. In the MDS within the combined field integral equation-based DG method (DG-CFIE), the BC functions act as testing functions for the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE), whereas the Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) basis functions are utilized for discretizing the electric field integral equation (EFIE). Numerical experiments demonstrate that the DG-CFIE employing the new mixed discretization scheme has notably improved accuracy while preserving the previous good properties of flexibility and fast convergence.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Synthesis Method Based on Space-Time Coding Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Space-time coding metasurfaces can control electromagnetic waves in the spatial domain and achieve multidimensional control in space, frequency, and time domain. A space-time coding metasurfaces is introduced with time modulation incorporated into traditional beam forming theory, summarizing the theoretical formulas for beam forming under space-time coding conditions and methods for multiple beams forming. Based on the derived theories, control of harmonics in space-time coded metasurfaces is theoretically calculated and verified through simulations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic-Thermal Coupling Analysis with FETD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper adopts the finite element time-domain (FETD) method to solve the coupled electromagnetic and thermal field equations for microwave circuits. The coupling occurs through electromagnetic losses and the temperature-dependent characteristics of the material parameters. An example of a rectangular waveguide is presented to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: An Edge Swapping Technique with Prioritized Surface Fitting in Adaptive Finite Element Method for Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a surface-fitting prioritized edge-swapping technique is proposed for curved surface mesh optimization in electromagnetic finite element. The Lawson algorithm is combined with Hausdorff distance to optimize the mesh quality by performing local edge swapping while ensuring good surface fitting. The example results show that the mesh quality is high and the surface is well-fitted after optimizing the mesh with the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Component RCS Analysis for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an analysis method of component RCS is proposed and applied to analyze the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The matrix equation is constructed with the whole structure and solved by multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). The local currents of the component are extracted to implement the component radar cross section (RCS) calculation. The component RCS results, which include the coupling effects between components, can accurately represent the effect of the component on the whole structure. Finally, two types of UAV are simulated by the proposed method to present the component RCS analysis.

articleTitle: Conformal Tightly Coupled Dipole Array With Ultrawideband Dual-Polarized Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces novel methods for removing common-mode resonance (CMR) in conformal tightly coupled dipole arrays (TCDAs) designed for ultrawideband dual-polarized operation. Two ultra-wideband dual-polarized unit cells of TCDA are proposed using ideal port feeding. Each unit cell is fed by a simple parallel double conductor, eliminating the requirement for designing a balun to balance the operating currents. The CMR can be suppressed by loading the shorting lines and utilizing a two-set unit cell configuration. The simplicity of feeding strategy enables the proposed TCDAs to achieve high performance while facilitating conformal operation. The conformal operation of the dual-polarized TCDA further optimizes the CMR, ensuring impedance stability for the proposed conformal TCDA during ultrawideband operation and wide-angle scanning.

articleTitle: The Impact of Plasma Wake on Radar Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Plasma sheath and plasma wake produced by meteor reentry vehicles flying at high speeds in the atmosphere can affect the detection performance of radar systems. This paper employs the Finite Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method to analyze the two-dimensional bistatic Radar Cross Section (RCS) of entire targets, including blunt bodies along with their plasma sheaths and wakes. The effects of different wake lengths on RCS frequencies of 30MHz, 300 MHz and 1GHz at normal and oblique incidence were investigated. The results showed that the RCS was significantly enhanced by plasma sheath and wake, with the increase being more pronounced at lower frequencies.

articleTitle: Design of a quad-band multipolarized monopulse Cassegrain antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a quad-band, multifunctional monopulse Cassegrain antenna suitable for integration into aircraft for deep space exploration. This design addresses the common limitations of space and weight in such missions. The antenna achieves multiplexing of the X1, X2, X3, and Ka bands using a 5-horn array feed. The X3-band monopulse function is realized through four square horns positioned around the array, with horizontal polarization for the X1 and X3 bands and vertical polarization for the X2 and Ka bands. Measurement results indicate that the VSWR is below 1.5 for the X2, X3, and Ka bands, below 1.6 for the X1 band, and below 1.6 for the X3 differential port. The measured gain exceeds 38.9 dB for the X1 band, 40 dB for the X2 band, 41.1 dB for the X3 sum port, 38.1 dB for the X3 azimuthal-differential port, 38.4 dB for the X3 elevation-differential port, and 51.2 dB for the Ka band. This antenna is well-suited for aircraft engaged in deep space exploration missions.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for Wideband Bandpass Filters Design Using Autoencoder and Grey Wolf Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an optimization method for structural parameters of wideband bandpass filters (BPFs) design based on autoencoder (AE) and grey wolf optimizer (GWO) is proposed. Once the AE is trained, the encoder of the AE can quickly predict the structural parameters from the S-parameters, the decoder of the AE can replace the EM simulation to obtain the S-parameters from the structural parameters. In order to quickly obtain the optimal structure parameters, the GWO and the decoder are used for optimization. A BPF with a pair of coupled-line and two short-circuited stub is proposed to prove the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can quickly and accurately obtain the optimal structural parameters of the BPF.

articleTitle: Research on Electromagnetic Scattering and Inverse Scattering of Target Based on Transfer Learning Physics-Informed Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Traditional electromagnetism is significantly more computationally complex and challenging when faced with, for example, more complex high-dimensional problems. In recent years, efficient data-driven methods such as deep learning have become powerful instruments for studying electromagnetic scattering and the inverse scattering of targets. Physical-informed Neural Networks (PINNs) can embed model equations as a physical driving force into the neural network, and are able to learn more generalizable models with small datasets compared to traditional data-driven neural networks. At the same time, transfer learning can accelerate the training speed of neural networks as well as their generalization ability. This paper combines transfer learning with PINNs and proposes Transfer Learning Physics-Informed Neural Networks (TL-PINNs), which greatly improves the training speed and generalization ability of PINNs and has broad application prospects.

articleTitle: Method for Surface-Waves Suppression in Millimeter-Wave PUMA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a method is proposed to suppress the surface waves guided by the wide-angle impedance matching (WAIM) layer in millimeter-wave planar ultrawideband modular antennas. Based on the analysis of the magnetic-fields and Poynting-vector distributions, a novel metallic structure is proposed, which suppresses the surface-wave mode effectively. By adding the metallic structures at the critical positions within the WAIM layer, the surface waves are suppressed while maintaining good radiation. Consequently, the proposed antenna array can scan to ±60° in E/H planes with active VSWRs < 3 in 21–69GHz.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency Circularly Polarized Slots Pair Element for K-Band Radial-Line Slot Array Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Circularly Polarized (CP) slot pair element designed for Radial-Line Slot Array (RLSA) antennas. By employing an all-metal parallel plate waveguide (PPW) integrated with metallic pins, the design effectively mitigates dielectric loss, resulting in enhanced radiation efficiency. Simulation results demonstrate a favorable axial ratio and radiation pattern at 19.5 GHz, with a 1-dB axial ratio bandwidth from 18.7 GHz to 20.3 GHz. The metallic pins' height optimization prevents grating lobes while maintaining wide bandwidth. The proposed design, with varying slot lengths, ensures uniform antenna performance, achieving a peak gain of 8.35 dBi and a minimum axial ratio of 0.1 dB. This high-gain, low-profile, wideband solution promises practical applications in K-band RLSA antennas.

articleTitle: Design of Circularly Polarized Metal Frame Smartwatch Antenna for GNSS Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a metal frame smartwatch antenna based on N-port network theory, operating in the L5/L1 bands of Global Navigation Satellite System(GNSS). By optimizing the N-port structure with multi-objective optimizer NSGA-III, changing the port state at the appropriate position, the proposed antenna achieves right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) in the L5 and L1 bands to provide positioning services. The proposed antenna has two breaking points on the metal frame, providing freedom for the multi-antenna design. The antenna is promising due to its simple structure and practicality.

articleTitle: A Broadband Low-Profile Folded Transmitarray Antenna Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A broadband low-profile folded transmitarray antenna is proposed based on metasurface(MS). The antenna consists of a transmitarray and a reflective surface (RS). In the transmitarray element design, the I-shaped resonator is placed in the middle of two substrate layers, while the upper and lower metallic layers are two orthogonal polarization gratings. The I-shaped resonator is also used in the RS element. By adjusting the size of the I-shaped resonator on both transmitarray element and RS element, the transmitting phase and the reflecting phase can be designed. Based on the above theory, the ratio of the height of the profile to the aperture of the array is reduced to 0.16 and the profile is reduced to 1/5 of the focal length. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna can achieve a peak gain of 24.8 dBi, a peak aperture efficiency of 54%, a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 18.4% and a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 35.4%.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Based Sparse Near-Field Scanning: When to Automatically Stop?
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Active machine learning can significantly improve the efficiency of near-field scanning (NFS) by adaptively selecting important sparse samples. However, an appropriate and automated stopping criterion for the machine learning method has not yet been investigated and defined. This article proposes a novel automated stopping criterion for active-learning-based sparse NFS by estimating the worst-case prediction error at the unsampled locations. The machine-learning-based NFS process is automatically stopped when the estimated worst-case prediction error is below a user-defined threshold value, which can serve as a highly reliable and intuitive criterion to accommodate different requirements on the near-field image accuracy while maximizing the NFS efficiency. The proposed stopping criterion is validated in both simulation and measurement cases.

articleTitle: A Sparse Reconfigurable Intelligence Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: While the reconfigurable intelligence metasurface (RIS) has attracted tremendous attention in recent years, it suffers from high cost and power consumption due to the use of a large number of electrically tunable components. Here, we propose a 2-bit sparse RIS for beam-scanning application in the X-band. It is composed of 196 digitally encoded unit cells; but different from conventional RIS, the number of tunable unit cells is largely reduced by 33.7%, and it can still maintain the beam-scanning range from -60° to 60° in the E-plane with the sidelobe below -12 dB. This is realized by a delicate sparse design that is optimized using a dual-layer nested genetic algorithm, which is presented in the paper.

articleTitle: IPD-Based Miniaturized Bandpass Filter Chip with Independently Controllable Transmission Zeros Using Lumped Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of a compact, bandwidth-adjustable bandpass filter (BPF) using Integrated Passive Device (IPD) technology. The BPF adopts a symmetrical configuration of lumped elements, enabling independent control over transmission zeros and flexible adjustment of bandwidth. The filter's performance is validated through odd-even mode analysis and confirmed by both electromagnetic simulation and experimental measurements. The fabricated BPF chip achieves excellent performance with dimensions of 1.40 mm × 0.88 mm, featuring an insertion loss of 1.26 dB in the passband and a stop-band rejection exceeding 21.44 dB.

articleTitle: Spoof Localized Surface Plasmon Sensor for Dielectric Material Measurements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a notched metal spiral spoof LSPs double-layer resonator structure is proposed, which is excited by microstrip lines and generates multipolar resonant modes, based on which a dielectric constant sensor is realized, and the microwave sensor operates in the frequency range of 3 GHz to 3.9 GHz, and the simulation results show that the sensor has the advantages of high sensitivity and good robustness, and has great potential in dielectric constant measurement. The simulation results show that the sensor has the advantages of high sensitivity and good robustness and has great potential in dielectric constant measurement.

articleTitle: Deep Image Prior Enabled Two-Dimensional Electromagnetic Computation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Supervised deep learning has shown promising progress in accurate and efficient electromagnetic modeling. However, a significant challenge arises when employing neural networks (NNs) in electromagnetic computations, as they typically require a substantial amount of training data, which are often not readily available.To address the problems associated with data training, we propose an unsupervised deep image prior (DIP) network for two-dimensional (2D) electromagnetic computations, which consists of three main components: an encoder, a decoder, and skip connections. The input data is only one low-resolution portrait of the fields generated through the 2D finite-difference time-domain method (FDFD) and is directly utilized by the DIP network to predict the numerical solution of electromagnetic fields. The resulting output data represents the distribution of the electric field with high-resolution. Through numerical tests, the proposed DIP method presents great applicability and robustness for 2D scattering problems involving scatterers with varying shapes and material properties, including relative permittivity, relative permeability, and electric conductivity. Utilizing a field distribution defined on a coarse mesh, the DIP network is capable of outputting a field distribution with accuracy comparable to that of a dense mesh. For instance, when provided with input data at a sampling density of 10 points per wavelength (PPW), the DIP method significantly enhances the original FDFD result at the same sampling density, achieving near-equivalence with the accuracy of FDFD with 20 PPW. Compared to previous research on the application of NNs in electromagnetic computation, which often relies on high-quality and generalizable data for training, our approach utilizing the FDFD method in conjunction with the DIP network allows for fast and precise computation of the 2D electromagnetic field distribution without the need for training data. The DIP method introduces novel directions and possibilities for research and applications within the domain of numerical computation of electromagnetic fields.

articleTitle: Multifunctional wavelength division multiplexer based on the topological rainbow in valley photonic crystals
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The topological rainbow is a peculiar physical phenomenon, and has important application prospects in the fields of topological photonics and micro/nano-photon devices. Here, we design a multifunctional wavelength division multiplexer by using the gradient topological valley photonic crystals. By introducing a rotational degree of freedom, it can be achieved the different cutoff frequencies of the interface state dispersion at different spatial locations. This multifunctional wavelength division multiplexer comprises a lateral transmission channel and several vertical transmission channels. It can precisely separate the electromagnetic waves with different frequencies and capture different positions of the transmission channels, thus achieving the precise control of the multi-band electromagnetic waves.

articleTitle: Parameter Extraction of Diode RIS Elements Based on the Waveguide Equivalent Test Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This study delves into the parameter extraction of diode RIS (Reconfigurable Intelligence Surface) array elements using the waveguide equivalent test method. An infinite periodic RIS array environment was constructed using waveguide equivalent simulation methods, enabling rapid acquisition of amplitude and phase information for diode-controlled RIS unit devices. Comparing the simulation data with the fitting results reveals a high degree of consistency, which validates the scientific and effective nature of the proposed method and provides a solid theoretical foundation and a cost-effective practical validation scheme for subsequent diode parameter extraction and RIS array design. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Research and design of dielectric filter antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the development of fifth generation (5G) mobile technology, the requirement for RF front-end integration is increasing. In this paper, the first integrated design of dielectric filter antenna is proposed, where the center frequency of dielectric filter is at 4.88 GHz and the bandwidth ranges from 4.8 to 4.96 GHz, and the cross-coupling is added. The filter and antenna are integrated to achieve better integration and frequency selectivity, while processing is easy and can be done using a single mould. The design is done using HFSS and CST joint simulation, and the design is completed by fitting and analyzing the data. Finally, the return loss is more than 14dB, the maximum gain is 6.04dB, and the radiation efficiency of the antenna reaches 90%.

articleTitle: An improved comtrast method with variable window limitation for dispersion compensation of MARSIS echoes and TEC inversion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Mars Advanced Radar for Subsurface and Ionospheric Sounding (MARSIS) on onboard the European Space Agency Mars Express spacecraft is a low-frequency nadir-looking radar sounder. The operation frequency is close to the maximum plasma frequency of Martian ionosphere. Accurate estimation of dispersion phase is beneficial for focusing imaging of echo signals, and accurate inversion of Total Electron Content (TEC). This paper proposes an improved Contrast Method (CM) to estimate the dispersion phase with Gamma model and local window constraint. Firstly, the local maxima detection is used to determine accurate group delay value based on the horizontal continuity of ionosphere. Then, the Gamma model and window function are used to optimize the higher-order terms of dispersion phase. Finally, all terms of dispersion phase are synthesized to compute the compensation phase for echo correction and to precisely estimate TEC along track. Compared to the conventional CM, the new method not only corrects group delay correctly, but also achieves stable high-order expansion terms, providing a better correction approach for ionospheric compensation of Mars subsurface radar.

articleTitle: On the use of the revised pulse vector basis functions for volume integral equation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A kind of revised definition for the pulse vector basis functions is proposed to discretize the the volume integral equation (VIE) by the method of moments. The traditional definition of the pulse vector basis functions (PVBF) is revised and three PVBF are defined in a pair of elements sharing a common face. It is shown that for electromagnetic scattering from thin dielectric objects, the solution efficiency of the VIE can be improved while keeping accuracy by the use of the revised PVBF.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band OAM Resonator Circular Array Antenna with High Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A dual-band resonator orbital angular momentum (OAM) array antenna is proposed in this study. A resonator antenna unit consisting of one patch with comb-like SSPP structure is first designed, and simulated. The proposed metallic resonator antenna achieves low loss compared to conventional dielectric resonator antenna, because most of fields concentrate in air rather than in dielectric. The proposed antenna array works at 2.6 GHz and 4.2 GHz respectively. Simulation results, including the E-field distribution in near field and radiation pattern in far field, validate that the proposed antenna array could generate vortex electromagnetic fields with mode 1 and generate high gain of 6 dB,10 dB at 2.6 GHz and 4.2 GHz respectively.

articleTitle: On the Doubt of the Simplified FEM Formulation for Waveguide Discontinuity Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: It is a key step for designing an efficient numerical solution to simplify the mathematic formulation based on the physical characteristics of problems. A doubt in the simplified FEM formulation is presented for the waveguide discontinuity problem. The reason is figured out why the look-like reasonable formulation cannot give accurate results. The explanation and numerical results further demonstrate that the uniqueness on boundary condition is the key issue causing the problem.

articleTitle: A Novel Adaptive Non-uniform Conformal Meshing Method for Efficient FDTD Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the process of generating conventional FDTD meshes, the model voxelization often takes up too many computational resources. To address this issue, this paper is devoted to presenting an effective mesh voxelization technique with adaptive partitioning and non-uniform grid generation. In this scheme, the entire computational domain is divided into subintervals based on the model's demarcation points, and the mesh generation parameters can be adaptively adjusted according to the information of each sub-interval in order to generate a reasonable non-uniform mesh. Besides, the scheme corrects mesh generation conditions for voxels across the model interface and records their conformal information, resolving the staircase approximation issue caused by traditional voxelization. The proposed mesh generation technique can minimize the number of grids while ensuring the geometrical accuracy of the model. The mesh quality is further validated by applied to meshing some typical objects in computational electromagnetics problems.

articleTitle: A Radar Contactless Blood Pressure Detection Technology based on Pulse Waves Using High-order Polynomial Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Compared with cuff-contact Blood Pressure (BP) measurement methods such as mercury sphygmomanometers, radar contactless BP detection technology has good application prospects in fields for patients with burns, infectious diseases, or homecare health monitoring due to its ability to continuously monitor BP for a long time without any constraints. Currently, research in this area is mainly based on the pulse transit time (PTT). In this paper, a PTT BP fitting method based on a high-order polynomial regression model was proposed, which uses a 24-GHz continuous wave radar to collect 42 sets of radial artery data from two subjects for seven days. Three regression models were applied for BP calculation and the results were shown. Compared with linear regression and logarithmic regression, the proposed method performed better in terms of the R-square, Root Mean Square Error(RMSE), and Mean Absolute Error(MAE). The Mean Deviation(MD) and Standard Deviation(SD) of systolic and diastolic BP were -0.106 ± 0.474 mmHg and 0.574 ± 2.161 mmHg, respectively. The feasibility and accuracy of this method was demonstrated.

articleTitle: A Distributed Nuclear Power Plant Electromagnetic Environment Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper develops a distributed electromagnetic environment monitoring system for nuclear plants. It enables uninterrupted monitoring of electromagnetic conditions across various locations, ensuring the safe operation of nuclear reactors and enhancing national infrastructure safety.

articleTitle: Method for Modeling of Cavity-Backed Conformal Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A method for modeling of cavity-backed conformal array antenna is proposed to precisely design arbitrary-shaped conformal antenna with low profile. The method is based on meshing tools which can obtain units’ position information and normal direction. The antenna designed by the method shows high uniformity in units compared with installation method with flexible materials and lower profile while the units’ cavities are embedded in the carrier. The arrangement of units is chosen as quasi-rectangular in order to obtain better radiation patterns. An arbitrary-shaped conformal array antenna is modeled and simulated. The results reach the expected target and show that the method is feasible and effective.

articleTitle: Design of a miniaturized K-band SIW filter based on LTCC process
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a K-band fourth-order substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) filter based on a low-temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) process is proposed for use in satellite receiving systems, which operates in the frequency band from 19 .2 GHz to 21.2 GHz with the in-band return loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>) of less than 24 dB and the insertion loss (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of less than 1.40 dB. The bandpass rejection capability is further improved by introducing a cross-coupling structure in the top- and bottom-resonant cavities, enabling the introduction of an out-of-band transmission zero at 18 GHz and 22.75 GHz, respectively. The overall size of the filter is 4.7 mm×5.2 mm×0.768 mm, which features miniaturization and low profile.

articleTitle: Characterization of Liquid Crystal Complex Dielectric Constants Based on Localized Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Liquid crystal (LC), as an anisotropic material, has attracted much attention in high frequency microwave and millimeter wave applications due to its tunable dielectric properties. It has great influence on the design of reconfigurable microwave devices like tunable phase shifters, beam-steering antennas and filters. Therefore, the accurate characterization of LC dielectric properties is highly valued that the design and optimization of reconfigurable microwave devices. In this paper, a device for measuring LC dielectric properties based on SLSP is proposed. The device makes full use of SLSP's high sensitivity, high Q factor and relatively consistent electric field line direction to detect the transmission response. Moreover, for anisotropic materials to be measured, the device applies an external bias electric field to change the electric field line and its angle to extract the complex dielectric constant. The perturbation method utilizes S-parameters to compute the complex dielectric constants of LC molecules in both horizontal and vertical states. The extraction results from a variety of standard samples have validated the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Forward modeling and analysis of scattering center of complex target with cavities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the forward modeling and analysis of scattering centers in complex targets with cavities. A forward modeling method for scattering centers in complex targets with cavities is proposed, followed by a ray-divided scattering source extraction method. Then, a scattering center model of a airplane target with cavities is established forwardly. By comparing the reconstructed radar image of scattering centers with the radar image obtained from simulation, the accuracy of scattering center parameters is verified.

articleTitle: Prediction of radiation pattern of flexible antenna based on ANN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The electrical performance of flexible antennas changes when subjected to bending in practical applications. To calculate the radiation pattern, traditional methods require multiple simulations, which is time-consuming and laborious. Aiming at this problem, this paper proposes a flexible antenna radiation pattern prediction model based on artificial neural network (ANN). Based on the dataset which includes simulation results of radiation pattern at different bending degree of the antenna, a fully connected ANN framework was established. The model predicts the radiation pattern by using input parameters which are bending degree of the antenna, polar angle θ and azimuthal angle φ of radiation pattern. The prediction model can efficiently predict radiation pattern of flexible antennas with the loss value of 1.95×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> and reduce the calculation time of one single state of bending from 1.5h to 12s, contributing to relevant research.

articleTitle: Study on the Electrical Properties of Anisotropic Composites and the Inversion of Inclusion Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Effective electrical properties (e.g., resistivity and permittivity) are important physical properties of composite materials, typically determined by various factors including material composition, proportion, and inclusion structure. However, most existing theoretical models neglect the influence of microgeometry when analyzing the effective electrical properties, thereby inaccurately describing composites with strong anisotropy, such as natural formations containing fractures. Furthermore, current electrical property measurement experiments are usually conducted only in a single direction, potentially leading to an inadequate interpretation of the electrical anisotropy exhibited by materials. This paper conducts a modeling analysis of rock samples containing fractures using the Finite-Element Method (FEM); and designs a multi-directional resistivity measurement system for the same rock sample, comprehensively analyzing the effective electrical properties of anisotropic composites. In addition, we use a chart-based inversion framework proposed in the previous study to predict fracture inclusion geometry. The validity of the inversion method is tested by comparing with the experimental data. The results of this study provide important theoretical support and experimental evidence for the electrical analysis of anisotropic composite materials.

articleTitle: Radiation Analysis of Electrically Large Structures Using a Combination of the Fast Dipole Method and the Physical Optics Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A hybrid approach integrating the fast dipole method (FDM) and physical optics (PO) is presented for the analysis of electrically large structures. This method accelerates the integration of method-of-moments (MoM) self-interactions and matrix-vector multiplications, streamlined through a Taylor’s series expansion. The approach is further refined using the equivalent dipole moment method (EDM) for impedance calculations. Compared to conventional methods, our technique demonstrates improved efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: Quad-Band Shared-Aperture Antenna Using A Multi-Function Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A four-port shared-aperture antenna with a multifunction metasurface is proposed and analyzed in this paper. The adopted metasurface can be simultaneously used as the radiation sources of a S-band microstrip patch radiator and a Ka-band microstrip grid array (MGA) and as the partially reflective surfaces (PRSs) of a X- and a Ka-band Fabry-Perot (F-P) antennas. By integrating the above four radiators compactly, the final antenna operates at 2.3, 11.5, 26.0 and 40.0 GHz each with their bandwidths of 4.0%, 2.0%, 7.4% and 9.5%. Besides, within these operation bands, the realized peak gains are 7.1, 11.0, 15.2 and 19.2 dBi, respectively.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Research on Electromagnetic Performance of Radomes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper utilizes genetic algorithms combined with entropy method and TOPSIS evaluation method to optimize the C-sandwich radome. The optimization objectives include minimizing transmission efficiency, averaging transmission efficiency, reflectivity, and aiming error. The core layer of the radome can be optimized with variable thickness in segmented sections. The optimization results indicate that the approach combining genetic algorithms with the entropy method and TOPSIS can rapidly converge to a core layer thickness scheme that meets the design criteria.

articleTitle: An Ultra-wideband Circularly-polarized Vivaldi Antenna with Wide Beam Angel
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A new kind of wide beam circular polarization UWB antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna consists of four Vivaldi antennas placed along the edge of the square. A copper column is placed around the antenna, and a copper ring is parasitic on the periphery of the copper column to realize the broadening of the beam width. The impedance matching of antennas can be improved by adding metal holes between antennas. The simulation results show that the 10 dB impedance bandwidth (IBW) of the antenna is 97.8% (7.3-21 GHz), and the 3 dB axial specific bandwidth (ARBW) is 100% (7-21 GHz). The antenna beam Angle is relatively large, and the -5dBi beam Angle is greater than 90°.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic wave scattering characteristics of plasma plumes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The FLUENT fluid simulation software was used to numerically simulate the flow field structure and electron density distribution of a rocket plume at the jet port of a rocket thruster under varying pressure and initial temperature conditions. The resulting variation in electron density within the rocket plume's flow field with respect to pressure and initial temperature was analyzed, leading to the development of an electromagnetic scattering characteristic model for the rocket plume. Radar cross sections (RCS) were then compared and calculated for the rocket thruster, single jet plume, and double jet plume. The findings indicate that RCS increases with higher jet pressure, while changes in initial temperature have minimal impact on RCS. Furthermore, compared to a single jet, a double jet configuration results in a larger RCS value with more frequent oscillations.

articleTitle: Wideband Electromagnetic Scattering: Adaptive Frequency Sampling for Multi-Scale Targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive frequency sampling (AFS) technique employing subdomain equivalent dipole moment (SEDM) to accelerate the calculation of wideband electromagnetic scattering for multi-scale targets. Overcoming the limitations of traditional iterative methods, this approach significantly reduces impedance matrix filling times and iterative convergence times. Numerical examples validate the efficiency and accuracy of the proposed method, demonstrating its potential in wideband electromagnetic scattering analysis.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Log-Periodic Dipole Arrays Antenna Using End loaded Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized Log-Periodic Dipole Arrays antenna (LPDA) using end-loaded dipole is presented. The length of the longest radiation dipole is shorter than 0.35λ at the lowest operating frequency, with a main-back lobe ratio greater than 13dB and a maximum gain better than 6.5dB. Measured results demonstrate that the miniaturized LPDA exhibits excellent radiation performance over a bandwidth of 3.3:1. The structure is easy to fabricate, and furthermore, this antenna can be utilized in broadband phased arrays due to its compact design.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electromagnetic Scattering from Rough Surface based on the Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The Method of Moments (MOM) is widely applied to solving electromagnetic scattering from rough surfaces due to its high precision, yet it suffers from significant computational time in generating and solving the target impedance matrix. Traditional Conjugate Gradient Method (CGM), on the other hand, encounters high computational costs when dealing with complex rough surfaces, requiring numerous iterations to converge to a satisfactory solution. To address this issue, this paper integrates machine learning with CGM, utilizing the supervised learning algorithm of Multi-output Support Vector Regression (MSVR) to predict the gradient direction and current distribution within CGM iterations. Compared to traditional CGM, this approach reduces the number of iterations, significantly shortens the time required to solve the matrix equation, and maintains sufficient accuracy.

articleTitle: Application of hybrid ACA-PO Method for Efficient Analysis of Antenna Array around Complex Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The Adaptive Cross-Approximation (ACA) technique is employed to accelerate the conventional MoM-PO for analyzing antenna array in the vicinity of an electrically large platform. The hybrid ACA-PO method compresses the self-impedance matrix of the MoM region and the interaction matrices between the MoM and PO regions, and utilizes the decomposed low-rank matrix to efficiently perform matrix-vector multiplication (MVM). A numerical example is provided to demonstrate the efficiency and precision of the proposed hybrid method.

articleTitle: Miniaturized Leaky Waveguide Antenna with Fixed-Beam for High-Power Microwave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A fixed-beam leaky waveguide antenna (LWA) featuring simple and miniaturized structure for high-power microwave (HPM) applications is proposed in this paper. The beam-squint reduction of conventional LWA is achieved by introducing a prism with the inverse dispersion behaviour in the radiating aperture. The miniaturized prism is precisely designed based on radiating characteristics of the LWA and geometrical optics.
