The proposed antenna radiates at an angle of 59.7◦ in a squint-free bandwidth of 3.9-4.5 GHz. And the simulated results show that the power-handling capacity (PHC) of the LWA is about 121 MW under the vacuum condition.

articleTitle: Simplified Method of Time-Domain Displacement Motion Recovery Using Doppler Radar Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Non-contact accurate detection system of displacement motion has a very wide range of application requirements and potential in medical health and elderly care, especially in vital signs. However, the system of radar-based precision demodulation is easily disturbed by nonlinear factors; it's also hard to achieve high linearity time-domain demodulation with low-complexity demodulation, which limits the application of radar-based detection method in practice. Based on the K-band Doppler radar sensor, this paper introduces the arc-chord approximation and automatic segmentation algorithms to present a simplified and robust demodulation system, which can achieve accurate time-domain detection of arbitrary displacement motion. Both simulation and experiments are conducted in this paper to show the effectiveness of our method. In the experiments, our method can recover 3.67-mm triangle displacement with the accuracy of relative root mean square error 4.47%. What’s more, the proposed method can recover vital sign with strong noise while traditional phase demodulation fails.

articleTitle: 2-18GHz Wide-Scan Tightly Coupled Dipole Array With Resistive FSS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An ultra-wideband (UWB) tightly coupled dipole array is proposed and investigated in this paper. The antenna element can be directly fed by a 50Ω port without a power divider due to the carefully designed folded Marchand balun with perforated stripline. A resistive frequency-selective surface (FSS) is placed between the dipole and the ground plane to suppress reflected waves, thereby widening the operational bandwidth. Furthermore, a double-layer FSS is designed at the top of the antenna to enhance the array’s scanning performance. Additionally, metallized vias are strategically positioned beneath the ground to connect the two reference grounds of the stripline, enabling the suppression of back radiation. The overall height of the design is 15.0mm (0.90 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">high</inf>). The proposed antenna achieves a voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) of less than 3 across a bandwidth of 9.5:1 (1.9-18.0GHz) when scanning up to 60° in the E-plane, and a VSWR of less than 3.1 across a bandwidth of 11.1:1 (1.8-20GHz) when scanning up to 30° in the H-plane. Finally, a 8 × 8 array prototype is presented to verify the performance.

articleTitle: A Broadband Circular Horn Antenna applied to Decoy System of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The swift advancement in science and technology, coupled with the burgeoning demand for national defense security and economic stability, has led to a substantial increase in the deployment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). However, the appearance of "black fly" UAV has given rise to a multitude of security challenges. To effectively manage and regulate the use of UAV, this paper outlines the design of a broadband horn antenna tailored for integration into a UAV decoy system. Simulation results demonstrate that the working frequency band of the designed antenna is in the range from 4.8 to 6.6 GHz with the relative bandwidth of 31.2%, the gain is greater than 10dBi, and the maximum gain is 12 dBi, the antenna is suitably equipped to satisfy the operational demands of a UAV decoy system, particularly at the 5.8 GHz frequency.

articleTitle: Broadband high-purity OAM generator based on metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A pair of mirror-symmetric meta-atom with outer arc and inner E-shaped patch is proposed. The proposed meta-atom can acquire high efficiency above 0.94 and broadband of 98%. When the rotation angle of the meta-atom changes, the reflection phase is varied over 360°and kept good linearity. With such a meta-atom, a reflective metasurface consisting of 18×18 meta-atoms are constructed, which can efficiently generate the OAM vortex beam with l= −2 under left-handed circularly polarized (LHCP) plane wave vertical incidences. The OAM mode purity higher than 66.5% from 7GHz to 22GHz (fractal bandwidth of 103%). Furthermore, the maximum mode purity is 92.2% at 15GHz.

articleTitle: Space Mapping Optimization Method for Four-Order Parallel Coupled Substrate Integrated Suspended Line Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: For substrate integrated suspended line (SISL) with complex structure, design optimization using EM simulation software requires a significant time cost. Space mapping (SM) optimization provides a solution to such problems, which can accelerate EM optimization. It has both the computational efficiency of coarse models and the accuracy of fine models. In this paper, standard SM optimization and parallel SM optimization are applied to the design optimization of the four-order parallel coupled SISL bandpass filter. The effectiveness of the SM method applied to SISL is verified through the analysis of experimental results.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Scattering of Moving Target Based on Improved SBR-PTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an improved hybrid method of shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) and physical theory of diffraction (PTD) method for the analysis of time-domain echo of moving target. Initially, the arbitrary incident pulse is decomposed into a linear superposition of plane waves. Secondly, the plane waves with different amplitudes and phases obtained by decomposition are substituted into the SBR method as the incident waves at different frequency points, combined with the quaternion and the dynamic octree algorithm, the scattering fields at different frequencies are obtained. Finally, the time domain scattering echo of the moving target can be obtained by combining the scattering fields. At the end of this paper, we compare the single-frequency RCS and time-domain echo of the moving targets with the results in the commercial software Feko, verify the accuracy of our method in the electromagnetic scattering analysis of the moving targets.

articleTitle: A 2-Bit Dual Polarized Broadband Metasurface Design for Beam Scanning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper develops a programmable reflective metasurface for wireless communication applications. A dual-polarized 2-bit unit cell composed of a center square patch surrounded by four trapezoidal patches is designed. By selectively switching the operation states of four PIN diodes inserted between the center patch and four trapezoidal patches, the reflection phase difference of 90° is obtained with the reflection magnitude better than -1.5 dB in the band of 4.5-5.5 GHz with a fraction bandwidth of 10%. The proposed unit cell is arranged into a 16-by-16 metasurface array. The simulation results demonstrate that when a horn antenna is adopted to illuminate the metasurace array, a wide beam scanning capability of ±50° is achieved through dynamic phase encoding manipulation within the array, providing an effective solution for wireless communication.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual-Band Structure-Shared Antenna for Sub-6 GHz and 5G millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a compact dual-band structure-shared antenna for sub-6 GHz and 5G millimeter-wave (MMW) applications. The antenna composites of a printed monopole structure operating in the microwave (MW) band and a SIW slot antenna operating in the 38 GHz MMW band. The structure-shared design contributes to reducing antenna size and improving space utilization. Simulation results indicate that the antenna's impedance bandwidth spans from 3.25 GHz to 6 GHz in the MW band and from 36.6 GHz to 41.2 GHz in the MMW band, with peak gain and efficiency achieved at 4.2/11.7 dBi and 96/90%, respectively. The proposed antenna shows stable radiation performance in two frequency bands. Isolation of 26 dB is achieved, ensuring the independent operation between two frequency bands and allowing for a combination of different frequency ratios.

articleTitle: Design of A Dual-band Reflect-Transmit-Array Antenna Using A Triple-layer Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel dual-band reflect-transmit-array (RTA) antenna using a triple-layer metasurface. The designed unit cell is capable of transmitting x-polarized incident waves in the 16-18 GHz band and reflecting x-polarized incident waves in the 32-34 GHz band. Additionally, the unit cell can achieve an independent 360° phase shift for both the reflection and transmission modes. The metasurface is fed by a horn antenna to construct a dual-band RTA antenna. Numerical simulation results demonstrate that the peak gain of the RTA antenna is 36.69 dBi and 31.66 dBi, with 1 dB gain bandwidth of 6.1% and 11.76% for the reflection and transmission modes, respectively.

articleTitle: Integration Designs of Waveguide Slot Array Antenna with Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents several filtering designs for waveguide slot array antennas. By incorporating various filter structures, such as metal nails, metal mushrooms, metal sheets, etc., inside or at the bottom of the waveguide slot array antenna, the antenna can exhibit stopband characteristics outside its operating frequency range. These characteristics include single stopband and dual stopband, which effectively enhance the antenna's ability to suppress out-of-band radiation without affecting its size and radiation performance.

articleTitle: Metasurface-Enabled Scanning Range Extension of a Phased Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to enhance the scanning range of phased array antenna by employing a transmissive phase gradient metasurface within a wide band. The proposed metasurface allows the incident wave to pass through it with tailored transmitted fields, thus extending the scanning range of the original phased array. As a proof of concept, a metasurface-loaded phased array antenna is designed in the Ku band, of which the maximum scanning angel is increased from 45° to 71° within a bandwidth of 2 GHz. With these merits, the proposed method may facilitate the application of metasurfaces in wide-angle scanning antenna systems.

articleTitle: Calculation of scattering characteristics of anisotropic coated targets based on SBR method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the propagation characteristics of anisotropic media are analyzed based on the layered model and generalized propagation matrix (GTM) method. Using the state vectors and coupling matrices of transverse fields in anisotropic media, GTM is introduced to obtain the reflection coefficients and transmission coefficients of layered anisotropic media, and the reflection coefficients of anisotropic media coated with a metal substrate are further deduced by using the ideal metal boundary conditions. The numerical calculations of the reflection coefficients of the multilayered anisotropic media are highly consistent with the results of commercial software. The electromagnetic propagation matrix is combined with the shooting and bouncing ray method (SBR) to obtain the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of the coated target.

articleTitle: A Monoblock Dual-Mode Dielectric Waveguide Filter With Symmetric Transmission Zeros
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a monoblock dielectric waveguide filter (DWF) with symmetric transmission zeros (TZs) based on degenerate dual-mode resonators is presented. The dual-mode dielectric waveguide resonator (DMDWR) based on the TM120 and TM210 mode consists of two pairs of blind holes located on the upper surface of the DMDWR. Resonance behaviors of the dual-mode dielectric resonator and coupling mechanisms of the proposed DMDWR are investigated. The cascaded quadruplet (CQ) topology is obtained by cascading two DMDWRs. By utilizing the frequency-variant coupling principle to realize the negative coupling of the CQ topology, and finally a 4-pole filter with two TZs on both sides of its passband is designed. The simulated results are in good agreement with the ideal synthesis results, which verifies the design concept of the DMDWR filter.

articleTitle: Design of Reconfigurable Dual Polarized Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Metagratings (MGs) are sparse arrangements of subwavelength polarizable particles (metaatoms) that have been proven to be effective in achieving various electromagnetic functions in recent years. This paper designs a reconfigurable metagrating by loading varactor diodes to achieve dynamic control of diffracted waves in two vertical planes.

articleTitle: Vanadium dioxide-based phase gradient-switchable coding metasurface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we design a phase gradient switchable coding metasurface based on vanadium dioxide (VO2). Each unit structure of the metasurface consists of three layers: a metal-VO2 composite structural layer, a polytetrafluoroethylene dielectric layer and a metal reflective layer. The metasurface utilizes the phase transition property of VO2 to dynamically reconstruct the phase gradient of the metasurface and realize the switching of two far-field beam functions. Simulation results show that when VO2 is in the insulating state, the phase difference between the units of the metasurface at 1.5 THz frequency is 90°, which can realize the anomalous deflection function of the 2-bit coding metasurface. When VO2 is transformed into a metallic state, the phase difference between the metasurfaces at the 2.1 THz frequency is 180°, which reconfigures the metasurface into a 1-bit phase-gradient coding metasurface and realizes the dual-beam beam splitting function. The phase gradient switchable coding metasurface designed in this paper enriches the flexibility of beam modulation and provides a new efficient and flexible beam modulation scheme for terahertz communication with potential applications.

articleTitle: Study on the Parasitic Effects of Yagi Antenna Based on Sub-Structure Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an improved five-element Yagi antenna with parasitic elements is designed based on the substructure characteristic mode theory (SSCMT). The antenna is composed of an active dipole, a reflector and three directors. The parasitic elements are placed near the directors. The impact of parasitic elements at different positions on the radiation performance is discussed. Parasitism of different directors can cause changes in the modal current distribution, leading to changes in modal far-field. A parasitic scheme is proposed based on the maximization of the modal current distribution of the end directors, which can maintain high gain and good directivity. The radiation performance of the proposed antenna is verified by numerical simulation. The antenna increases the bandwidth by 33MHz and the peak gain in the operating bandwidth (2.38- 2.62GHz) by 0.63dBi.

articleTitle: An Optically Controlled Active Frequency Selective Surface with Tunable Passband
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an optically controlled active frequency selective surface with a tunable passband. The passband can be continuously adjusted by varying the capacitance of varactors, which are powered by photodiodes. The design includes resistors to effectively isolate DC and high-frequency signals. The symmetrical structure ensures polarization insensitivity. The results demonstrate that the passband frequency can be continuously tuned from 5.56 GHz to 2.92 GHz, with a maximum insertion loss of less than 0.6 dB. The proposed structure introduces a novel technique for actively controlling the electromagnetic properties of frequency selective surfaces.

articleTitle: Hybrid Eccentric SIM With Embedded Ring/Separate Elliptic SEM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a complicated biaxially anisotropic multiple spectral integral method (SIM), both nested vertical multilayers and separate eccentric elliptical cylinders embedded in the same lateral layer are considered simultaneously. Furthermore, a hybrid SIM/spectral element method (SEM) is proposed, in which SIM is used as the truncated boundary condition for the discretized arbitrary anisotropic subregions by SEM. Two examples corresponding to these two methods are well matched with COMSOL respectively.

articleTitle: A C-band quad-cluster low-profile broadband circularly polarized antenna array based on sequentially rotating metasurface-based
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a metasurface-based left-handed circularly polarized (CP) sequential rotating metasurface-based (MTS) antenna array for C-band. The array comprises a cluster of 4 × 4 periodically aligned MTS cells, which exhibit excellent performance at a low profile of 0.08 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The antenna array is constructed on a Rogers RO4003 dielectric board in two layers. The upper surface of the upper layer is the MTS, the floor has a gap between the upper and lower layers, and the lower surface of the lower layer is the sequential feed network. The simulation conducted in HFSS software yielded an integrated bandwidth (IBW) of 95% (3.79-8.54 GHz) and an antenna radiation bandwidth (ARBW) of 49.8% (3.77-6.26 GHz), respectively. The dimensions of the antenna are 1.33λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 1.33λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.08λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. This configuration results in a miniaturized, compact, and low-profile antenna array. This antenna configuration is applicable to satellite communications using circularly polarized waves through MTS units.

articleTitle: A dual-band filter based on blind-vias-patterned eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide with L-shaped microstrip line
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper reports a dual-band filter using eighth-mode substrate integrated waveguide (EMSIW) and microstrip line. By patterning blind vias periodically in the conventional EMSIW cavity, the equivalent capacitance of the structure can be enlarged, thus its resonant frequency will be effectively decreased. Then, as a L-shaped microstrip line is connected with the blind-vias-patterned EMSIW, dual-mode resonance is generated and two individual passbands can be achieved. By using the EMSIW-microstrip dual-mode resonator, a dual-band filter is designed and optimized. Numerical simulations show that the dual-band filter achieve two passbands of 1.58-1.68GHz and 2.55-2.85GHz. The insertion losses are less than 2.1dB and 1.2dB, respectively, with the return losses both better than 16dB. The out-of-band rejection between the two passbands is over 16dB.

articleTitle: Fast frequency sweep technique based on subdomain method of moments and adaptive MBPE for Wideband RCS of multi-scale targets
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach of adaptive rational interpolation based on the subdomain method of moments (SMoM) and Model-Based Parameter Estimation (MBPE) to overcome the difficulties of low accuracy and inefficiency when analyzing the wideband radar scattering cross section (RCS) of multi-scale targets by traditional methods. This approach utilizes the SMoM to overcome the problem of low matrix convergence since the multi-scale target leads to the non-uniform meshes, while the adaptive rational interpolation MBPE is used to achieve accurate and efficient analysis for the wideband RCS of multi-scale targets without a priori knowledge. The numerical example verifies the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method in this paper.

articleTitle: Dual-Band and Circular-Polarization Graphene Antenna Array with Dual-Beam Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this study, we present a dual-band and circular-polarization graphene antenna array, covering both 2.45 GHz band (right-hand circular polarization) and 5.8 GHz band (left-hand circular polarization). And the antenna array has dual beams, by symmetrical arrangement of the linear array. The antenna array is fabricated by a highly conductive graphene assembly film that is lightweight, corrosion-resistant, environmentally friendly, and flexible. The proposed antenna array has characteristics of dual-band, dual circular-polarization, and dual-beam which will make it easy to be applied in future wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Research on the Electromagnetic Scattering Characteristics of Plasma Sheath by Subdomain-Level DGTD Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper developed a discontinuous Galerkin time-domain (DGTD) method to simulate the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of plasma sheath. Based on the domain decomposition technique, the computing domain is decomposed into multiple subdomains. To handle the dispersion properties of plasma in the time domain, we introduced the electrical flux density to construct an auxiliary differential equation (ADE). Finally, the scattering characteristics of a plasma sheath coated blunt cone is studied by the proposed method.

articleTitle: Dual-band Antenna Based on Glide-Symmetric Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: T-shaped glide symmetric double-layer unit is proposed. Such unit exhibits stronger field confinement and higher degrees of freedom in modulating dispersion characteristics. Besides the basic transmission characteristic, additional radiation characteristic based on such T-shaped glide symmetric double-layer units performs well with continuously beam scanning in a large frequency and angle range. Experimental results agree well with numerical simulations, demonstrating the superior performance of T-shaped glide symmetric double-layer Spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs). The radiation method of such T-shaped glide symmetric double layer SSPPs can be applied to antenna design, which is conductive to the development of highly compact plasmonic integrated circuits and systems.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Leaky-wave Endfire Antenna Using Multipole Element
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an all-metal high-gain backward endfire leaky-wave antenna (LWA), which is composed of densely and uniformly arranged dipoles fed by double-sided parallel-strip lines (DSPSL). Different from the conventional LWA, its element is a highly directional endfire multipole which is formed by densely placed dipoles with precise feed phase. The feed phase inversion is achieved through the spiral inversion of DSPSL, meeting the phase requirements of both the element and the array. The dipole unit design includes a parasitic structure to improve the impedance matching between the dipole and DSPSL, and to reduce the mutual coupling between elements, thereby enhancing radiation efficiency and directivity. The proposed antenna achieves a realized gain of 16.7 dBi within an array length of 4.8, a high front-to-back ratio (FTBR) of 28 dB, and a maximum relative sidelobe level of -16 dB at 1 GHz with a 3 dB endfire gain bandwidth of 5.4%.

articleTitle: Phase-Coherent Signal Generation Based on Single-Sideband Time-Modulator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A method for achieving an 8-channel phase-coherent signal source through time modulation is proposed. Utilizing a power divider to split the signal into multiple paths and designing the control timing design of the single-sideband time modulation (SSBTM) module to achieve phase control of the radio frequency (RF) signals, thereby obtaining a phase-coherent signal source. The phase differences of two channel is measured with the root means square errors (RMSE) of 0.30° and maximum error of 0.68° from 300MHz to 3GHz.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Method of Asymptotic Waveform Estimation and Hierarchical Matrix for Fast Acquisition of Broadband RCS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A hybrid method combining asymptotic waveform estimation (AWE) technique and hierarchical matrix is proposed for calculating broadband RCS. Compared with traditional AWE, when calculating the coefficients of the derivatives of the impedance matrix, a hierarchically off-diagonal low-rank (HODLR) is introduced to calculate the inverse matrix of the impedance matrix, greatly reducing calculation time. Numerical example show that the proposed method effectively improves computational efficiency without losing accuracy.

articleTitle: Design Approach of Wide-band and Wide-beam Antenna for The Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the rapid development of wireless communication technology, the antenna with wide-bandwidth and wide-beamwidth are widely used in radar and satellite communication systems. Due to this background, a new design method is proposed to enhance the beamwidth of the printed dipole antenna, thus to achieving the wide beam scanning for the phased array in this paper. Herein, we use the folded printed dipole to achieve the wide-beamwidth and wide-bandwidth simultaneously. Meanwhile, the parasitic elements are introduced to further improve its beamwidth at E-plane. Based on this element, the array antenna with eight dipole is constructed to realize the high gain performance, and the active VSWR of the proposed antenna is also reduced down. Based on the above results, the VSWR and active VSWR of the antenna are kept of less than 4.2 and 2.9 in the operating band of 8 ~ 12GHz, respectively. Meanwhile, the antenna has realized the wide beam scanning performance as desired.

articleTitle: Mechanical Accuracy Measurement of the PNF Scanner : A comprehensive analysis of the PNF scanner accuracy around the world
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper discusses the mechanical accuracy of the PNF scanner including the accuracy measurement and evaluation method which is based on the project experience from NSI-MI, MVG Orbit and LT. There is some difference from each based on different data process theory. And the real measure data from the tangle project is attached for reference.

articleTitle: A Higher-Order Local Interpolation/Anterpolation Scheme of MLFMA for Computing Electromagnetic Scattering by Low RCS Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Realistic electromagnetic (EM) scattering problems often consist targets or structures aiming to reduce radar cross section (RCS) at some angle ranges, generating a challenge for the interpolation/anterpolation schemes of MLFMA. In this paper, we demonstrate that for a specially designed low RCS object, traditional local interpolation schemes using 4×4 samples cannot guarantee satisfactory accuracy. To remedy this, a higher-order Lagrangian interpolation scheme is proposed, whose performance is verified by numerical results. The proposed scheme has been used to calculate real-life EM scattering problem with coated cavities, nonconformal mesh grids and unknowns exceeding 48 million.

articleTitle: Design of W-band pixelated programmable metasurface for flexible beam steering
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: We proposed a two-dimensional pixelated programmable metasurface (PPM) specifically designed for W-band operations. This PPM uses PIN diodes and a simple architecture to realize accurate 0/180° phase control at each element. The meticulously designed 20×20 elements PPM array demonstrate robust beamforming capabilities, effectively beam steering within ±45° in both the E-plane and H-plane. This advancement establishes a crucial foundation for the enhancement of future millimeter-wave wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: Efficient ISAR Image Prediction Method for Multi-Target Through Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In highly dynamic multi-target scenes, inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging has important effects on analyzing electromagnetic scattering characteristics of clustered targets, which are composed of the electromagnetic scattering characteristics of each single target and the coupling characteristics between targets. Considering that simulation calculation of the coupling characteristics is time-consuming, it cannot meet the needs of real-time calculation of multi-target ISAR images. To address the issue, this paper proposes a deep neural network (DNN) based on U-Net, which predicts the ISAR images of the multi-target scene from the ISAR image of each single target. Compared with physical optics (PO) simulation and range-Doppler (R-D) imaging methods, the proposed DNN can achieve a 99% speed increase while maintaining a mean square error (MSE) of 0.21.

articleTitle: A Decoupling Structure of Ultra-wideband based on Planar Spiral Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a high-isolation ultra-wideband (UWB) circularly polarized (CP) dual-element antenna array is introduced in this article. Firstly, a square planar spiral antenna that has stable gain, axial ratio (AR) < 3 dB and VSWR < 2 over 4 – 10 GHz is proposed, secondly, a "glasses"-shaped frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed to analyze the reflection & transmission of its unit and eliminate the spatial-wave coupling. The periodic isolation network can effectively improve the isolation level of 4 – 10 GHz up to 13.5 dBi, with little impact on antenna's pattern and gain.

articleTitle: Design of Wide Band Rectangular-Shaped Antenna Array for 5 G mmwave Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband mmWave antenna array for 5G network. The proposed single element is designed on Rogers 5880 substrate having dimensions of 8×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, it is then converted into a four elements array system with an entire size of 15×26 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A single element is rectangulary designed which is tranformed into 1×4 array to achieve high gain. The rectangular patch and half ground plane are truncated in the top middles. The proposed antenna array operates in the Kaband, covering a wide band from 24 GHz to 40 GHz, including the 28 GHz and 38 GHz licensed bands for 5G communications. The peak gains of the single element and four elements array are 4.1 dB and 7.3 dB at 28 GHz and 4.3 and 8.5 at 38 GHz, respectively. Features such as simple design, compact size, wide bandwidth and high gain make it a suitable candidate for fifth-generation (5G) communication systems.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Omni-directional Antenna Works in the VHF and UHF Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A new structure of ultra-wideband vertical polarization omni-directional antenna for very-high frequency (VHF) and ultra-high frequency (UHF) bands is proposed in this letter. The antenna consists of two dipoles for high and low frequency bands which are coaxially nested. The antenna achieves ultra-wideband and the high radiation gain in the horizontal plane by using slot coupling, radiator reuse, asymmetric and gradient structure. The simulated results show that the ultra-wideband vertical polarization omni-directional antenna designed based on this method can achieve a relative bandwidth of 1:10.

articleTitle: Finite Element Boundary Integral Method to Calculate Eddy Current Responses
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a numerical simulation for eddy current responses is carried out using the finite element boundary integral (FEBI) method. The finite element method (FEM) is applied to deal with the interior of the object, and the boundary integral method (BIM) is applied as the boundary condition for the solution domain of the FEM method. The iterative method is applied to solve the discretized matrix obtained by FEBI. The eddy current responses, which are the impedance variations of the object under detect, are calculated by the Auld formulation. By testing the benchmark problem, the results achieved by FEBI are compared with those by other methods, which prove that FEBI can simulate the responses of eddy currents both accurately and efficiently.

articleTitle: Research on the Electrical Performance of Deformable Radomes
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Under the influence of airflow, the radome fitted in supersonic aircraft will deform, further affecting the electrical performance of the antenna system. In order to explore the impact of deformation, this article first uses Abaqus software to simulate the force that act on the radome and obtains the deformed radome. Afterwards, electromagnetic simulation is performed on the deformed radome to study the electrical performance changes caused by deformation.

articleTitle: Mechanically Reconfigurable Metasurfaces Enabled by Bianisotropic Effect in 3D Curved Conformal Meta-atoms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The manipulation of electromagnetic wavefronts using metasurfaces has garnered significant attention and found numerous applications. Recently, the focus has shifted towards reconfigurable metasurfaces, yet achieving dynamic control over their bianisotropy remains challenging. In this study, we propose a novel approach utilizing a 3D curved rotating magnetoelectric system. By manipulating the lateral length, radius, and gap of split ring resonators, we demonstrate the ability to modulate frequency. Additionally, we analyze the asymmetric reflection properties of the rotating metasurface and calculate its bianisotropy in multiple scattering scenarios. Finally, we showcase the utility of this rotating system for beam steering. Our findings suggest promising implications for communication and imaging technologies.

articleTitle: Broadband and Wide-Angle Absorber Based on Indium Tin Oxide Films
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel broadband and wide-angle absorber constructed from indium tin oxide (ITO) films, designed via a multi-objective optimization algorithm. The absorber, based on a lossy frequency selective surface with multiple layers, utilizes multilayer absorption equations and equivalent circuit models to calculate its absorptive properties. Addressing issues of bandwidth and thickness imbalance in the structure, the optimization algorithm adjusts the geometric dimensions and sheet resistance parameters. The resulting multilayer absorber achieves a 90% absorption bandwidth across a frequency range of 2-18 GHz and supports incidence angle up to 45 degrees. Remarkably, its overall thickness corresponds to only 0.133 times the wavelength, rendering it highly suitable for applications in stealth technology and electromagnetic shielding.

articleTitle: Fabrication Challenges and Performance Optimization of Inclined 2D Lithium Niobate PhC Waveguides
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we design and simulate a 2D Lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) based photonic crystal (PhC) waveguide with an Inclination angle. Additionally, the challenges associated with the fabrication process are also discussed. This study aims to provide key insights into designing advanced photonic devices that take advantage of the unique properties of Lithium niobate (LiNbO₃) and precise structural design.

articleTitle: A Study of the Near Singularity Problem in the High-Order Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A method is proposed for evaluating near-singular integrals in the context of a high-order method of moments (MoM) for surface integral equations (SIE). In particular, the method is tailored towards the specific challenges associated with high-order elements and high-order basis functions. The method works for kernels with weak $\left( {\frac{1}{R}} \right)$ and strong $\left( {\nabla \frac{1}{R}} \right)$ singularity, and exhibits excellent efficiency and accuracy.

articleTitle: The RCS of a dipole-incidence inhomogeneous plasma coated missile and sharp cone target
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the RCS of a dipole-incidence inhomogeneous plasma coated missile and sharp cone target are calculated by using Po method. The effects of dipole distance, plasma parameters and incident wave frequency on the RCS of the target are analyzed. The results show that the RCS of the target can be reduced by coating the surface of the target with inhomogeneous plasma layer. Moreover, when the dipole incidence distance is far enough, the dipole incidence on the target degrades to plane wave incidence on the target.

articleTitle: A low-noise amplifier for wearable Beidou system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The article designs a high gain, low noise amplifier that can cover all frequency bands of the Beidou navigation system. The circuit is implemented using three-stage amplification. The simulation results show that in the operating frequency band of 1.1-1.6GHz, the in band return loss is better than 10dB, the power gain is greater than 40dB, the noise coefficient is less than 1dB, and the area is 3.5mm × 2mm. This circuit achieves miniaturization while maintaining good circuit stability, and can meet the working requirements of Beidou wearable antennas.

Author Keywords: RF receiver and wearable Beidou antenna

articleTitle: Efficiently Simulate Anisotropic Graphene and Plasma Based Structures by An Improved ADI-FDTD
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The transmission properties of graphene-based structure with a plasma substrate are effectively simulated by the proposed improved alternating-direction-implicit finite-difference time-domain algorithm (ADI-FDTD). With two extra sub-time steps added, the developed method can precisely and efficiently simulate the anisotropic objects with fine structures. It is used to compute the transmission coefficient of an infinitely wide magnetized plasma slab. It is shown that the proposed method can maintain high accuracy by taking a large timestep. Further, the static electromagnetic field-biased graphene-plasma-based structures are studied. Numerical results show that the adjusted transmission characteristics can be investigated efficiently and effectively.

articleTitle: Design of A 2.45 GHz RFID Vortex Wave Antenna based on Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multimode vortex electromagnetic wave antenna for 2.45 GHz radio frequency identification (RFID) applications is proposed. Characteristic mode theory is used to analyze the characteristic currents of the array element column antenna so as to reduce the coupling between the array elements. The simulation results demonstrate that the return loss of a single array element and the whole array reach -26.14 dB and -25.85 dB, respectively, indicating excellent performance. Furthermore, both the antenna array element and the entire array are capable of functioning effectively within the 2.45 GHz band. The helical structure of each pattern is clearly discernible, indicating optimal performance characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Scattering Effects of one-dimensional Moving Dusty Plasma
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this study, we utilize the theory of weakly ionized dusty plasma to determine the relative permittivity of the plasma plate and calculate its reflection, transmission, and absorption coefficients at various velocities using the Lorentz-FDTD method. The results indicate that as the velocity increases, the reflection and absorption coefficients increase, while the transmission coefficient decreases.

articleTitle: High Efficient Automatic Test Method for SIP Products
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to satisfy the requirement of temperature test for (System In a Package) SIP products, a high efficiency automatic test sorting system for temperature is developed. To solve the problem of low efficiency of temperature test for SIP products, select the temperature change module to open the sealed heat preservation cavity to realize local temperature control and avoid affecting the running accuracy of the device. The automatic manipulator and high-precision visual recognition system are selected, and the adjustable automatic rotating tray is adopted to realize the automatic temperature test of SIP products. Finally, assist data processing program, automatically generate test report. Finally, the temperature automatic test and sorting system is developed, which is unattended for 24 hours and increased the test efficiency by 350%.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Incoherent Scattering Spectra of Magnetized Plasma in the Middle and Low Latitude Ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Incoherent scattering technique is an important means of detecting ionospheric plasma parameters. Based on Sheffield’s incoherent scattering theory, this paper analyzed the incoherent scattering spectra of ionospheric plasmas at middle and low latitudes. We first give the incoherent scattering properties of plane waves in the magnetized ionospheric plasma. Then we study the spectral line characteristics of the actual ionospheric parameters in different latitude and longitude regions based on the actual ionospheric parameters. The higher the latitude, the higher the magnetic field intensity and the electron density. At the same latitude, the electron temperature, ion temperature and the electron density are proportional to the height, and the magnetic field intensity is inversely proportional to the ionosphere height. For the ion line spectra, different latitude has little effect on the line. In general, the peak value of the spectral lines increases slightly with the increase of latitude. For the plasma line spectra, the higher the latitude, the peak value of the spectral line moves to the right, and the peak value in the F-layer increases obviously. The work in this paper lays a foundation for further study of the incoherent scattering characteristics of plasma, and is helpful to promote the development of the plasma diagnosis.

articleTitle: Multifrequency Electromagnetic Inversion Based on Early Fusion Deep Learning Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper utilizes the early fusion deep learning framework (EFF) to address real-time multifrequency electromagnetic (EM) inverse scattering problems (ISPs) with heightened precision. The EFF incorporates both the scattered field encoder (SFE) and the backpropagation encoder (BPE). his fusion involves amalgamating the extracted features of the scattered field and the BP method across various frequencies, thereby capturing multiple scattering phenomena more comprehensively during the solving process. Additionally, it has been observed that the mutual regularization of multiple scattering information and BP distributions effectively enhances the encoding process, leading to accelerated convergence and more stable inversion results. Moreover, the multifrequency data provide more adequate information in the solving process, and effectively improve the performance of EFF. The superior veracity, stability and generalization ability of the multifrequency EFF have been demonstrated by the synthetic results.

articleTitle: Photonic Nanojet Generated by a Coated Hemisphere with Tunable Core
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Photonic nanojets are generally generated by a dielectric microcylinder or dielectric microsphere illuminated by a plane wave. When the plane wave incident on the microsphere, the parallel components of the wave vector cancel each other out, and the perpendicular component has a very long scale due to the superposition effect. Therefore, in the backward direction of the microsphere, we get a focusing spot with a transverse scale smaller than the wavelength and a longitudinal scale of several wavelengths, which is the photonic nanojet, and it can greatly enhance the field strength on the basis of the incident field [1]. Such high-intensity photonic jets are diffraction-free, high-intensity, and able to break through the diffraction limit, and this phenomenon is now widely used in optical imaging [2 - 5], optical tweezers [6 - 8], nanolithography [9 - 10], and optical switches [11]. Without changing the incident field parameters, the morphology of the photon jet is most affected by the scattering object. Therefore, this paper discusses the influence of the radius of the scattering hemisphere on the morphology of the photon jet based on the finite difference frequency domain (FDFD) method. It has some application prospects in the design of optical devices such as optical tweezers.

articleTitle: Design of High Isolation Terminal Multiple Antennas Based on Characteristic Mode Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Two Inverted-F Antennas (IFA) with high isolation is proposed based on characteristic mode analysis (CMA). By manipulating the resonance frequencies and mode weight coefficients (MWC) of two specific modes, both can be simultaneously excited. This ensures the creation of a current null zone at the opposite port when feeding a single port, effectively achieving decoupling. The proposed antenna operates within the range of 1.89-1.93GHz, exhibiting in-band isolation improvement from 9dB to exceeding 20dB. At the resonant frequency of 1.91GHz, the isolation reaches a maximum of 25dB.

articleTitle: An extremely low-profile wideband patch antenna for 5G smartphones
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, an extremely low-profile and broadband multimode microstrip antenna is proposed for fifth-generation mobile applications. By cutting two unsymmetrical slots and loading two metallic vias on the microstrip antenna, the TM10 and Anti-TM10 mode are excited simultaneously to achieve the broadband operation in an extremely low-profile of 0.9 mm. The volume of the proposed antenna is 31.3×30.3×0.9 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The simulated results show that the antenna has the bandwidth of 4.25-5.07 GHz, covering the 5G N79 band. The proposed antenna has the advantage of low-profile, large bandwidth, high total efficiency, providing a feasible solution of 5G mobile phone antenna on the back cover of the device.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of the Reactive Energy and Q-Factor of Small Antennas
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper aims to accurately calculate the reactive energy and determine the Q factor of small antennas using numerical calculation methods. The traditional approach of integrating the reactive energy density over the entire space around the antenna leads to infinite value. The integration domain also needs to be truncated. The numerical accuracy and efficiency are generally not satisfactory. This paper adopts an alternative formula where the reactive energy is explicitly defined over the source region. The numerically evaluated reactive energy is finite and independent of coordinate systems.

articleTitle: A Wearable All-Textile Filtering Antenna with High Selectivity for 2.4-GHz ISM Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wearable all-textile filtering antenna with high selectivity is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna is composed of a rectangular patch etched with two slots and four parasitic strips. Two radiation nulls at the both band edge of the antenna gain curve are realized by the slots and the parasitic strips. The frequency of two radiation nulls can be flexibly controlled by the length of slots and the length of strips. The proposed antenna has a -10dB impedance bandwidth of 10.2% (2.31-2.56GHz), which effectively covers the 2.4-GHz ISM band. The antenna has a very flat gain with the average of 7.2 dBi within the frequency range of 2.36 to 2.51GHz. The suppression level of the out of band gain on both sides is more than 13.5 dB. The lower and upper band selectivities are both of 212.5dB/GHz.

articleTitle: An Integrated Wideband SIW Horn Antenna for Applications in X and Ku Bands
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an integrated broadband horn antenna for the X and Ku bands is proposed. By loading a double-sided parallel-strip line (DSPSL) structure with slots on the extended substrate of the Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) horn antenna, the impedance characteristics at low frequencies are adjusted, and high-frequency resonant mode is introduced, effectively broadening the antenna’s operating frequency range. By integrating a Defected Ground Structure (DGS) around the horn aperture, the backward radiation of the antenna is significantly reduced, enhancing its radiation performance. Ultimately, the proposed antenna achieves a relative bandwidth of 70.3% in a compact size of 1.39λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.79λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.16λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, along with stable end-fire radiation performance and moderate gain. These features make the proposed antenna highly suitable for conformal integration on small aircraft.

articleTitle: Asymmetric square-slotted conformal antenna for GPS applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a circularly polarized(CP) conformal microstrip patch antenna with asymmetric rectangular slots is designed for GPS systems. Sequential embedding of four asymmetric rectangular slots in a circular patch to excite two orthogonal modes of CP radiation and reduce antenna size. Four symmetric slits are symmetrically embedded along the orthogonal directions of the asymmetric rectangular slotted patch to further reduce the antenna size. The shape of the antenna is conformal to the surface of the cylinder, allowing the antenna to be integrated within the body of the cylindrical carrier. The realized antenna is measured the 10 dB impedance bandwidth of this antenna is 11 MHz (1.571~1.582 GHz) and the 3 dB axial-ratio(AR) bandwidth is 10 MHz (1.573~1.583 GHz) .

articleTitle: A Wide-Beamwidth Dual-circularly Polarized Microstrip Patch Antenna with Stable Radiation Pattern for K-band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A beamwidth broadening structure of microstrip patch antenna is presented, which can effectively broaden the antenna beamwidth. It is different from the general microstrip antenna beamwidth that decreases with the increase of frequency, and has a stable radiation pattern. The proposed microstrip antenna is surrounded by an un-grounded parasitic metal vias, and the beamwidth increases from 88° to more than 120° in its operating bandwidth form 19.3GHz to 20.9GHz. The beamwidth of the antenna is significantly improved, and is stable with the change of frequency, the realized gain fluctuation is small. That is, it has a stable radiation pattern, which has the advantage of being applied to the wide-angle scanning phased array.

articleTitle: Energy-Selective Surface Absorbing In-Band and Out-of-Band High Power Microwave
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: An adaptive double-layer energy-selective surface is designed, consisting of an energy selective/absorption layer and an energy selective layer. It can absorb in-band and out-of-band high power microwave. The simulation results show that the insertion loss of the ESS unit is less than 1 dB for low-power signals in the range of 4.9-5.3 GHz and two absorption peaks are observed at 3 GHz and 6.57 GHz. When exposed to HPM, the shielding effectiveness is more than 20 dB and an absorption band range of 3.25-6.7 GHz is obtained. This novel ESS simultaneously achieves protection and stealth for high-power electromagnetic (EM) in a wide band.

articleTitle: Improving the Radiation Efficiency of Terahertz Photoconductive Antenna with Hierarchical Spoof Plasmonic Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To improve the output power of the Photoconductive Antenna (PCA), one of the most widely used radiation sources of the Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy system, a design scheme for PCA based on hierarchical spoof plasmonic structures is proposed. Hierarchical structures are composed of the golden nanorod array and periodic micro-gratings. The theory and simulation results show that the golden nanorod array achieves near-field enhancement and photon-electron conversion efficiency improvement through spoof localized surface plasmon resonance effect, and the periodic micro-gratings improve vertical directivity of PCA by suppressing horizontal leakage with the forbidden band of the fundamental spoof surface plasmon polariton mode. Numerical calculation results further validate that compared with the unmodified PCA, hierarchical spoof plasmonic structures achieve vertical radiation power density improvement of PCA in a relatively broad band from 0.86 to 1.51 THz.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach to Time-Domain Electromagnetic Modeling Based on Dynamic Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a data-driven methodology that utilizes Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) for the time-domain (TD) electromagnetic (EM) modeling of microwave devices. As an unsupervised machine learning technique, DMD leverages a limited set of unlabeled spatio-temporal electromagnetic (EM) data to determine DMD eigenvalues and eigenmodes. Then, the obtained DMD model reconstructs the dynamics as a series of exponential terms based on linear assumptions. The effectiveness of this approach is demonstrated through the TD EM modeling of photonic crystal waveguides. Comparative analysis with the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method shows that the DMD model not only achieves precise modeling but also facilitates robust short-term forecasting.

articleTitle: A Folded Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity Slot Filtenna with Controllable Nulls and Low Cross Polarization
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a folded substrate integrated waveguide (FSIW) cavity slot filtenna with controllable nulls and low cross polarization. The antenna is composed of a folded substrate integrated waveguide resonant cavity, a radiating slot etched on the top layer, and three types of metal vias. And it utilizes coaxial feeding. The antenna has a center frequency of 5.73 GHz and a 10 dB impedance bandwidth ranging from 5.41 GHz to 6.05 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of 11.17%. It exhibits excellent radiation performance within the frequency band and achieves an out-of-band suppression greater than 20 dB. The isolation between main polarization and cross polarization is greater than -30dB.

articleTitle: A Wideband SIW Filtering Antenna with Multiple Radiation Nulls
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a broadband filtering antenna based on substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. The antenna consists of an SIW resonant cavity, a circular patch, and a complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR) on the ground. The antenna is fed diagonally and two slits are opened on the top layer to generate perturbation effects, splitting the cavity radiation mode. Two slots are opened on the patch to split the patch radiation mode. The combined radiation of the cavity and patch achieves a wider impedance bandwidth. Opening a complementary resonant split ring on the ground further expands the bandwidth. Simulation results indicate that the antenna has a wideband and good filtering effect.

articleTitle: A Novel Double-Sided Printed Omnidirectional Antenna with Broad Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel printed omnidirectional antenna. It consists of two FR4 dielectric substrates, each of which is printed on one side with different radiation units. Each radiating unit comprises two symmetrical monopole antenna arms, with the upper and lower radiating units forming a set of symmetrical dipole antennas. Additionally, the shape of each monopole is altered to enhance the radiation performance. The connection between the feedline and the arms is made by a stepped impedance converter to improve the broadband characteristics of the antenna. A gap is left between the top and bottom plates to introduce an air layer to improve the antenna radiation performance. The -10 dB bandwidth of the antenna simulation is 15.6% (from 2.66 GHz to 3.11 GHz, centered at 2.885 GHz), demonstrating excellent omni-directional radiation characteristics within this frequency range.

articleTitle: A Longitudinally Miniaturized SIW H-Plane Horn Antenna With Flat-Top Beam
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A longitudinally miniaturized substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) H-plane horn antenna with flat-top beam (FTB) is proposed in this paper. The metal-via arrays are used to adjust the amplitude and phase of the horn aperture to achieve the FTB. The metal strips are aimed at impedance matching and gain improvement. The length reduction of the waveguide can further widen the 1dB beamwidth of FTB. Longitudinal miniaturization and FTB of SIW H-plane horn antenna are simultaneously implemented. The longitudinal length of the proposed horn is reduced by about 60%, and an FTB in the angle range of ±45 degrees is obtained, with the fluctuation less than 1 dB.

articleTitle: Broadband Absorptive Frequency Selective Rasorber With Unidirectional Transmission Window
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel broadband frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with unidirectional transmission window is investigated. It is designed to transmit y-polarized waves with polarization conversion along the +z direction, while simultaneously absorb y-polarized waves across a wide frequency band along the -z direction. The FSR is a composite structure consisting of an upper lossy layer and a lower absorptive transmission-reflection surface (ATRS). The upper layer incorporates two concentric square resonators and four lumped resistors to enable absorption across both low- and high-frequency bands. The ATRS is comprised of three metallic layers, with upper and lower layers consisting of triangle patches connected by a via. A cross slot is etched on the top patch, and three lumped resistors are integrated to facilitate absorption at middle-frequency band. The proposed FSR achieves a wide absorption band in 4.28-25.65 GHz (142.8%) and a wide polarization-conversion transmission band (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>|> -3dB) within the range of 14.47-22.53 GHz (43.57%) according to simulation results.

articleTitle: A Wide-angle Low-scattering Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A new design method for wide-angle radar cross section (RCS) reduction for both co- and cross-polarizations is presented based on characteristic mode theory (CMT) and frequency selective surface (FSS). Taking the modal amplitude as the important mode selecting criterion, the important scattering and radiating modes are analyzed for a microstrip antenna. By cutting off the scattering modal currents, the wide-angle RCS reduction (RCSR) except the normal angle is obtained for co-polarization. Then, the FSS structure is used on the ground plane to reduce wide-angle RCS for cross-polarization and normal angular RCS for co-polarization. A wide-angle low-scattering microstrip antenna is achieved for both co- and cross-polarizations. For the co-polarization, it can realize RCSR from 0° to 90°, and the average and peak reductions are 6dB and 15 dB respectively. For the cross-polarization, it can realize low-RCS from 0° to 90°, and the average RCSR is 6dB. In the meantime, its transmission and radiation performances keep well.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method of Five-Order SISL Microstrip Bandpass Filter Using Mesh Deformation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the size information of a five-order microstrip bandpass filter with simplified shielded SISL structure has been designed optimally using the method of mesh deformation. There are many ways to optimise the response of a filter with simplified SISL structure, and mesh deformation is one of them. Firstly, the electromagnetic field information of the simplified SISL structure is analysed by FEM, and then the dimensions of the SISL structure are changed using mesh deformation and the design is optimised to meet the specified design specifications. An example of a Five-order SISL microstrip bandpass filter is given in this paper, and using the method of this paper, it is much faster compared to the direct optimisation of the structure in HFSS.

articleTitle: A novel harmonic emission source locating algorithm based on Pearson correlation coefficient
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Harmonic emission sources are a common source of interference that can damage the normal circuit boards. It will spread interference in space in the form of electromagnetic waves, affecting the normal operation of the circuit board. This paper proposes a method based on the emission results obtained by the near-field electric field probe, and the harmonic fundamental frequency is known. The Pearson correlation coefficient is used to determine the correlation of the harmonic characteristics of each point on the PCB circuit board, and the convex hull algorithm is used to finally determine the harmonic emission. This method reflects the spectrum correlation of different positions and can offset the interference of environmental noise to a certain extent. Compared with the traditional method, this method can also locate the emission area of the harmonic emission source on the PCB board, achieving better visualization and facilitating electromagnetic compatibility rectification. This method was specifically implemented on an actual measurement result and achieved good results.

articleTitle: One Real Time Detection and Positioning Method for Ground Targets by Unmanned Aerial Vehicles based on GNSS, MEMS, and Machine Vision Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Ground target point positioning is an important function of unmanned aerial vehicle battlefield reconnaissance. Target point positioning requires high real-time and positioning accuracy. The objective of the paper is the real-time target positioning method of the unmanned aerial vehicles, which adopts the multiple information fusion methods. And the correction methods for coordinate errors in the method.A real-time using multiple information fusion method is proposed in the paper, the correction method for reducing coordinate errors is also proposed.The actual measurement results show that based on the above method, the target positioning accuracy has been significantly improved compared to traditional aerial target positioning methods. The oblique target positioning error can be controlled within 5 meters, and the vertical target positioning error is basically close to the GNSS error. This method will greatly improve the real-time performance and target positioning accuracy of unmanned aerial vehicle reconnaissance targets.

articleTitle: High-performance compact range test antenna for FR2 band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a highly efficient Compact Antenna Test Range (CATR) antenna operating in the 24GHz52GHz band. The main body of the reflector is a parabolic surface, with its extended part mixed with elliptical curved edges. The parameters of the mixed curved edges are optimized using the particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm to produce minimal diffraction fields under design constraints. The feed employs an axially slotted corrugated horn, characterized by a wide beam, low cross-polarization, and symmetrical wideband radiation patterns. The designed compact field antenna was simulated using FEKO software. Simulation results indicate that the antenna's aperture efficiency is as high as 53% and it exhibits excellent quiet zone performance, providing new insights and methods for OTA testing.

articleTitle: Mechanical-electro-thermal coupling analysis of 3D RF MEMS-BAW filters chip based on the FEM method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article presents a mechanical-electro-thermal multi-physical field analysis method for three-dimensional (3D) bulk acoustic wave (BAW) filter modeling. Based on the finite element method (FEM), the energy dissipation problem caused by the electrode loss on the chip in the 3D BAW filter model is investigated. Firstly, the 3D multi-order filter is modeled and simulated, so that the impedance curves of each resonator unit are obtained by mechanical-electro coupling simulation. Secondly, the electromagnetic simulation is carried out to get the S-parameters of the filter through the transformed dielectric constant, the simulation calculation results are compared with the test data. Finally, the electromagnetic-thermal simulation shows the effect of loss on the chip, to investigate the mechanical-electro-thermal coupling effect in the RF BAW filter.

articleTitle: Fast Analysis of Characteristic Modes Using Hybrid Integral Equation Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To expedite the characteristic mode analysis (CMA) of electromagnetic target structures, this paper combines frequency- and material-independent reactions (FMIR) with characteristic mode analysis using the volume-surface integral equation (VSIE). Although the CMA based on VSIE is not affected by spurious modes when calculating targets containing dielectric, its matrix is high dimensional, resulting in slower calculations. FMIR only needs to store the calculation once for matrices that are independent of frequency and material parameters, which greatly reduces the repetitive operations when calculating multi-frequency impedance matrices. Numerical results show that combining FMIR with the CMA using VSIE can effectively improve the computational speed.

articleTitle: Design of Highly Selective Filtering Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a highly selective filtering antenna module based on LTCC process is designed to cascade a single-layer six-cavity dielectric filtering with a microstrip patch antenna array through a one-part-four T-shaped power divider, and a Ferro-A6M sheet with a thickness of 0.47 mm is used as the dielectric. A CQ topology is used to introduce cross-coupling, which generates transmission zeros at both ends of the passband and improves out-of-band rejection. The module as a whole achieves a return loss of less than -10.5 dB in the N257 band from 27 GHz to 29 GHz, a maximum antenna gain of 9.4 dBi at the center frequency, which is suitable for millimeter-wave communications because of its high selectivity and high out-of-band rejection.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Dipole Antenna with Wide-Beam and High-Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a radiation pattern reconfigurable dipole antenna with two radiation modes: a wide-beam mode and a high-gain mode. The switching between these modes is achieved through the use of photodiodes. Both modes operate at a center frequency of 1.57GHz. In the wide-beam mode, the half-power beamwidth (HPBW) in the E-plane is larger than 135°, while the maximum gain of the high-gain mode is 4.9dBi.

articleTitle: A Back-Cover Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This article proposes a leaky-wave antenna based on spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP), featuring an extremely low profile that allows it to be placed on the back cover of a mobile phone. The antenna’s -10dB bandwidth covers 23-30 GHz, including the n257 and n258 frequency bands of 5G. Operating in the millimeter-wave frequency range, this antenna does not occupy the space traditionally used by antennas on the phone frame, offering significant potential for 5G communication technology.

articleTitle: Multi-Link Empowered ISAC Mechanism based on Multiple Radar Subbands Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a dual-link cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) mechanism. Specifically, two transmitters simultaneously send integrated signals across different frequency bands for both sensing and data communication. For radar sensing, the receiver employs multi-band fusion technology to combine the received echo signals into an ultra-wideband (UWB) signal. For communication, the two signals can serve different users by separately modulating the information required by each user. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed mechanism achieves performance gains in both sensing and communication functions by embedding communication information into specific radar signals. This integration allows for efficient utilization of resources and improved performance in both radar sensing and communication tasks.

articleTitle: Analysis of Periodic Arrays Using Characteristic Mode Basis Function Method Combined with Sampling Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To address the issues of low efficiency of the traditional method of moments (MoM) in analyzing the scattering properties of periodic electromagnetic arrays, the characteristic mode basis function method based on block theory is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the target is divided into multiple identical unit cells, and the characteristic modes are extracted from the self-impedance matrix established on the single unit cell. Secondly the characteristic modes are sorted, and the appropriate thresholds are selected to partition the characteristic modes series. Thirdly, the entire eigenvectors corresponding to in-band characteristic modes, and the eigenvectors corresponding to out-of-band characteristic modes obtained by uniformly sampled are selected to form the basis functions collectively. Finally, the constructed basis functions are utilized to reduce the dimension of the original impedance matrix. Numerical results demonstrate that compared to the traditional MoM, the proposed method exhibits higher computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Monostatic RCS Simulation of Simple Targets in a Terahertz Compact Range
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Introducing a radar cross section (RCS) measurement system based on a tri-reflector compact antenna test range (CATR) system. Using the output field of the tri-reflector CATR system as the incident wave, simulate the RCS of the dihedral reflector and sphere. The simulations are carried out at the radar frequency of 100 GHz. Comparing the simulation results with theoretical calculations and those obtained under ideal plane wave illumination. There is an acceptable agreement within the results The output field of the tri-reflector CATR system is obtained in GRASP, while the RCS of the target is obtained in FEKO.

articleTitle: A Design of Wideband Conformal Discone Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The antenna usually needs to be installed in the cavity to achieve conformal design with the platform. But it usually affects the radiation performance of the antenna. In this paper, an antenna is designed in the cavity. It is composed of a traditional discone antenna, a short-circuited configuration, a double-plate structure, and a metal ring loaded with resistance. It makes the proposed antenna low-profile and wideband. The simulation results show that the VSWR of the antenna is less than 3.5 in the bandwidth of 203-492MHz, a height of only 86mm.

articleTitle: Generation of Gaussian Beam in FDTD using Surface Current Source
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the implementation of Gaussian beam in FDTD using surface current source is proposed. By appropriately introducing a Gaussian-distributed surface current source into the computational domain of FDTD, the propagation of a Gaussian beam can be accurately simulated. A numerical example is given, and its results are compared with CST with a peak-to-peak amplitude error of less than 0.2 dB, proving the correctness of the implementation.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Scheme for Boresight Error Prediction of the Antenna-Radome System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a machine learning (ML) scheme to predict the boresight errors (BSE) in a range of antenna scan angles. With electric and magnetic currents calculated by the method of moments (MoM) at only a few scan angles, the training set is constructed by dividing the entire meshes into small pieces. A PointNet neural network is employed as the ML model in this paper.
