Numerical results show that the trained ML model has higher calculation accuracy than the physical optics (PO) method, and compared with MoM, this method saves calculation time because fewer scan angles need to be calculated.

articleTitle: Design of a 1-bit Wideband High Efficiency Reconfigurable Transmit-array
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A 1-bit linearly polarized widedband high-efficiency reconfigurable transmit-array is proposed, consisting of magnetoelectric dipole and butterfly shaped metal patch. The 180° phase difference is achieved by controlling the state of the PIN diodes. A 12 × 12 array was designed and tested in HFSS, and the test results showed that two-dimensional beam scanning can be achieved with a scanning range of ±40°. The maximum gain in the broadside direction can reach 22.38dBi, the aperture efficiency is 34.7%, and the 3dB gain bandwidth is 26.2%.

articleTitle: A Novel Polarization Conversion Metasurface With Wide Transmission band
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel broadband polarization conversion metasurface (PCM) that has a wide transmission band with low insertion loss. The PCM is composed of a polarization conversion layer and a band-pass frequency-selective surface (FSS). A high transmission window with an insertion loss less than 1.5 dB in the desired pass band from 5.8 GHz to 10.7 GHz and a wide low-backscattering band from 3.5 GHz to 18 GHz are achieved simultaneously.

articleTitle: Forward electromagnetic modeling and inverse scattering of cylinder with various cross-section using physics informed neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Physical informed Neural Networks (PINNs) represent an innovative approach that integrates the precision of physical modeling with the computational power of deep learning to effectively solve partial differential equations (PDEs) and other complex physical problems. The primary objective of this study is to thoroughly investigate the electromagnetic scattering and inverse scattering characteristics of an object using PINNs, by utilizing the Maxwell equations expressed in sparse matrix form as the physical constraints for PINNs, and accurately incorporating the results from finite-difference frequency-domain method (FDFD) as input field data for the neural network, in order to achieve a comprehensive and precise analysis of electromagnetic phenomena.

articleTitle: Design of a 75-110GHz Turnstile Junction Orthomode Transducer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a waveguide orthomode transducer (OMT) for the 75-110 GHz band, which transmits in mode TE10. The main structure of the orthomode transducer is the turnstile junction. The OMT has an input signal via a circular waveguide and two WR10 rectangular waveguide outputs. The presented orthomode transducer architecture exhibits an isolation between rectangular ports better than 50 dB, a transmission loss less than 0.1dB and a return loss better than 17 dB, in the 75-110GHz range.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized GPS Antenna for Limited Space
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized global positioning system (GPS) antenna is proposed inside a terminal device with limited space. The size of the terminal device is approximated to be 0.3 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.1 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.03 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and contains many metal elements that affect the bandwidth of the antenna such as battery and metal coils. The circular polarization was formed by using the the inverted-F antenna(IFA) and the edge of the ground next to it, and miniaturization was achieved by introducing L-shaped folded branches at the ground. By utilizing the metal ground, the folded branch, and the IFA, miniaturization and circular polarization are achieved in the special scenario with high radiation efficiency. The designed antenna operates in the GPS L1 band and is suitable for small tracking and positioning devices.

articleTitle: 2D System Simulation Modeling for Millimeter Wave Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radiometer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to develop an accurate imaging model to simulate the imaging process of millimeter-wave Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radiometer(InSAR), enabling system designers to accurately predict the imaging effect and deeply analyze the impact of various parameters on InSAR performance. The core advantage of this model lies in its ability to accurately characterize the target radiated signals and the receiver received signals in the time domain, which significantly enhances the accuracy of the model. The effectiveness of the imaging model has been validated by 2D simulation experiments, providing designers with a powerful tool to guide the construction and optimization of real systems, thereby improving the overall performance of millimeter-wave InSAR systems.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Metasurface Coating for Infrared-Radar Stealth Compatibility
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The compatibility of infrared and radar stealth is the key to deal with multi-band detection technology. In this paper, a thin infrared-radar compatible stealth structure is constructed based on resistive frequency selective absorber (RFSA) and metal frequency selective surface (MFSS). Using the equivalent circuit model (ECM), the frequency response of the unit in radar and infrared bands is quickly analyzed. The thickness of the proposed compatible stealth structure is only 0.074 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. The reflection coefficient of the structure in the Ku-band is less than -10 dB and the infrared emissivity is less than 0.3 in the infrared band of 8-14 μm.

articleTitle: Singularity Analysis in Fast Physical Optics Method for Electrically Large Scatterers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this work, the singularity in the fast physical optics method based on quadratic quadrilateral patch discretization (Q-FPO) is studied. By introducing first-order integrations, the physical mechanism of the singularities is revealed, and the critical point contributions in different singular cases are extracted. Closed-form expression of physical optics integral in singular case is proposed. The accuracy and efficiency of new method is validated on an electrically large aircraft scatterer with electrical size of 373.3. The computational time of the new method is reduced to 13.0% of the Gordon method and 40.4% of the Q-FPO method.

articleTitle: Study on scattering characteristics of discrete charged particle system
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The scattering characteristics of discrete charged particle system are studied in this paper. Firstly, we give the Mie theory of a single charged particle illuminated by plane wave, and then the scattering theory of discrete charged particle system is derived by combining the particle size distribution function. Based on the above theories, the effects of particle size and surface charge on extinction efficiency are mainly analyzed. The general trend of extinction efficiency of charged particle system decreases and the corresponding transmittance increases with the increase of surface conductivity. The research results have important applications in aviation, aerospace, remote sensing, imaging and many other fields.

articleTitle: Training Neural Operator Model and Solving Inverse Problems with AH FDTD Simulation Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper explores a data driven machine learning neural network, the neural operator network, as an alternative to traditional simulation methods for solving the inverse problem of the TMz field in a two-dimensional non-uniform conductivity distribution. The neural operator network learns the mapping between the non-uniform conductivity distribution and the output Ez field distribution, the training data obtained by AH FDTD method. After training the neural operator network model, it can predict the conductivity distribution with reasonable accuracy given an Ez field. Furthermore, a comparison was made among four neural operator network models, with the GNO model demonstrating the highest accuracy. The LNO model required the least amount of training time.

articleTitle: Simulation Study of Radiation System for L-band Magnetically Insulated Line Oscillator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A magnetically insulated line oscillator is a narrow band cross-field device that combines the technologies of slow wave structure and self-insulating magnetic field, resulting in its giga-watt operation without electric breakdown. This paper presents a simulation study of an L-band MILO with reflectors and a mode-transducing antenna. MILO is simulated using CST with the particle-in-cell method. Simulation results show that a 1.82 GHz high power microwave of dominant output TEM mode with peak power of 9.1 GW and peak power efficiency of 22% is generated when diode voltage of 680 kV and beam current of 60kA is applied at the input. While in conventional MILO, the peak output power is 7.6 GW so the reflector configuration resulted in a 20% efficiency increase. To get maximum power at boresight as well as good radiation symmetry pattern and low sidelobes level, a radiation system based on TEM-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> plate inserted mode converter and Gaussian profile conical horn antenna is designed and simulated for MILO with reflectors. The conversion efficiency of the mode converter is 98.5% at 1.82 GHz and over the frequency range of 1.65-1.9 GHz, it is above 90%. The antenna has a gain of 18.8 dBi at 1.82 GHz and VSWR less than 1.5 dB over the operating frequency range. Both the E-plane and H-plane, have 3-dB beamwidth of 21.6° and 21.2° respectively, and sidelobes level less than -36 dB.

articleTitle: Fast Frequency Scanning of Dielectric Targets Utilizing MLFMM-Maehly Approximation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A rapid approach utilizing the PMCHWT framework with Maehly approximation is suggested for the estimation of monostatic radar cross section (RCS) of the dielectric targets. Firstly, the Chebyshev nodes within a specific wideband are obtained through coordinate transformation. Subsequently, the Method of Moments (MoM) is applied to address the electric field integral equation, enabling the determination of the surface current at the Chebyshev nodes. This process facilitates the computation of the Chebyshev polynomial representing the induced surface current across a broad frequency range, thereby allowing for the calculation of the necessary coefficients. Meanwhile, the Chebyshev polynomial undergoes a conversion process into a rational function through the Maehly approximation technique. Finally, the current is computed at various frequency points falling within the designated frequency spectrum, and the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of the dielectric target is ascertained. Additionally, the utilization of the multilevel fast multipole method (MLFMM) is employed to diminish the computational time required for predictions.

articleTitle: Marching-on-in-Time Analysis of Electromagnetic Scattering of Uniformly Moving Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this article, we propose a numerical method for calculating the electromagnetic scattering fields of an arbitrarily shaped perfectly electrical conducting (PEC) target in uniform motion. The current variation during the movement is analyzed in the laboratory frame where the observer remains stationary. An additional layer of current is introduced to describe the current caused by the moving of the surface charges on the object. The marching-on-in-time (MOT) method is used to obtain the scattering fields in time-domain. The numerical results of a PEC sphere in uniform motion are presented and compared with the results of using the Lorentz-Mie method, which verify the feasibility of the method.

articleTitle: Thermal Cycling Reliability Analysis of 2.5D Chiplet Based on Silicon Interposer
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: As an important technology in the post-Moore era, Chiplet has been widely used in system design. In this work, the thermal cycling reliability of 2.5D Chiplet based on silicon (Si) interposer is investigated. First, a quarter 2.5D Chiplet thermal simulation model is established. Secondly, we found radial deformation distribution patterns for die, Si interposer and bump arrays. The maximum warpage occurs at the corners of Si interposer. The stresses in each bump are concentrated at the two ends, which are more prone to cracking. Finally, as the thickness of the Si interposer increases, the stress on it decreases, however, the deformation first decreases and then increases slightly.

articleTitle: Terahertz Broadband 1-bit PB-phase Metasurfaces via independently controlled flip-chipped HEMT-atoms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: High-performance reconfigurable intelligent surfaces have demonstrated significant potential in achieving precise and wide-angle terahertz beam steering. This study introduces a double-layer metasurface independently coded to leverage the Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase for 1-bit terahertz beam steering. The metasurface design ensures smooth phase shifts and consistent amplitudes across a broad frequency spectrum, enabled by flip-chipped PB-phase elements. Notably, an upper dual-split square ring resonator enhances the cross-polarization conversion of the HEMT-controlled PB-phase structure and interlayer coupling. Simulation results indicate a phase difference of 180° within the 0.122-0.16 THz band, phase shift errors below 2°, insertion loss less than -6.13 dB, and a scanning range exceeding ±60° in two dimensions. With quasi-ideal coding states and straightforward fabrication, this metasurface holds promise for applications in 6G wireless communications and terahertz radar detection.

articleTitle: An Improved Dehazing Algorithm Combining Dark Channel Prior and Artificial Bee Colony Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Aiming to address significant issues like severe halo effects and excessive noise present in images processed by the traditional dark channel prior-based dehazing algorithm using fixed values, a proposed enhancement method leverages the characteristics of the artificial bee colony algorithm for parameter optimization. It seeks the optimal atmospheric light transmission factor values within different average image brightness ranges and integrates these values into the dark channel prior-based dehazing algorithm. Simultaneously, in estimating the atmospheric light, a median filtering algorithm replaces the original twostep minimum value filtering process. This improvement exhibits notable effectiveness in reducing halo effects and noise compared to the traditional dark channel prior-based dehazing algorithm.

articleTitle: A Dual-Band Common Aperture Reconfigurable Metasurface Element
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Reconfigurable metasurfaces are considered as high potential devices that can replace phased array antennas to a certain extent in radar and communication systems in the future, as they not only play a role in beam modulation but also significantly reduce their cost compared to phased array antennas. Universally, most current metasurfaces were operated at one frequency band, which has a limitation in flexibility. Therefore, we propose a dual-band common aperture reconfigurable metasurface at X and Ka bands. Their center frequencies are 11.8 GHz and 28 GHz, where the metasurface has a 1-bit phase switch. Besides, this element uses only one positive intrinsic-negative (PIN) diode to simultaneously manipulate two frequency bands, minimizing the number of active devices and simplifying the control circuit.

articleTitle: Characterization Method of Gas Discharge Tube Under High-altitude Electromagnetic Pulse
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Besides the peak amplitude of the electromagnetic interference, other norms such root action and peak rate of rise time play an important role in evaluating the immunity of electric device to HEMP. Therefore, the spark-over voltage of GDT provided by manufactures is not enough for supporting its application in HEMP protection field. A characterization method based on GDT spark-over voltage amplitude and delay time is proposed in this paper, which can be used to predict the residual waveform and describe the performance of GDT under HEMP excitation. Meanwhile, the method is validated by different HEMP conducted environment. The work will be helpful to evaluate the protection effect of GDT to HEMP.

articleTitle: A Model for Scattering of Composite with Randomly Distributed Fibers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Fiber-reinforced composites are commonly used for good electromagnetic properties such as wave absorption. This paper proposes a multi-scale model for studying the scattering properties of composites with randomly distributed micro fibers by Fourier modal method. Reflection coefficient is calculated and compared with the simulation result from commercial software HFSS, proving the calculation is valid and correct. The relationship between scattering properties of fiber-reinforced composites and randomness of fiber distribution is investigated through this model.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna with the Profile of 0.5 mm Covering 3.4~3.6 GHz and 4.8~4.96 GHz for 5G Mobile Terminal Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The antennas on the metal bezel for the mobile terminal devices are so crowded that the engineers must find another space such as the screen or the back cover to accommodate all kinds of antennas with diverse functions. This article proposes a novel method to develop a dual-band planar antenna with an extremely low profile of 0.5 mm on the back cover. The first two characteristic modes TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,0</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,1</inf> of the half-mode patch antenna are used to cover the lower band of partial 5G band N78 (3.40~3.60 GHz) and higher band of 5G band N79 (4.80~4.96 GHz). A back-to-back topology of magnetic coupling introduces a parasitic half-mode patch to produce an additional resonance for bandwidth enhancement of each band. The simulated results show that the -6 dB impedance bandwidths are 3.39~3.67 GHz (280 MHz, 7.9%) and 4.80~4.99 GHz (190 MHz, 3.9%) with average total efficiencies of -2.3 dB (58.9%) and -3.3 dB (46.7%) at the lower and higher bands respectively. The proposed antenna is with an extremely low profile of 0.5 mm, about 0.006 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> refers to the lowest frequency of the operation band), which has a great potential to be applied in mobile terminal devices.

articleTitle: Radar Doppler Signature Time-Modulated Reflective Metasurfaces for Target Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the rapid increase in the number of manned and unmanned devices, higher requirements have been put forward for long-range target recognition. In this article, a time-modulated reflective metasurfaces of modulating frequency change sequences is proposed, which has the advantage of low cost and low complexity. By controlling the switch status of the P-I-N diode to achieve different phase reflection response. Different time modulation sequences can lead to different harmonic frequency characteristics. The target covered by a time-modulated metasurface, its harmonic frequency scatters can be changed over time. The radar detector can recognize targets through different time-frequency characteristics. The proposed method provides an attractive choice for future long-range target recognition scenarios.

articleTitle: DGTD Methods for Bidirectional PIN Limiter Simulation Using MNA-SPICE
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposed the Discontinuous Galerkin Time-Domain (DGTD) methods for simulating a bidirectional PIN limiter using the Modified Nodal Analysis-Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (MNA-SPICE). The proposed method combines the advantages of MNA-SPICE for circuit simulation with the high accuracy and efficiency of DGTD for electromagnetic field analysis. Numerical simulations demonstrate the effectiveness and reliability of this method.

Author Keywords: Simulation Program with Integrated Circuit Emphasis (SPICE)

articleTitle: Validation of traditional electric dipole model of the corrosion-related static electric source with a FEM simulation model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: When ships navigate and dock at sea, the static electric field with significant characteristic is generated due to electrochemical corrosion. Through the use of the finite element method-based multiphysics simulation software COMSOL, simulations of the spatial electric field of typical targets have been conducted. The simulation results indicate that corrosion-related static electric fields exhibit distinct distribution characteristics. This paper supplements the traditional dipole method for modeling ship static electric fields, and compares the results of the dipole modeling with simulations in COMSOL. The analytical results verify that under certain conditions, the electric field simulated by the dipole method is highly similar in numerical magnitude and spatial distribution to that simulated by the COMSOL software.

articleTitle: Inversion of Target Electromagnetic Parameters Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the inversion of relative permittivity and geometric dimensions of complex targets based on deep learning convolutional neural networks. Taking the B2 bomber as the target object, the raw data is derived from the FEKO software, and bistatic RCS data is simulated using the Physical Optics (PO) algorithm. This simulated data serves as the input to the convolutional neural network, with the corresponding output being the relative permittivity and size of the target. Finally, the network's output results are compared with those of the test set. The results show that the fitting coefficients (R^2) of relative permittivity and size reach 0.975 and 0.941, respectively, indicating the accuracy of convolutional neural networks in handling nonlinear regression problems.

articleTitle: A Compact Planar Van Atta Array with a Crossover
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to implementing a compact planar retrodirective array(RDA). By adopting a crossover structure, the feeding network of the RDA can be significantly simplified. The developed array operates at 10 GHz, and exhibits a 3dB beamwidth of 94.93° in the E-plane and 81.67° in the H-plane, demonstrating robust retrodirective performance.

articleTitle: Sensitivity Test Methods and Characteristics of Active Filter Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Active filtering amplification circuits are often used in electronic systems with high frequency stability requirements to improve the stability and power level of crystal oscillator signals. However, active filtering amplifiers may also receive electromagnetic interference signals from the other systems in the same environment. Even if it is an out of band electromagnetic interference signal, it may cause abnormal output of the active filtering amplifier, leading to malfunction. Therefore, this paper designs a sensitivity test method for out of band electromagnetic interference excitation filter amplifier circuits based on the basic working principle of filter amplifier circuits, and studies the sensitivity law of active filter amplifiers. In this proposed method, a directional coupling based port conduction sensitivity testing method is proposed, and three kinds of interference signals (sine signal, pulse modulation signal, and frequency offset modulation signal) are considered for excitation. The relationships between the frequency and amplitude of the excitation signal and the output signal of the active filter amplifier are studied. The experimental results show that the proposed method can be used for effectively evaluted the sensitivity phenomenon of the active filtering amplifier. At the same time, it can be seen that the signal-to-noise ratio emission of the output signal of the active filter amplification circuit significantly decreases (exceeding 10 decibels) under the effects of out of band sine, pulse modulation, and frequency offset modulation; and exhibits a typical "threshold initiation" characteristic.

articleTitle: Detection of Road Structural Layer Thickness Using LSTM on Ground Penetrating Radar Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) technology plays a crucial role in road engineering due to its non-destructive, efficient, and accurate assessment of structural layer thickness. Despite being a common function in commercial GPR systems, layer detection typically involves manual selection followed by automatic tracking, resulting in inefficiencies, subjective biases, and the need for post-processing. This paper presents a real-time automatic identification method utilizing Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models to analyze GPR data and identify road structural layer thickness. Initially, the GPR data undergo preprocessing. Subsequently, the LSTM model is designed and trained to effectively learn and recognize the A-Scan data. Validation on multiple real road datasets demonstrates that the LSTM-based method outperforms traditional methods in accuracy and robustness. This approach not only enhances the automation of GPR data processing but also overcomes the limitations of traditional methods in real-time automatic detection, providing reliable technical support for road structural layer detection with promising application potential.

articleTitle: Radiation source location technology of complex space based on point cloud neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a point cloud neural network (PCNN) to locate radiation sources in complex space. The network has the ability to process 3D sampling information which consists of the electric field intensity and coordinate. The ability of the network to predict the location of the radiation source is obtained by training and fitting the relationship between the sampled electromagnetic information and the radiation source position. Compared with traditional methods, the proposed PCNN method avoids the calculation of electromagnetic wave propagation law in complex space, as well as reduce the computing resources and time required for positioning process. The performance of the proposed method is validated by a series of simulation dataset.

articleTitle: A Full-wave Simulation Technique for Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a full-wave simulation technique based on the Finite Element-Boundary Element-Domain Decomposition Method (FEM-BEM-DDM) for the analysis of Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces (RISs) loaded with lumped-element loads. The RISs considered in this study consist of electrically controlled elements loaded on quasi-periodic geometries. The method separates the geometric model of the lumped-element loads on each unit of the quasi-periodic array into a geometric structure without the lumped-element loads and an additional term representing the lumped-element loads, with the geometric structure partitioned and meshed according to the array units. The additional term treats the mesh at the location of the lumped-element loads separately, considering it as an additional current boundary condition, and utilizes zeroth-order Whitney basis functions for computation. The accuracy of the proposed technique are demonstrated through a numerical examples.

articleTitle: E-plane Waveguide Bandpass Filter based on Double-Layer Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a novel design method of bandpass filter (BPF) using the high-order modes of spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) is proposed. With the proposed design method, an E-plane waveguide BPF is specifically designed, which contains two metallic layers with different metallic patterns coated on the front and back sides of a printed circuit board (PCB) and tightly coupled with each other. The high-order mode dispersive characteristics of SSPP unit cell can be effectively adjusted by changing the dimensions of the patterns, allowing control over the upper and lower cut-off frequencies of the proposed BPF. Good simulated filtering performance of the E-plane waveguide BPF verifies the potential and feasibility of the proposed design method for millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Bandpass-Filtering Periodic Structure and its Application on Pattern Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes the bandpass-filtering periodic structure and then applies it to manipulate far-field transmitting patterns. The periodic element is synthesized and designed using the equivalent transmission line model. By changing the length of slotlines in each element, the passband can be adjusted, where the element is further quasi-periodically arranged for manipulating the transmitted wave. Finally, an array with 10×20 elements is realized, with a deflection angle of 30°. In addition, the proposed array possesses the angular stability within 45°.

articleTitle: Low Profile Electromagnetic Functional Metasurfaces with Passband Switchable Function
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper proposes a multifunctional switching electromagnetic functional metasurfaces based on PIN diodes, which has the advantages of low profile and angular stability, and is suitable for fast switching in different passbands. By cascading a two-layer non resonant structure, it has a dual transmission passband (6.5-7.0 GHz and 11.9-12.8 GHz) in the "off state" and a single transmission passband (9.5-10.5 GHz) in the "open state". After simulation, both functions ensure a 70% transmittance (within a 45 ° incidence angle range) at a profile height of 1mm, and have a high cutoff state outside the passband.

articleTitle: Application Research on Blockchain-based Asynchronous Federated Learning in Data Security Sharing in Vehicle Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In the vehicle-connected environment of intelligent transportation systems, although data sharing brings new development opportunities, it is also accompanied by challenges such as privacy and security (such as data leaks) and upload efficiency. These issues reduce the enthusiasm of data providers to participate. In order to solve the above problems, this research aims to propose a new architecture based on asynchronous federated learning, focusing on solving bandwidth, security and privacy issues encountered in IoT vehicle data sharing, and is committed to improving the reliability of data sharing. and efficiency. By adopting blockchain technology to enhance the security and reliability of model parameters, reducing transmission loads and alleviating privacy concerns. At the same time, the research also uses a distributed, efficient and secure data sharing architecture based on blockchain to select nodes and further optimizes the asynchronous federated learning scheme to improve overall efficiency. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme not only improves the learning accuracy, but also significantly accelerates the convergence speed, and at the same time enhances privacy protection and service quality, fully verifying the effectiveness and practicality of this research method.

articleTitle: A Compact Filtering Balun with Wideband and Wide Stopband Using Half-Mode SIW and Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel wideband filtering balun with compactness and wide stopband using the dielectriccovered F-shaped groove (DCFSG) half-mode substrate integrated waveguide and spoof surface plasmon polariton (HMSIW-SSPP) structure. Due to the DCFSG HMSIW-SSPP unit cell’s dispersion curve featuring a wideband passband and low upper cut-off frequency, the proposed filtering balun has wideband properties and compact size. The proposed filtering balun is fabricated and measured. It has a wide passband (29.9% 3-dB fractional bandwidth from 6.4 to 8.65 GHz) and a wide stopband rejection (25-dB at 2.15 times the center frequency).

articleTitle: A Fast ISAR Image Prediction Method for Multiple Isomorphic Targets Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In order to improve the computational efficiency of dynamic isomorphic multi-target radar imaging, this paper proposes a rapid multi-target inverse synthetic aperture radar (ISAR) imaging method based on prior information from radar parameters. By using an ensemble deep learning model, including a fully connected neural network (FCNN) and a U-Net to train with the simulated electromagnetic field data and the distance between targets, the proposed network has successfully predicted the ISAR image of two targets with an extremely high Structure Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.961 compared to the images generated by simulation results. This method demonstrates the potential of the ensemble deep-learning network for fast prediction of ISAR images. Numerical and graphical results are presented to evaluate the effectiveness of the efficient imaging method, which indicates that the proposed method is effective for the rapid prediction of multi-target ISAR images.

articleTitle: Plane Spiral OAM Antenna Based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The paper proposes a new method for generating Plane Spiral Orbital Angular Momentum (PSOAM) based on Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons. Using the SSPP unit structure as a foundation, a leaky-wave antenna with fine wires placed on the backside is designed. Subsequently, the designed leaky-wave antenna is curved into a cylindrical shape and successfully radiates PSOAM beams. Near-field phase patterns illustrate corresponding PSOAM modes at different frequencies. The range of PSOAM modes spans from 2 to 4.

articleTitle: RCS Reduction of Vivaldi Antenna Based on Characteristic Mode Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a low radar cross section (RCS) Vivaldi antenna which covers entire X-band is designed based on Characteristic Mode Analysis (CMA). A typical frequency point (8.5Hz) is selected for applying CMA. The analysis of the magnitude and phase of each mode is introduced, which makes the analysis more effective for guiding the RCS reduction design. By modification, the whole scattering modes are effectively suppressed and the monostatic RCS is reduced significantly.

articleTitle: An Efficient Incremental Length Diffraction Coefficients Method Based on Quadratic Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: High frequency electromagnetic scattering algorithm has been widely used in analyzing the scattering characteristics for electrically large scatterers. The incremental length of diffraction coefficients (ILDC) method considers the Fock current, which could capture the diffraction field contributed by the creeping wave. However, the traditional ILDC method is not available for arbitrary convex targets with discretized mesh. In this work, a fast physical optics (PO) and ILDC hybrid (FPO-QILDC) method based on quadratic patches is proposed to compute the scattered field accurately and efficiently. The error between results computed by the FPO-QILDC and the full wave method could be reduced to 0.46 dB.

articleTitle: A novel rectangular waveguide array with side-fed structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel waveguide antenna array using rectangular waveguide with metallic block as radiator element is presented. The radiator elements are same as each other ,which simplifies the design. The simulated sidelobe of sum pattern is less than -22dB and the simulated efficiency is about 45% ,which show that this proposed novel waveguide antenna is of the characteristics of low sidelobe levels and great efficiency as traditional slotted waveguide antenna.

articleTitle: A Wideband Frequency Selective Rasorber With Fractal Square-Loop Resonator
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency selective rasorber (FSR) with a passband located between two absorbing bands. The FSR consists of a lossy layer and a bandpass frequency selective surface (FSS) layer. The lossy layer is composed of a fractal square-loop resonator loaded with lumped resistors, which can generate parallel resonances. A conventional square slot configuration is adopted in the bandpass FSS layer. The simulation results show that the 3 dB transmission band extends from 5.59 GHz to 9.35 GHz, and the minimum insertion loss of 0.09 dB is achieved at 7.5 GHz. The dual-polarization FSR has the characteristics of wideband, and the reflection coefficient lower than −10 dB is 4.1 to 18.3 GHz with a 127% fractional bandwidth (FBW).

articleTitle: Research on shielding effectiveness of field-to-wire coupling model based on time-domain hybrid method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper adopts an efficient time-domain hybrid method to solve the complex field-to-wire coupling model. Under the irradiation of high frequency electromagnetic pulse, the transient response of different types and different lengths of cables arranged in parallel in a large engine room model is simulated. By analyzing the electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) inside and outside the model, the three-dimensional current distribution on the model surface and the shielding effectiveness of the model, the results show that the aircraft shell itself has good electromagnetic protection characteristics. In addition, the experimental results by numerical simulation show that improving the electromagnetic protection capability of the fuselage, adopting the shielded cable structure and changing the wiring mode can effectively improve the shielding effectiveness of the inner cable of the fuselage under the irradiation of high-energy electromagnetic pulse.

articleTitle: A Broadband Wide-Angle Microstrip Antenna Based on Coplanar Coupling L-shaped Probe
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a broadband wide-angle microstrip antenna with coplanar coupling L-shaped probe (CCLP) is presented. The CCLP is composed of a cylinder probe perpendicular to the patch and a microstrip line with dimension gradient parallel to the patch. The tapered impedance achieved by the CCLP with the tapered dimension. Therefore, the antenna bandwidth has been expended dramatically. In addition, the traditional feeding method of interlayer coupling with at least two layers of substrates has been replaced by coplanar coupling. The difficulty and cost of the processing has been greatly reduced. By optimizing the shape and size of the CCLP, The bandwidth of the proposed antenna with the VSWR ⩽ 2.0 is from 7.3 GHz to 12.6 GHz, with a relative bandwidth of about 53%. The active VSWR is less than 2.0 in the frequency band of 7.5 GHz-12.3 GHz within the scanning angle range of 0°-45°. When the incidence angle increases to 60°, the bandwidth is still maintain 6.5 GHz-11.2 GHz with active VSWR⩽ 2.0 .

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of an Ultra-Wideband Energy Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband energy selective surface (ESS) for high-power microwave (HPM) protection is designed. Based on the adaptive transformation of the PIN with the power, which makes the passband moved. Afterwards, by designing the filtering equivalent circuit, the ESS model is devised to realize the requirement of being a band-pass filter in the operating band when the low-power electromagnetic wave is incident with low insertion loss (IL). Meanwhile, it has very high shielding effectiveness (SE) when the high-power electromagnetic wave is incident. Whatsmore, using the mapping relationship between the equivalent circuit and the model structure, the ESS model is conceived. Moreover, the performance of the ESS model is investigated by combining the equivalent circuit model with the advanced design system (ADS) and the full-wave simulation in the 3-D electromagnetic simulation software computer simulation technology (CST). The emulation results demonstrate that low IL less than 1 dB bandwidth is 6.7 GHz-14 GHz with a relative bandwidth of 70% at low-power electromagnetic wave incidence, and the SE is greater than 26 dB at high-power incidence in the corresponding frequency band. It also realizes the TE and TM dual-polarization characteristics and 60° angular stability.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Energy Selective Surface with High Shielding for Large Angles of Incidence Based on Origami
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The energy selective surface (ESS) has been widely studied in the field of electromagnetic protection for high power. However, there are still challenges for shielding high-power waves with large angles of incidence. Here, a reconfigurable ESS based on origami is proposed. Utilizing origami, the density of x-direction strips is increased, thus increasing the shielding strength for TM mode. By parameters sweeping, an ESS that satisfies simultaneously shielding requirements for both polarizations can be designed. This work opens an alternative way to design ESS for any angles of incidence and dual polarization.

articleTitle: Design of Co-designed Wideband Circularly Polarized Filtering Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A wideband circularly polarized filtering antenna (CPFA) based on coupled resonant networks is proposed in this paper. By using a combination of a microstrip patch antenna and a microstrip non-radiating resonator to realize the actual circuit of the filtering antenna. The 3D EM simulation results of S11 achieve a matching target of less than -15 dB in the range of 4.84-5.11 GHz, the FBW calculated according to the center frequency of 5 GHz is 0.054, and its 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth is 4.79-5.19 GHz. This axial ratio bandwidth completely covers its -15dB matched bandwidth, and the total efficiency of the antenna is greater than 0.945 in the effective bandwidth range. The antenna is LHCP mode for the main polarized wave in the effective bandwidth as well as throughout the 3 dB axial ratio bandwidth, where the actual LHCP gain is almost the same as the total gain and much larger than the RHCP gain. The proposed integrated design of CPFAs is of great general interest, guidance, and utility.

articleTitle: Efficient Nyström Method for Solving Ultrasonic Scattering Problems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Elasticodynamic scattering plays an important role in ultrasonic scattering problems, especially in evaluating the far-field scattering amplitude of defects. To address the elasticodynamic scattering problem, we employ the high-order Nyström method (NM). This approach utilizes high-order surface triangles for meshing and employs high-order interpolation to define the basis functions on each surface triangle unit. Within the impedance matrix generated by the high-order NM model based on the conventional boundary integral equation (CBIE), the diagonal and near blocks are stored in a full matrix, while the far blocks are compressed and stored using adaptive cross approximation (ACA) technique. The results predicted by the ACA based solver are compared with those predicted by pure NM to verify the accuracy and effectiveness of this method.

articleTitle: An efficient algorithm for the response of gyrotropic-like anisotropic media in arbitrary deviated Wells
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: To expedite forward simulation studies, this paper proposes a universal analytical algorithm for calculating gyrotropic-like anisotropic formation models. the Maxwell equation system underwent a 2D Fourier transform, yielding a set of ordinary differential equations featuring the system matrix, field vector, and source vector. The response in the medium model is obtained by solving the differential equation. We introduce the reflection and propagation matrices to describe electromagnetic wave propagation at the stratigraphic interfaces, and obtain the frequency domain response of electromagnetic waves at each layer. Finally, a two-dimensional inverse Fourier transform was applied to translate the frequency domain responses into the spatial domain. The accuracy of the algorithm was verified by comparing the calculated results with the numerical simulation algorithm results. Moreover, the eigenvalues of the system matrix are uniquely defined and are associated with factors such as formation parameters and anisotropy. The characteristic values of various types of anisotropic formation system matrix are analyzed, which not only contributes to extracting formation information but also provides a basis for geological interpretation and oil and gas exploration.

articleTitle: Influence of High-Power Near-Field Modulation Pulse Interference on IGBT Inverter Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The reliability of Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) significantly impacts the performance and efficiency of power conversion systems, making them crucial in industry and energy storage applications. With the ongoing trend towards higher power density in power conversion devices, IGBTs are increasingly vulnerable to interference from external sources during operation. This study investigates the high-power near-field modulation pulse magnetic field interference in the IGBT switching circuit during practical operation, with a focus on the impact of parasitic parameters on output waveform. Experimental verification under various interference conditions provides insight into actual interference effects.

articleTitle: Recent Advances in Electromagnetic Optimization Methods for Metamaterial Absorbers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Metamaterial absorbers have superior performance in absorbing, suppressing, and manipulating the electromagnetic (EM) waves. Due to the challenges of finding the optimal design parameters, the EM optimization for metamaterial absorbers is time-consuming. It is important to develop an efficient method to improve the speed and efficiency of EM optimization for metamaterial absorbers. This paper provides recent advances in EM optimization methods for metamaterial absorbers, including the artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate-based optimization method and the ANN-space mapping (SM) surrogate-based optimization method.

articleTitle: A wearable CPW-fed quad-band-notched two-port MIMO antenna for IoT applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a wearable quad-band-notched two-port Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna and it utilizes coplanar waveguide (CPW) for feeding for wearable IoT applications. The antenna uses Liquid crystal polymer (LCP) flexible substrate with dimensions of 30mm*54mm*0.1mm. By creating four C-shaped slots on the patch, the proposed antenna creates four notched bands. To improve the isolation between the antenna elements, a fence construction is added in the center. The proposed antenna ultimately achieves a band coverage of 3.26-10.8 GHz, with the notched-band coverage of 4.0-4.57 GHz (C-band radar Note7), 4.8-5.0 GHz (N79 mobile), 5.62-6.0 GHz (WLAN downlink), and 8.08-8.79 GHz (ITU-R)`, and the isolation is greater than 20 dB. In addition, the key performance metrics of the MIMO antenna design, including ECC, DG, and TARC, and the antenna is subjected to bending and human body experiments, and all the results show that the antenna has the advantages of small size, multiple notched bands, and high isolation, which has a good prospect of application in the wearable field.

articleTitle: A Graph Isomorphism Neural Network Algorithm For Solving The Maximum Clique Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Combinatorial Optimization (CO), as a crucial domain within optimization, has been spanned across a broad spectrum of fields, imparting significant practical relevance to the study of combinatorial optimization problems. Graph Neural Network (GNN) emerged as an algorithmic framework adept at learning from graph-structured data through deep learning techniques. Notably, its outstanding performance has garnered substantial attention from scholars, spurring in-depth investigations. This research specifically delved into the application of graph neural networks in addressing the maximum clique problem, offering a feasible scheme for leveraging GNNs to tackle optimization challenges constrained by various factors. The proposed methodology employed graph neural networks and utilized unsupervised loss functions for training, while weight sharing among networks was implemented to enhance the accuracy in predicting the membership probability of each node within the maximum clique. Ultimately, the optimal solution was derived through a decoder. Comparative analyses conducted on real-world datasets underscored the efficacy of the proposed scheme when juxtaposed against existing approaches.

articleTitle: SSCA-net: Few-shot Detection without Fine-tuning for Online Garbage Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Few-shot object detection has garnered notable interest due to the long-tail distribution of real-world data and the recent impact of data scarcity on detector performance. Currently, it is applied in various fields such as autonomous driving, medical image detection, remote sensing image analysis, and agricultural pest detection. However, effective research on online detection for low-power waste robots is still lacking. The fine-tuning stage required by existing methods is time-consuming and challenging to deploy on low-power waste robots, especially with the ever-increasing variety of new categories. To address this issue, we introduce a new network architecture, "SSCA-net," designed for online detection without fine-tuning. Specifically, we propose a support-guided network within the existing Faster R-CNN detector framework. Our network includes a Cross-Attention Region Proposal Network (CA-RPN) for generating object proposals, which boosts the recall rate for candidate bounding boxes of new classes, and a Support Class Feature (SFF) network that captures more representative prototypes of the support classes. In addition, we incorporate SimAM global attention to improve the quality of feature maps. To demonstrate the viability of our proposed method, we conducted extensive experiments on the VOC2007 dataset and a dedicated waste dataset. SSCA-net attains comparable or even batter results then exhaustive fine-tuning methods, achieve a 10-20% improvement over the baseline without fine-tuning.

articleTitle: Two-Material and Ridged Metal-Strip Substrate Integrated E-Plane Waveguide for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel substrate integrated E-plane waveguide (SIEW) with an extended single-mode bandwidth for broadband E-plane devices. The proposed structure consists of four dielectric layers, whose middle layer adopts a material with a high permittivity, and the remaining layers utilize the low-permittivity material. The middle layers are partially plated with a pair of ridged copper strips to guide the longitudinal current, where the strips aligning the direction of electroplating through holes assist in the propagation of E-plane electromagnetic waves for the bandwidth extension. The proposed SIEW achieves the cutoff frequencies of 5.8 and 29.2 GHz at the fundamental and second modes, respectively, resulting in a cutoff frequency ratio (CFR) of approximately 5.0. Consequently, the SIEW is fabricated and tested to verify its electromagnetic properties.

articleTitle: An Integrated Microsystem Electromagnetic Protection Scheme Based on Resistor-Embedded Spoof Surface Plasmon Polariton Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) always affects the normal operation of integrated microsystems. With the continuous development of modern electronic technology, the size of chips and circuit systems is constantly shrinking, and the working frequency band is increasing, which brings some trouble to electromagnetic protection. In order to solve these problems, a compact spoof surface plasmon polariton (SSPP) absorbing structure is proposed. This structure binds electromagnetic waves to the metal surface, and then reduces the intensity of electromagnetic waves through resistance, so as to achieve the purpose of electromagnetic protection. The SSPP structure is used for chip-level electromagnetic protection, which has high requirements for size, and the length and width of the structure are 2λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, and the thickness is 0.004 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the minimum wavelength in the operating frequency band), which is suitable for most situations. The working frequency band of the structure is 3-12GHz, the relative absorption bandwidth is 89%, and the working bandwidth of the absorption rate is more than 90% is 4.6-12GHz, which achieves an effective electromagnetic protection effect.

articleTitle: Transient Thermal Analysis of Chiplet-Based Systems with Dual-Channel Message Passing Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents a novel transient thermal analysis method for chiplet-based systems using the dual-channel message passing neural networks (MPNNs). Firstly, the package information is transformed into graph-structured data by using the finite difference approximation. Secondly, the temperature and power features are extracted through the dual-channel MPNNs to obtain the temporal gradient of temperature. Finally, the augmented neural ordinary differential equations are employed to learn the continuous-time dynamics of the heat transfer equation. The experimental results demonstrate that the model can accurately estimate the transient thermal maps with the mean absolute error of 0.272 K and the root mean squared error of 0.387 K. It is shown that the model can predict thermal maps at arbitrary time points, exhibiting good transferable capability.

articleTitle: A Fast Forward Solver for 3D Gain Pattern of Microstrip Antenna Arrays Based on CNNs
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A fast forward solver for 3D gain pattern of microstrip antenna arrays based on convolutional neural networks (CNNs) is proposed in this paper. The proposed method utilizes a deep learning approach to predict the gain pattern of the antenna array with high accuracy and efficiency. Firstly, the architecture of the proposed method is introduced. Then the off-line training process of the proposed CNN is described. Finally, the experimental results showcase the on-line performance of the proposed method. The proposed method requires 0.13 seconds for predictions, which is 108 times faster than HFSS, while utilizing only 1/35 of the memory required by HFSS.

articleTitle: Efficient Modeling of Two-Dimensional Infinite Periodic Structures and Its Application to Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel modeling method of two-dimensional infinite periodic structures is introduced, and they are modeled as infinite surfaces whose reflection coefficients are numerically known. In the similar manner as a layered media Green’s function (LMGF), a reduced form of Green’s function for the two-dimensional infinite periodic structures is obtained. Self/mutual coupling between source and observation point is formulated via method of moments (MoM). Numerical simulation of an antenna over frequency selective surfaces (FSSs) is performed, and it is found that the proposed modeling method works well for including contribution of the FSSs to the numerical results.

articleTitle: Scattering Properties of Multilayer Anisotropic Composites With Line Source
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper aims to develop a computational model of electromagnetic scattering properties of multilayer anisotropic composites with waves generated by a line source. The waves generated by finite sources are actually non-planar, but they can be expanded into a series of plane waves. Therefore, based on the scattering properties of multilayer anisotropic composites with plane wave incidence, the scattering properties can be obtained when a line source is used as the input source. With this computational model, the field distribution of multilayer anisotropic composites can be obtained when the waves generated by the line source are used as incident waves.

articleTitle: Transparent Four-Port MIMO DRAs Decoupled by Conformal Strips
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A four-port multi-input multi-output (MIMO) dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) is presented in this paper. Combing four rectangular DRs together can form a single DR element. With shape modification and conformal strips, the four ports can be decoupled. To verify the design idea, a transparent prototype can be designed and fabricated for 2.4-GHz band applications. The measured results show an impedance bandwidth of 5.8% and an isolation level of 24 dB.

articleTitle: A Conformal Antenna Array with Adjustable and Small-size Focal Spot for Head Hyperthermia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A microwave near-field focused antenna array operating at 915 MHz is proposed for head hyperthermia. The proposed array consists of 2×4 identical microstrip antenna elements, whose spatial distribution is helmet-like. With different excitation phase of 8 elements, the focus position for the antenna array can be adjustable, which makes the proposed array suitable for diversity of tumor locations. When the total input power of the array is 32W, the maximum temperature at the focal spot can reach 44℃, which can effectively kill cancer cells. Each power loss density -3dB focal spot region is around 2×2×2cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which causes less damage to normal cells surrounding cancer cells. The focal spot size of the proposed antenna array is much smaller than that of other near-field focused antenna array. Full-wave simulation verifies the feasibility of the near-field antenna array with adjustable focus position for head hyperthermia.

articleTitle: Design of Circularly Polarized Filtering Array Antenna with Two Radiation Nulls
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a quasi-cascaded triplet (CT) cross-coupled second-order perturbation circularly polarized filtering array antenna (CPFAA) is proposed. A simple microstrip patch antenna is used as a radiated resonator, and quasi-third-order cross-coupling topology is utilized with a coupled band-rejected resonator, which introduces two radiating nulls with high frequency selectivity and realizes circular polarization with better integration performance. The reflection coefficient of the proposed antenna is less than -10dB from 3.24GHz to 3.62GHz. The effective bandwidth range of the circular polarization of the antenna is 3.43-3.57GHz.This antenna achieves high-efficiency left-handed circularly polarized radiation function within the effective bandwidth.

articleTitle: An Incremental Delaunay Triangulation Construction Algorithm for Complex Electromagnetics Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper presents an incremental Delaunay triangulation construction algorithm for generating high-quality unstructured meshes. The algorithm is based on computer-aided design (CAD) models, which are efficiently meshed according to the geometric structure of the CAD model, and the mesh can be encrypted according to the surface structure to obtain a high-quality mesh that can be used for numerical computation. Mesh partitioning experiments are carried out on some complex geometrical models, and the results show that the method can realize unstructured and accurate surface mesh partitioning, numerical validations and applications demonstrate the reliability, accuracy of our dissected meshes.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Shared-Aperture Dual-Band Reflectarray Antenna with High Aperture Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A novel single-layer shared-aperture dual-band reflectarray is proposed, operating in the Ku-band and K-band. The reflection units of two frequency bands are alternately distributed on the same dielectric substrate, and a nearly 360° phase shift is achieved by changing the size of the reflection units. Based on this, a square reflectarray operating at 15.3 GHz and 21.6 GHz with an aperture diameter of 128 mm is designed, which consisting of 20×20 K-band reflection units and 10×10 Ku-band reflection units. At 15.3 GHz, the gain is 21.9 dBi and the aperture efficiency is 29%. At 21.6 GHz, the gain is 27 dBi and the aperture efficiency is 47%. In addition, the sidelobe levels are below -19.1 dB.

articleTitle: Research on Two-element Superdirective Antennas and Their Novel Application as Driven Elements
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Superdirective antennas can reach the limited boundary of antenna size and gain. However, they are difficult to design efficiently and are inherently narrowband, which would hinder their widespread application. Herein, we first introduce our developed supergain topology, which can assist with the easy realization of two-element supergain antennas. Then, a new strategy to convert the supergain antenna into a high-gain driven element is considered and investigated. Finally, two cases as examples are proposed by employing the driven element to excite other parasitic radiators. Simulated results verify the effectiveness of obtaining enhanced bandwidth with miniaturized size and considerable high gain.

articleTitle: Hybrid Method for EM Scattering from a Moving Ship on Dynamic Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, the ray-transfer technique is combined with the hybrid semi-deterministic facet scattering model (SDFSM) and shooting and bouncing ray (SBR) method to calculate and study the composite electromagnetic scattering of a moving ship on dynamic sea surface. Firstly, the world coordinate system (WCS) of sea surface and the local coordinate system (LCS) of target are established. Then, the incident rays are converted between LCS and WCS based on the motion of ship. The scattering field of ship in LCS is calculated by SBR. The scattering field of sea surface in WCS is calculated by SDFSM. The coupling field is obtained by the four-path model. Finally, compared with the MLFMM method, the effectiveness of proposed method in calculating the composite scattering of a moving target on flat plate is verified. The composite scattering of a moving ship on sea surface is also calculated.

articleTitle: Optimization of Iterative Physical Optics Method through CPU-GPU Heterogeneous Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of radar technology, electromagnetic simulation has found widespread applications across various fields. When solving for the Radar Cross Section (RCS) of electrically large scattering bodies using the Iterative Physical Optics Method (IPO), the number of unknowns is significant, leading to substantial memory usage and computation time. To address this issue, this paper constructs an IPO method based on parameter space for computing the RCS of electrically large radar targets and introduces CUDA parallel computing (Compute Unified Device Architecture) technology to achieve parallel computation on heterogeneous CPU-GPU platforms. Compared with commercial software, a speedup of 137.79× is achieved on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3050 GPU. The exemplary results demonstrate the feasibility and efficiency of the CPU-GPU heterogeneous parallel IPO algorithm, enabling the resolution of scattering problems for electrically large targets that previously could only be tackled on high-performance computers or computer clusters.

articleTitle: Application research of Webshell detection system based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Aiming at the limitations of traditional Webshell detection methods, such as relying on static rule matching, easy to be affected by confusing technologies, and difficult to cope with constantly evolving attack means. A Webshell detection method based on deep learning is proposed. This method not only integrates convolutional neural network (CNN) algorithm and recurrent neural network (RNN) algorithm, but also introduces multi-dimensional strategies of opcode analysis, regular detection and entropy detection to enrich the detection means. It is proved that this algorithm greatly improves the accuracy and real-time of Webshell detection.

articleTitle: A suspended capacitively coupled feed broadband circularly polarized microstrip antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A capacitance-coupled circularly polarized microstrip antenna is designed to solve the problem of bandwidth widening and off-center pattern when the feed is off-center. The antenna radiation patch realizes circular polarization through a pair of slots and truncating patch corners. A metal post is introduced in the centre of the patch to connect with the floor to broaden the bandwidth of the antenna and correct the deviation of the direction pattern. The simulation results show that the antenna |S11| < -10dB bandwidth of 1.85-2.48 GHz (31%), 3dB Axial Ratio bandwidth of 2.25-2.45 GHz, gain up to 8.6 dBi. The antenna is made of aluminium, which is simple and low cost.

articleTitle: Parallel EM Optimization Method for Microwave Filter Design Using Neuro-TF Surrogate and Isomorphic Orthogonal DOE Sampling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: This paper introduces a parallel electromagnetic (EM) optimization method using neuro-transfer function (neuro-TF) surrogate and isomorphic orthogonal Design of Experiments (DOE) sampling for microwave filter design. A sampling strategy that combines isomorphic orthogonal DOE with parallel EM simulations is employed to generate training data for the neuro-TF surrogate. This sampling strategy ensures a scattered distribution, thereby enhancing the accuracy of the surrogate model and speeding up the optimization process. Using adaptive splitting, a poleresidue tracking technique adjusts based on neighboring sample data, improving the continuity and precision of the surrogate’s pole-residue representation. This approach results in faster and more efficient optimal solutions with fewer iterations, as demonstrated in an example of EM optimization for a microwave filter.

articleTitle: 1-bit Terahertz beam-scanning space-time-coding metasurfaces based on PB phase principle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: The beam scanning range and precision are limited by the low quantization accuracy of traditional space-coding metasurfaces. Aiming at this problem, we first propose a 1-bit reflective time-coding metasurface based on the Pancharatnam-Berry (PB) phase principle, with an accurate phase difference of 180° and a phase shift error of less than 0.5° in the operating band of 95GHz-115GHz. The insertion loss of the unit cell is less than 5.6 dB, with a bandwidth of 19.4%. In this paper, the equivalent 4-bit phase distribution is optimized by fractional time-coding to compensate for quantization errors. Finally, quasi-continuous beam scanning with a large field of view greater than ±70° is achieved with a minimum step size of 0.5°. The proposed terahertz space-time-coding metasurface offers a low-cost, low-profile, and reconfigurable approach for potential applications in future 6G communication and radar imaging.

articleTitle: A Fast Pattern Synthesis Method for Conformal Antenna Array Based on Conbined Convex Optimization and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Different to the beam scanning of planar phased antenna array, the beam shape and sidelobes of conformal antenna array will be distorted due to the nonuniform coupling and anisotropic radiation patterns of each antenna unit. The simple linear phase shifting strategy for the planar array is invalid. The amplitude and phase distribution of the conformal array need to be re-optimized at every scanning angle without analytical formula, greatly increasing the calculation complexity and time cost, and it is not suitable for the real-time beam controlling. In this paper, a fast pattern synthesis method for the conformal antenna array based on the combinated convex optimization and neural network is proposed. Firstly, the problem of maximizing the directivity coefficient with sidelobe level(SLL) constraint is expressed as a standard convex model. The amplitude and phase distribution of the array in a specified scanning angle can be obtained by convex optimization method, as the training dataset for the following neural network training. Secondly, using scanning angles as input and amplitude/phase distributions as output, the trained neural network can grasp the implicit scanning rules for the conformal array, and it can quickly export the amplitude/phase distribution at arbitrary scanning angle. The efficiency of the proposed pattern synthesis method is also verified by typical sample simulations and the comparison of other different methods.

articleTitle: Reconstructing Feed Pattern in a Composite Aperture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: A millimeter-wave antenna integrated in a composite system is proposed for high-performance radars. Since it shares the same aperture with the optical system, the millimeter-wave feed of the reflector antenna is partially blocked. Due to this blockage, the power and phase patterns of the millimeter-wave feed are distorted. To solve this problem, the radiation pattern of the feed is reconstructed.

articleTitle: Fast Pattern Synthesis of Time-Modulated Arrays for Radar Beamforming Using Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In this paper, a pattern synthesis method of the time-modulated array (TMA) for radar beamforming is established. The proposed method uses artificial neural networks to accelerate the optimization process. A numerical example for a 100×100-element TMA demonstrates that the method effectively suppresses sidelobe levels and reduces the sideband levels within the mainlobe. The synthesis process is completed within one minute.

articleTitle: A Novel Range Estimation Method based on MUSIC High-Resolution Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Radar technology is widely used for precise distance measurements for objects, yet facing challenges of range resolution limit in indoor environments. This work utilizes a novel approach employing the multiple signal classification (MUSIC) algorithm to obtain both range and angle information for multiple objects, particularly those in close proximity, where the traditional fast Fourier transform (FFT) method falls short. A series of experiments were conducted with angular reflectors to validate the enhanced range resolution of the purposed method, using a 60GHz frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar. The results demonstrate that the MUSIC-based range estimation method can effectively distinguish multiple objects, surpassing the theoretical range resolution of FFT method.

articleTitle: Analysis of Conformal Quasi-Periodic Array Based on Sub-entire Domain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: In recent years, conformal array has been studied comprehensively owing to a few distinct advantages. However, the Floquet’s theorem and periodic Green’s Function method cannot be used for spherical arrays because the array is not periodic in an absolute sense. To develop a quasi-periodic analysis method with improved efficiency for conformal arrays on spherical surface, a sub-entire domain (SED) method is developed to calculate the far-field characteristics. A conformal bowtie array is analyzed by the proposed method as an example, and the obtained results are compared with those by full-wave method of moments (MoM). The proposed SED method has improved the efficiency greatly while keeps a reasonable accuracy.

articleTitle: A Beamforming Method to Enhance the Main Lobe Direction of NSB Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 International Applied Computational Electromagnetics Society Symposium (ACES-China)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the main flap directivity of the array antenna is shifted greatly outside the effective scanning range. In this paper, a beamforming method to enhance the main lobe directivity of the Null Steering Beamformer (NSB) algorithm is proposed without changing the array antenna structure.
